actionability_rule.text: A Fix is actionable when it names a concrete source edit, a runnable command, or a repository/system path. Concrete edits use an imperative operation with a named code fragment, declaration, value, or other object; structured source_edit, suggested_source_edit, replace, remove, and generated markers count as executable edits. A command must name a recognized executable and subcommand (or a REPL command). A path must name a literal path or filename. Placeholders, generic advice, inspection-only advice, and prose such as `follow the guidance`, `check the definition`, or `nothing to fix` are not actionable.
actionability_rule.tier_command_text: A tier/toolchain diagnostic is actionable only when its What or Why also names the command the user ran; a command that appears only in Fix is a remedy, not the invoking command.

rows.meaning: A non-finite collecting loop uses a collection arrow (D-LOOPEVAL1)
rows.what: This collecting loop cannot return a List because it has no finite exhaustion edge.
rows.why: A collecting loop must finish after a statically finite source or C-style condition. Bare infinite and condition-only loops do not provide that boundary.
rows.fix: Remove `->`, or iterate a finite source. Return one final value from an ordinary loop with `break value`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Remove `->`, or iterate a finite source. Return one final value from an ordinary loop with `break value`.

rows.meaning: A collecting loop path produces no item or `()` (D-LOOPEVAL1)
rows.what: This collecting loop path produces no item.
rows.why: Every accepted iteration must contribute one non-unit value unless `next` explicitly omits it.
rows.fix: Return a value on this path, or use `next` to omit the item. Remove `->` if the loop only performs effects.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Return a value on this path, or use `next` to omit the item. Remove `->` if the loop only performs effects.

rows.meaning: Collecting loop item types do not agree (D-LOOPEVAL1, D-COMPREHENSION1)
rows.what: This collecting loop produces incompatible item types.
rows.why: One collecting loop builds one `[T]`, so every contributed item must have the same type.
rows.fix: Convert the items to one type, or split the operations into separate loops.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Convert the items to one type, or split the operations into separate loops.

rows.meaning: A collecting loop uses a break payload instead of its List result (D-LOOPSTATE1)
rows.what: This collecting loop cannot use a break payload.
rows.why: Its result is already the accumulated `[T]`. A second payload would give the same exit two result channels.
rows.fix: Write `break` to return the accumulated list, or return one final value from an ordinary loop.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `break` to return the accumulated list, or return one final value from an ordinary loop.

rows.meaning: Ordinary-loop exits omit a result or use incompatible payload types (D-LOOPSTATE1)
rows.what: This result loop has a missing or incompatible break payload.
rows.why: An ordinary loop used as a value has one final result type. Every exit that targets it must provide that type.
rows.fix: Add the missing payload and make every payload the same type, or target an inner effect-only loop.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Add the missing payload and make every payload the same type, or target an inner effect-only loop.

rows.meaning: The retired Grant scope marker was used (D-AUTHORITY-SCOPE1, D-ONCE-RETIRE1)
rows.what: The `#Grant` scope marker is retired.
rows.why: `#FX` now narrows a block and binds an `Authority` handle when its head has a name.
rows.fix: Write `#FX(grant: FS, Net) { ... }`.

rows.meaning: A finite value loop is missing its exhaustion route, or uses bare immediate `?? next`/`?? break` (D-CHOOSE-FIND1)
rows.what: This finite value loop needs a written exhaustion route, or cannot use an immediate `?? next`/`?? break` route.
rows.why: A finite source can end without a matching `break`; `next` and `break` after the closing brace would control the loop that just closed instead of naming a target.
rows.fix: Add `?? fallback` after the closing `}`, or write a labeled search such as `found :: loop { ... break(found, value) }`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Add `?? fallback` after the closing `}`, or write a labeled search such as `found :: loop { ... break(found, value) }`.

rows.meaning: Effect-only loop uses a result exit (D-LOOPSTATE1)
rows.what: This effect-only loop uses a result exit.
rows.why: A break payload makes an effect-only loop a value expression.
rows.fix: Bind the loop with `::`, or remove the payload.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Bind the loop with `::`, or remove the payload.

rows.what: A read or write window starts from something that is not a place.
rows.why: Only a name followed by fields, indexes, or one range has stable storage that can be accessed without copying.
rows.fix: Bind the call or temporary to a name first, then take the window from that name.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Bind the call or temporary to a name first, then take the window from that name.

rows.meaning: `SharedGuard.map` projection is not a stable stored field place (D-SHAREDGUARD1)
rows.what: `` `SharedGuard.map` needs a stored field projection ``.
rows.why: A mapped guard must keep a stable stored place inside the value protected by the original lock. A computed field is a value, not a place.
rows.fix: Use a direct stored-field projection such as `guard.map(value -> value.field)`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use a direct stored-field projection such as `guard.map(value -> value.field)`.

rows.meaning: `SharedGuard.split` projections overlap or are not stable stored field places (D-SHAREDGUARD1)
rows.what: `` `SharedGuard.split` needs two disjoint field projections ``.
rows.why: Two child guards must preserve non-overlapping provenance under one original lock. Equal, enclosing, nested, or computed projections cannot prove that law.
rows.fix: Project two stored sibling fields, such as `value.left` and `value.right`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Project two stored sibling fields, such as `value.left` and `value.right`.

rows.meaning: A Cell guard is stored in an unsupported aggregate or captured by a lambda (D-LOCALCELL1=A)
rows.what: A Cell guard is stored inside an unsupported value or captured by a lambda.
rows.why: A Cell guard is a temporary loan handle. Storing it inside another value could keep the loan after its local scope ends.
rows.fix: Keep the guard in a local name or a tuple, and use `.map(...)` or `.split(...)` for projections.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Keep the guard in a local name or a tuple, and use `.map(...)` or `.split(...)` for projections.

rows.why: A pin promises one storage location will not move, so it has to name that location with the write-access marker; see the sigil reading rule above.
rows.fix: Write `mem.pin(&place)` with the write-access marker `&`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `mem.pin(&place)` with the write-access marker `&`.

rows.meaning: A pinned place is moved, replaced, or resized while a pin is still live (D-PIN1=A)
rows.what: A pinned place is moved, replaced, or resized while a pin is still live.
rows.why: The pin promises that storage keeps its address; moving or replacing it would leave every stored address pointing at the old place.
rows.fix: Finish using the pin before changing the place, or narrow the pin's scope.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Finish using the pin before changing the place, or narrow the pin's scope.

rows.meaning: A place is read through its owner while an exclusive write window / pin into it is still live (card #1361, I2)
rows.what: A place is read through its owner while an exclusive write window into it is still live.
rows.why: An exclusive window (a pin or a mutable view) already gives write access to that storage; reading the owner beside it would be rejected after lowering.
rows.fix: Read or edit through the live window name instead of the owner.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Read or edit through the live window name instead of the owner.

rows.meaning: A part of persistent or static state cannot be moved independently

rows.why: Persistent and static storage is shared state; safe lowering can only take or replace the complete root.
rows.fix: Move or take `{name}` as a whole, or update it atomically.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move or take the persistent value as a whole, or update it atomically.

rows.meaning: Persistent or static state cannot be mutably borrowed
rows.what: A mutable borrow of `{name}` cannot escape its persistent or static storage cell
rows.why: Persistent and static state must be changed by computing a replacement and assigning the whole binding. A mutable borrow or mutating receiver would let access escape the cell.
rows.fix: Compute an owned replacement, then assign the persistent or static binding as a whole instead of passing `{name}` with `&` or using a mutating receiver.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Compute an owned replacement and assign the persistent or static binding as a whole.

rows.meaning: C25/D-RANGE2: `step` in an arm head — `step` is a loop modifier, not an arm construct
rows.what: `` `step` `` is not allowed in a range arm — range arms test a band, not a sequence.
rows.why: A stride modifies a loop range to skip values (`loop i in 0..10, 2`); an arm head like `1..10` just checks whether the subject is between 1 and 10. A stepped range is not a contiguous band and can't be used for membership testing.
rows.fix: Remove the stride; to match only multiples of N, use a full condition: `subject >= lo && subject <= hi && subject % n == 0 ->`.

rows.meaning: Invalid scoped policy: unknown key, prohibited scope, conflict, or widening (D-MARK-SCOPE1)
rows.what: A scoped policy is unknown, conflicts, widens an inherited constraint, or is attached at a prohibited scope.

rows.meaning: Inferred `.new(...)` has no expected receiver type (D-SHAPE3a)

rows.meaning: An identifier violates Jet's machine-enforced casing category (D-SHAPE-CASE1)
rows.what: An identifier is not written in the casing required for its grammatical category.
rows.why: Jet enforces one two-tier law: type-like names use PascalCase; value-like names use snake_case. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: Rename the identifier to the exact spelling shown by the diagnostic. Foreign names inside FFI binding modules are exempt.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Rename the identifier to the exact spelling shown by the diagnostic. Foreign names inside FFI binding modules are exempt.

rows.meaning: Retired word-cased acronym spelling; use the caps form (D-ACRO-CASE1, D-ACRO-LEX1)
rows.what: `{old}` is spelled `{canonical}`.
rows.why: Jet keeps acronyms fully capitalized inside PascalCase names (D-ACRO-CASE1=A, D-ACRO-LEX1=A).
rows.fix: Write the capitalized spelling shown by the diagnostic.

rows.meaning: Physical quantity dimensions are incompatible for the requested operator (D-SHAPE-QUANTITY1)
rows.what: `+` can't combine Length with Time
rows.why: Physical quantities must have compatible dimensions before they can be added, subtracted, or compared
rows.fix: Use matching dimensions, or use `*` or `/` to derive a new dimension
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use matching dimensions, or use `*` or `/` to derive a new dimension

rows.meaning: A nominal type uses arithmetic without the required operator hook (D-OPDEF1)
rows.what: No `{symbol}` operator is defined for `{type}`.
rows.why: User arithmetic dispatches only through the matching fixed operator trait hook; the compiler does not guess a method or fall through to rustc. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: Implement the named `Type.Trait` hook, or call a named method instead.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Implement the named `Type.Trait` hook, or call a named method instead.

rows.meaning: An operator hook directly dispatches back to itself through its symbol (D-OPDEF1)
rows.what: `{hook}` calls itself through `{symbol}`.
rows.why: The symbol inside its own hook dispatches directly back to that hook, so evaluation would recurse forever.
rows.fix: Combine the value's fields directly, or call a different named helper inside the hook.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Combine the value's fields directly, or call a different named helper inside the hook.

rows.meaning: A hooked compound assignment targets a nested field place not yet lowerable as one write (D-OPDEF1)
rows.what: Compound assignment can't target a nested operator field.
rows.why: Hooked compound assignment must read and write one stable place exactly once; nested field places are not yet represented by the operator assignment spine.
rows.fix: Bind the inner value, update it, then assign the whole inner value back.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Bind the inner value, update it, then assign the whole inner value back.

rows.meaning: Anonymous-union member is not a concrete closed type (D-UNIONTYPE1)
rows.what: `{Type}` can't be a union member.
rows.why: Anonymous unions (D-UNIONTYPE1=A) hold concrete closed member types only — not type parameters, trait objects, or function types.
rows.fix: Use a named enum when a member needs an open shape.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use a named enum when a member needs an open shape.

rows.meaning: Inclusive `0..xs.len()` indexes that same `xs` (D-RANGE-EXCL1=C)
rows.what: This range includes `{xs}.len()`, one past the last index.
rows.why: An inclusive range that ends at a list's length runs one step too far when the body indexes that list.
rows.fix: Write `loop (i, item) in xs` — or `loop i in xs.indexes()` — or `0..<xs.len()`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `loop (i, item) in xs` — or `loop i in xs.indexes()` — or `0..<xs.len()`.

rows.meaning: Repeated anonymous-union match member (D-UNIONTYPE1)
rows.what: Arm `{Type}` is unreachable — that case is already handled.
rows.why: Every earlier arm already covers this pattern.
rows.fix: Remove this arm or merge it with the one above.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Remove this arm or merge it with the one above.

rows.meaning: Teaching: pattern arms need `==` — other distributed markers do not bind structural patterns (D-IFDIST1)
rows.what: A pattern arm sits under a non-`==` distributed `if` table.
rows.why: Structural patterns bind under `if subject == { … }` only. Other markers (`<`, `!=`, …) distribute bare values, not shapes.
rows.fix: Write `if subject == { … }` for pattern arms, or use a Bool head.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `if subject == { … }` for pattern arms, or use a Bool head.

rows.meaning: Bare variant pattern needs a leading `.` (D-ENUMDOT1)
rows.what: Pattern `{name}` needs a leading `.`.
rows.why: Match patterns take a leading dot so the name isn't read as a variable or call (D-ENUMDOT1).
rows.fix: Write `.{name}` or `.{name}(…)`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write the member access as `.<name>` or `.<name>(...)`.

rows.meaning: Fence expansion has no entries (D-EACH1=C, D-VERDICT-1320-1)
rows.what: This fence is empty.
rows.why: A fenced statement needs at least one entry to expand.
rows.fix: Write one or more entries between `@[` and `]@`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write one or more entries between `@[` and `]@`.

rows.meaning: One binding fence repeats a name (D-EACH1=C, D-VERDICT-1320-1)
rows.what: `{name}` appears twice in this fence.
rows.why: One binding fence must name each generated copy once.
rows.fix: Remove the second name or give it a different name.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Remove the second name or give it a different name.

rows.meaning: Lock-step fences have different entry counts (D-EACH1=C, D-VERDICT-1320-1)
rows.what: Fences on one statement have different entry counts.
rows.why: Multiple fences expand in lock-step, so every fence needs one entry for each copy.
rows.fix: Give every fence the same number of entries.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Give every fence the same number of entries.

rows.meaning: Fence appears outside a binding target or expression statement, or a binding fence carries a non-name entry (D-EACH1=C, D-VERDICT-1320-1)
rows.what: This fence is not in an allowed statement position, or one of its entries has the wrong shape (empty entry, trailing comma, non-name in a binding fence, malformed numbered range).
rows.why: D-EACH1 expands complete binding or expression statements; a binding fence takes plain names or one ascending numbered-name range, an expression fence takes comma-separated expressions.
rows.fix: Move the fence to a binding target or a complete expression statement, or fix the entry.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move the fence to a binding target or a complete expression statement, or fix the entry.

rows.meaning: Teaching: an adjacent effect `if`, `else`, or `loop` body needs braces (D-ONELINE-BODY1=B)
rows.what: This `{body}` body needs braces.
rows.why: Use `->` for one effect statement; braces make a multi-statement or scoped body's boundary visible to readers, editors, and the compiler.
rows.fix: Write `-> statement` for one statement, or wrap the body in `{ ... }`; `jet fmt` applies this fix.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `-> statement` for one statement, or wrap the body in `{ ... }`; `jet fmt` applies this fix.

rows.meaning: Teaching: explicit semicolons are statement boundaries, not canonical Jet syntax (D-SEMI1=A)
rows.what: This explicit semicolon is not part of canonical Jet syntax.
rows.why: Jet uses line boundaries for statements; the parser preserves this boundary so the same program can be repaired without changing behavior.
rows.fix: Replace the semicolon with a line break when code follows it, or remove it at the end of a line; `jet fmt` applies this fix.
rows.structured_fix: source_edit|behavior-preserving

rows.meaning: Teaching: retired `comptime`; use implicit folding or `@` (D-VERDICT-1308-1)
rows.what: `comptime` is retired.
rows.why: Jet folds ordinary foldable expressions automatically; explicit compile-time demand lives on the marker plane.
rows.fix: Remove the keyword for ordinary code, or replace it with `@` when failure to compute now must stop the build.

rows.meaning: Retired `#Default` on a field; write `field: T{{expr}}` (D-DEFAULT-SHAPE1=B)
rows.what: `#Default` on a field is retired.
rows.why: Field absence and construction defaults ride the field's type as `field: T{{expr}}` (D-DEFAULT-SHAPE1=B).
rows.fix: Write `field: T{{expr}}` instead of `#Default(expr)`.

rows.meaning: Teaching: C-style counter loop `init, cond, step` retired (D-LOOP-HEADER3=D)
rows.what: C-style counter loop headers are retired.
rows.why: A three-slot loop header is binding, source, and step rule — not init, condition, and assignment (D-LOOP-HEADER3=D).
rows.fix: Write `loop i in 0..<n { … }` or `loop i in 0..n, 2 { … }`; keep `loop name := value, condition { … }` for mutable state.

rows.meaning: Teaching: retired `#Known`, `#Known if` and the `#Known` block; write the mark on the name (D-META-STAGE1=B)
rows.what: `#Known` is retired.
rows.why: Compile time has one mark, `@`, and the mark belongs to the name, so it is written at every mention.
rows.fix: Write `@name :: …` for a binding, `@if <condition> { … }` for a compile-time branch, and `@ { … }` for a compile-time block.

rows.meaning: Teaching: retired alias binding `=`; write `::` (D-ALIAS-OP1=B)

rows.why: `::` defines a name; `=` fills a slot inside an existing declaration (D-ALIAS-OP1=B).

rows.meaning: Teaching: a guard follows its source with no comma (D-LOOP-GUARD1=A)

rows.meaning: Retired marker declaration shape; use one named parameter list (D-MARKER-SITES1=B)

rows.why: D-MARKER-SITES1=B gives every marker one named parameter list: ordinary names have types, and `@` names have fixed metadata values.

rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `marker Name(args..., @sites: [...], @repeatable: true, ...)`.

rows.meaning: `#Memo` requires a bare computed field (D-FIELDMEMO1=A)

rows.meaning: Teaching: source loops join a binding and source with `in`, not a comma (D-LOOP-IN1=A)

rows.meaning: Teaching: expression-position membership uses `.contains(x)`, not `in` (D-LOOP-IN1=A)

rows.why: Expression `x in xs` has no operator meaning in Jet. Collection membership is a method call.
rows.fix: Write `xs.contains(x)` (the `.contains(x)` method) instead of `x in xs`.

rows.meaning: Teaching: retired declaration default `name: Type = value`; write `name: Type{{value}}` (D-DEFAULT-SHAPE1=B)
rows.what: This declaration uses the retired `name: Type = value` default spelling.
rows.why: Declaration defaults ride the type as `name: Type{{value}}`; `=` remains for reassignment and extern slot fill.
rows.fix: Write `name: Type{{value}}` for a declaration default, or keep `=` for reassignment and extern slot fill.

rows.meaning: A bare distributed atom group is a direct operand of `&&` or `||` (D-ARMHEAD-PAREN1=A)

rows.why: A `|` arm head is one distributed group, so its boundary must stay visible before a Boolean operator applies.

rows.meaning: Unknown scope member, or a member used in a marker that declares none (D-DOTSCOPE1)
rows.what: `.{name}` isn't a member of `#{marker}`.
rows.why: Inside a marker block a `.name { … }` statement must name one of that marker's declared members. `#{marker}` understands: {list}.
rows.fix: Use one of the listed members, or remove the block.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use one of the listed members, or remove the block.

rows.meaning: A `.name { … }` scope-member statement outside a member-declaring marker block (D-DOTSCOPE1)
rows.what: `.{name}` only works inside a marker block that declares it.
rows.why: A leading-dot member statement resolves against the enclosing applied rule's vocabulary; out here there is no such block.
rows.fix: Move it inside a `#Test("…") { … }` block, or write an ordinary statement.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move it inside a `#Test("…") { … }` block, or write an ordinary statement.

rows.meaning: `.setup` is not the first statement in the test (D-DOTSCOPE1)
rows.what: `.setup` must be the first statement in the test.
rows.why: `.setup` marks the test's initialization; anything before it would run first.
rows.fix: Move `.setup { … }` to the top of the block.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move `.setup { … }` to the top of the block.

rows.meaning: A scope member has the wrong argument shape (D-DOTSCOPE1)
rows.what: This scope member has the wrong arguments.
rows.why: Each member has a fixed shape: `.timeout(500ms)` takes one duration value, `.setup`/`.expect_fail` take none, `.skip` takes an optional reason string.
rows.fix: Match the member's shape, e.g. `.timeout(500ms) { … }`, `.timeout(wait) { … }`, or `.skip("reason") { … }`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Match the member's shape, e.g. `.timeout(500ms) { … }`, `.timeout(wait) { … }`, or `.skip("reason") { … }`.

rows.meaning: A scope member is nested instead of a top-level statement of the marker block (D-DOTSCOPE1)
rows.what: Scope members can't be nested.
rows.why: Each member is a top-level region of the marker block; nesting one inside another member or a control block has no meaning.
rows.fix: Move the member out to the top level of the block.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move the member out to the top level of the block.

rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Remove the import, or remove or update the boundary rule in `package.jet`.

rows.fix: Move the statements into the entry file's `fn run`, or import a declaration-only file.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move the statements into the entry file's `fn run`, or import a declaration-only file.

rows.fix: Run `jet fix` to move the loose statements into `fn run`, or remove the explicit function.

rows.meaning: An arena `view` escapes its region — returned, stored, given away, or captured (D-ALLOC2/D-REGION1)
rows.what: `{view}` cannot be shared — it does not live long enough to {escape}.
rows.why: `{view}` is a view into `{arena}`; sharing it outside the region would let it outlive `{arena}` and point into freed memory.
rows.fix: Keep the view inside the arena's region, or copy what you need out with `~` before it leaves.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Keep the view inside the arena's region, or copy what you need out with `~` before it leaves.

rows.meaning: An arena `view` is read after its arena was reset (D-ALLOC2)
rows.what: `{arena}` was reset here, so the value `{view}` points into is gone.
rows.why: `reset` invalidates every value allocated in the arena; reading the view afterward would read reused memory.
rows.fix: Use the view before `reset`, or re-`alloc` after to get a fresh value.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use the view before `reset`, or re-`alloc` after to get a fresh value.

rows.meaning: The `Authority` handle bound by a named `#FX(…)` region escapes its scope — returned, stored, or captured (D-AUTHORITY-SCOPE1)
rows.what: The `Authority` handle `{handle}` can't escape its `#FX` block.
rows.why: `#FX(…)` revokes the `Authority` at scope end (RAII); returning, storing, or capturing the handle would let revoked rights outlive the scope.
rows.fix: Use the handle only inside the `#FX` block, or perform the work that needs it there.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use the handle only inside the `#FX` block, or perform the work that needs it there.

rows.meaning: An effect used inside a `#FX(…)` region has no authority — it isn't in the authority list (D-AUTHORITY-SCOPE1)
rows.what: This `#FX` region uses the effect `{effect}`, which has no authority backing.
rows.why: `#FX(…)` allows exactly the listed effects; an effect reached inside — even transitively through a call — that the list omits has no authority backing it.
rows.fix: Add the named effect to the `#FX(…)` list, or move that work outside the region.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Add the named effect to the `#FX(…)` list, or move that work outside the region.

rows.meaning: A tagged value reaches a destination denied by that tag declaration (D-TAG-SURFACE1)
rows.what: A `{tag}` value is denied at `{api}`.
rows.why: The declaration for `{tag}` lists a destination that covers `{api}`. The tag spreads with derived data until an exact-tag scrubber removes it.
rows.fix: Remove the destination use, change the declaration if its policy is wrong, or pass the value through `#Scrub({tag})`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Remove the destination use, correct its policy, or pass the value through an appropriate `#Scrub(Tag)`.

rows.meaning: A `#Credential` value reaches a log, display, or serialization destination (D-TAG-SURFACE1)
rows.what: A `Credential` value is denied at `{sink}`.
rows.why: The Prelude `Credential` tag denies logging, display, and serialization destinations because they would leak a secret.
rows.fix: Log a non-secret field, or pass the value through a matching `#Scrub(Credential)` function.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Log a non-secret field, or pass the value through a matching `#Scrub(Credential)` function.

rows.meaning: A `#Replayable` function reaches ambient `Time`/`Rand`/`Net`/`IO` (D-REPLAY1)
rows.what: `{fn}` is `#Replayable` but reaches `{effect}`.
rows.why: `#Replayable` code must replay from explicit inputs; ambient time, randomness, network, or console IO would make the same replay diverge.
rows.fix: Inject a deterministic clock/RNG or mockable input, pass recorded data in, or move the ambient effect outside the replayable function.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Inject a deterministic clock/RNG or mockable input, pass recorded data in, or move the ambient effect outside the replayable function.

rows.meaning: A `tag` is used where dispatch/methods are expected — `derive`d, or implemented/used as a trait (D-QUAL2)
rows.what: `{tag}` is a tag, but {context} needs a trait.
rows.why: A `tag` is a marker that erases at runtime and carries no methods; dispatch and method attachment need a `trait`.
rows.fix: Declare `{tag}` as a `trait` with the method(s) it should provide.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Declare the tag as a trait with the methods it should provide.

rows.meaning: A method is declared in a `tag` body, but tags have no methods (D-QUAL2)
rows.what: The tag `{tag}` declares a method `{method}`, but tags have no methods.
rows.why: A `tag` is a marker that erases at runtime; only a `trait` carries methods and dispatches.
rows.fix: Make `{tag}` a `trait` if `{method}` should dispatch, or remove the method to keep `{tag}` a marker tag.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Make the tag a trait for method dispatch, or remove the method and keep it as a marker tag.

rows.meaning: A value tag does not name a declared `tag`, with a suggestion from declared tags (D-TAG-SURFACE1)
rows.what: There's no tag called `{tag}`.
rows.why: A value tag must name a declared `tag`; Prelude declares `Input`, `PII`, `Secret`, and `Credential`.
rows.fix: Declare it with `tag {tag} { deny: [Effect] }`, check the spelling, or use the suggested tag.
rows.structured_fix: suggested_source_edit|needs-review

rows.meaning: A tag declaration has no policy body, lacks non-empty `deny`, repeats a field, or names an unknown body field (D-TAG-SURFACE1)
rows.what: tag `{tag}` has an incomplete policy body.
rows.why: Every tag declares an enforceable policy with a required non-empty `deny` list and optional `from` list.
rows.fix: Write `tag {tag} { deny: [Effect], from: [source.path] }`; omit `from` when it is not needed.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Declare the tag with its deny list and optional source path.

rows.meaning: A tag `deny` or `from` entry does not name a known effect, sink, or source path (D-TAG-SURFACE1)
rows.what: `{path}` is not a known tag source or destination.
rows.why: `deny` entries name effects or registered sinks; `from` entries name effects or function paths.
rows.fix: Correct the path using the suggested effect, sink, or declared function.
rows.structured_fix: suggested_source_edit|needs-review

rows.meaning: `#Scrub(Tag)` does not consume that tagged type and return an untagged result (D-TAG-SURFACE1)
rows.what: `#Scrub({tag})` does not match this function signature.
rows.why: A scrubber removes exactly one tag, so it must consume a value carrying that tag and return a value without it.
rows.fix: Accept a `#{tag} T` parameter and return the untagged result.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Accept a tagged parameter and return the untagged result.

rows.meaning: A function's inferred effects exceed its declared `-[…]>` bound (D-EFF1)
rows.what: `{fn}` uses the effect `{effect}`, which its signature doesn't allow.
rows.why: A `-[…]>` list is an upper bound on what the body may do; the inferred effects must be a subset. An effect the body reaches that the bound omits breaks that contract.
rows.fix: Add the named effect to the `-[…]>` list, or stop using it (drop the Core call that introduces it, or move it out of this function).
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Add the named effect to the `-[…]>` list, or stop using it (drop the Core call that introduces it, or move it out of this function).

rows.meaning: Retired duplicate of the unified `#FX` check (D-AUTHORITY-SCOPE1)
rows.what: *Retired by D-AUTHORITY-SCOPE1* — the `#FX` subset check now reports E0712 for bare and named regions.
rows.why: Bare and named `#FX` regions use one authority check; E0741 is retained only as tombstone history.
rows.fix: Fix the E0712 diagnostic, then add the effect to the `#FX(…)` list or move the work outside the region.

rows.meaning: A trait-method impl uses effects beyond the trait method's declared bound (D-EFF3)
rows.what: This `{method}` impl uses the effect `{effect}`, which the trait doesn't allow.
rows.why: A trait method may declare an effect upper bound (`fn hash(self) -[]>`, `fn render(self) -[GPU]>`); every implementation's inferred effects must fit inside it, so the bound holds for all impls (D-EFF3).
rows.fix: Remove the offending work from the impl, or widen the bound on the trait method.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Remove the offending work from the impl, or widen the bound on the trait method.

rows.meaning: Dynamic trait dispatch has no declared effect bound under an enclosing effect ceiling (D-EFF3)
rows.what: Dynamic call `{trait}::{method}` has no effect bound.
rows.why: A trait value can select any implementation at runtime, so an enclosing effect ceiling needs the trait method's declared upper bound (D-EFF3).
rows.fix: Declare an effect row on the trait method, such as `-[]>` for pure dispatch, or move the dynamic call outside the bounded function.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Declare an effect row on the trait method, such as `-[]>` for pure dispatch, or move the dynamic call outside the bounded function.

rows.meaning: *Retired by D-SHAPE8=A* (was: `#Pure fn` combined with a non-empty `#(…)` effect list)
rows.what: *Retired by D-SHAPE8=A.*
rows.why: This code diagnosed the former contradiction between `#Pure fn` and a non-empty `#(…)` effect list. Both spellings are now rejected earlier by E0066.
rows.fix: Use one canonical effect arrow: `-[]>` for an empty row or `-[Effects]>` for a bounded row.

rows.meaning: An irreversible effect (Net/FS/Exec/FFI) used directly inside a `#Transact { … }` block — can't be rolled back (D-TXN2, D-BOUND-UNDO1)
rows.what: `{api}` has the `{effect}` effect, which can't be rolled back inside a `#Transact` block.
rows.why: A `#Transact` block undoes its work on a `?`-failure; network, file, subprocess, and foreign effects leave external state a rollback can't take back unless the foreign binding declares a compensating undo.
rows.fix: Move the call after the block, register it with `<handle>.on_commit(() -> { … })`, or declare `#Undo(inverse)` on the foreign binding.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move the call after the block, register it with `<handle>.on_commit(() -> { … })`, or declare `#Undo(inverse)` on the foreign binding.

rows.meaning: A callback argument exceeds its parameter's effect bound (`fn(…) -[]>` / `fn(…) -[E]>`) (D-EFF2)
rows.what: This callback uses the effect `{effect}`, which the parameter doesn't allow.
rows.why: A `fn(…) -[]>` parameter demands a pure callback, and a `fn(…) -[E]>` parameter bounds the callback to the listed effects; the actual callback's inferred effects must be a subset (D-EFF2). The bound is checked at the call site, so an impure callback is rejected before it runs.
rows.fix: Pass a callback within the bound (a `fn … -[]>` for a pure parameter), or widen the parameter's effect bound.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass a callback within the bound (a `fn … -[]>` for a pure parameter), or widen the parameter's effect bound.

rows.meaning: `-[via f]>` names a non-existent parameter, or one that isn't a function type (D-EFF2)
rows.what: `-[via {param}]>` on `{fn}` names no such parameter or a parameter that isn't a callback.
rows.why: `-[via f]>` publishes a function's effects as a tight pass-through of its callback parameter `f` (D-EFF2); `f` must be a parameter of the function whose type is a `fn(…)`.
rows.fix: Point `via` at a function-typed parameter, or drop the `-[via …]>` annotation.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Point `via` at a function-typed parameter, or drop the `-[via …]>` annotation.

rows.meaning: A function reaches an effect it prohibits with `-[!E]>` in its own call graph, including a denied `Panic` stop (D-PROP1=A, D-NOPANIC1=D)
rows.what: A function reaches an effect it prohibits with `-[!E]>` in its own call graph, including a denied `Panic` stop (D-PROP1=A, D-NOPANIC1=D)
rows.why: The registered sema rule names the effect or panic site and keeps the three legal exits
rows.fix: Remove the offending effect, return a fallible result, add facts or a `#Pre`/refinement proof, or drop the prohibition
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Remove the offending effect, return a fallible result, add facts or a `#Pre`/refinement proof, or drop the prohibition

rows.meaning: An effect declaration lacks a leaf, or a dotted effect under a checked root is not a declared package-view leaf (D-EFFECT-DECL1=A)
rows.what: `{effect}` is not a declared effect leaf.
rows.why: This package view has declared leaves under the same root, so dotted effect names must match one of those declarations exactly.
rows.fix: Use the suggested declared leaf, add an `effect {effect}` declaration, or use the bare root.
rows.structured_fix: suggested_source_edit|needs-review

rows.meaning: Panic is a deny-only effect row (D-PANICROOT1=A)
rows.what: `Panic` can't be granted, only denied
rows.why: `Panic` is a deny-only effect row; no positive effect bound or authority can grant it
rows.fix: Drop `Panic` from the list, or write `-[!Panic]>`
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Drop `Panic` from the list, or write `-[!Panic]>`

rows.meaning: `#Context` field uses `=` instead of `:` (D-CTX1, S17)
rows.what: `#Context` field uses `=` instead of `:` (D-CTX1, S17)
rows.why: The registered parser rule applies here
rows.fix: Use `:` rather than `=` for a `#Context` field.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use `:` rather than `=` for a `#Context` field.

rows.meaning: Unknown `#Context` field name (v1 allows only `allocator`, `logger`, `deadline`)
rows.what: Unknown `#Context` field name (v1 allows only `allocator`, `logger`, `deadline`)

rows.fix: Write bare names like `default.[cargo, ripgrep]`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write bare names like `default.[cargo, ripgrep]`.

rows.meaning: Fixed-size list length is not a computable integer (D-META-CONST1/S76)
rows.what: A fixed-size list length must be known at compile time, must be an integer, and must fit the target's array-size representation.
rows.why: Use a literal, a same-file `@` binding, or another comptime expression that produces an in-range integer; a destructuring pattern must then name exactly that many elements.
rows.fix: Use a literal, a same-file `@` binding, or another comptime expression that produces an in-range integer; a destructuring pattern must then name exactly that many elements.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use a literal, a same-file `@` binding, or another comptime expression that produces an in-range integer; a destructuring pattern must then name exactly that many elements.

rows.meaning: Length-changing op (`push`/`pop`/`insert`) on a fixed-size `[T#N]` (S76)
rows.what: A length-changing method (`push`, `pop`, `insert`, `remove`, `clear`) was called on a fixed-size `[T#N]`.
rows.why: The length of `[T#N]` is fixed at compile time and cannot change at runtime.
rows.fix: If you need a growable list, bind it with `:=` (e.g. `r := [...]`) so its length can change.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|If you need a growable list, bind it with `:=` (e.g. `r := [...]`) so its length can change.

rows.meaning: Compile-time or interval-proven index out of range on `[T#N]` (S76, D-TYPE2-REFINE1)
rows.what: An index interval is out of range for a `[T#N]` at compile time.
rows.why: Literal indexes and interval facts must fit 0 through N−1; anything outside that range would panic at runtime.
rows.fix: Use an index in the valid range, widen to `[T]` for runtime checking, or tighten the range.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use an index in the valid range, widen to `[T]` for runtime checking, or tighten the range.

rows.meaning: module contribution value isn't a struct literal of its namespace's type (`Env`/`System`/`Image`)
rows.what: A module contribution's value isn't a struct literal of its namespace's type.
rows.why: `env.dev: Env { … }` ties a namespace to its matching type so the merge engine knows what it's combining.
rows.fix: Wrap the value in the matching type, e.g. `Env { … }`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Wrap the value in the matching type, e.g. `Env { … }`.

rows.meaning: §6 merge conflict: a named source got irreconcilable refs
rows.what: Two modules contributed different refs to the same source name.
rows.why: §6 merges sources by name, so one source name must resolve to one ref.
rows.fix: Make every declaration of the source agree, or rename one of them.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Make every declaration of the source agree, or rename one of them.

rows.meaning: A module `sources:` entry isn't a `target@provider` ref or bare path (D-JPK-REF1/U6/U8)
rows.what: A `sources:` entry's value isn't a `target@provider` ref or bare path.
rows.why: D-JPK-REF1 puts the upstream target before `@` and its provider after it; local `./`, `../`, and `/` paths stay bare. A `jet build` run reports this package-source error.
rows.fix: Write `default: owner/repo/rev@github`, `default: channel@nixpkgs`, or a bare local path.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Write `default: owner/repo/rev@github`, `default: channel@nixpkgs`, or a bare local path.

rows.meaning: An `imports:` discovery directive isn't `find("<dir>")` with a literal path (U4)
rows.what: An `imports:` discovery directive isn't `find("<dir>")` with a single literal path.
rows.why: Imports auto-discover a directory of modules (U4); discovery uses one literal `find` path, while recognized first-party integrations use their typed calls.
rows.fix: Write `imports: find("./modules")`, or use a recognized typed integration call.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Write `imports: find("./modules")`, or use a recognized typed integration call.

rows.meaning: `imports: find("<dir>")` points at a directory that doesn't exist (U4)
rows.what: `imports: find("<dir>")` points at a directory that doesn't exist.
rows.why: `find` walks that directory for `.jet` modules (U4); it must exist relative to the file that declares it, or there is nothing to discover.
rows.fix: Create the directory, or fix the path so it points at your modules folder.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Create the directory, or fix the path so it points at your modules folder.

rows.meaning: A discovered module has its own `imports:` (liftability law, U4)
rows.what: A module discovered by `find(…)` has its own `imports:`.
rows.why: The liftability law (U4): modules contribute to the merged whole, they never import each other — nesting `find` would make composition explode and break "drop a file in."
rows.fix: Remove the `imports:` from the discovered module; declare all `find(…)` directives in the top-level env.jet.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Remove the `imports:` from the discovered module; declare all `find(…)` directives in the top-level env.jet.

rows.meaning: Unknown field on a frozen `System`, active `Image`, or dev `Service` record (D-JETOS-FREEZE1, D-JPK-IMAGE1, D-JPK-SERVICE1)
rows.what: A `System` / `Image` / `Service` record has a field it doesn't define.
rows.why: These records have decision-owned field sets (D-JETOS-FREEZE1, D-JPK-IMAGE1, D-JPK-SERVICE1); an unknown field is usually a typo or a value that belongs elsewhere.
rows.fix: Remove the field, or use one of the known fields named in the error.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Remove the field, or use one of the known fields named in the error.

rows.meaning: `target` (or cross-compile platform) isn't a known platform value (D-JPK-PLATFORM1)
rows.what: A `target` (or cross-compile platform) names a platform Jet doesn't know.
rows.why: D-JPK-PLATFORM1 makes `target` a typed platform value, not quoted text — it must be `linux.x64` or `linux.arm64`, so it type-checks and LSP-completes.
rows.fix: Write `target: linux.x64` or `target: linux.arm64`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Write `target: linux.x64` or `target: linux.arm64`.

rows.meaning: A frozen `System` has no `target` (D-JETOS-FREEZE1)
rows.what: A `System` has no `target`.
rows.why: D-JETOS-FREEZE1's captured `System` schema requires every machine to name its typed `target`.
rows.fix: Add `target: linux.x64` (or `linux.arm64`).
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Add `target: linux.x64` (or `linux.arm64`).

rows.meaning: A `Service` has no `enable`, or `enable` isn't `true`/`false` (U12)
rows.what: A `Service` has no `enable`, or its `enable` isn't a yes/no value.
rows.why: U12: every `Service` is an open record whose required first field is `enable: Bool`.
rows.fix: Add `enable: true` (or `false`) to the service.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Add `enable: true` (or `false`) to the service.

rows.meaning: An `Image` uses a frozen disk-image format (D-JETOS-FREEZE1)
rows.what: An `Image` uses a frozen disk-image format.
rows.why: D-JETOS-FREEZE1: `iso`, `qcow`, and `raw` disk images are jetos research capture; Jetpack only builds `.Oci` images today. A `jet image` run reports this image declaration error.
rows.fix: Use `kind: .Oci` for an active image, or keep disk-image notes in the jetos research appendix.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use `kind: .Oci` for an active image, or keep disk-image notes in the jetos research appendix.

rows.meaning: An `Image` has no active `from`, or restates a frozen system field (D-JETOS-FREEZE1)
rows.what: An `Image` has no active `from`, or restates a frozen system-inherited field.
rows.why: Active Jetpack images are OCI containers built `from: packages.<name>`; `system.*` disk images are frozen jetos research. A `jet image` run reports this image declaration error.
rows.fix: Add `from: packages.<name>` for an `.Oci` image, or remove fields inherited from frozen `system.*` research.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Add `from: packages.<name>` for an `.Oci` image, or remove fields inherited from frozen `system.*` research.

rows.meaning: An `Image` `from:` references a frozen/unknown `System` (D-JETOS-FREEZE1)
rows.what: An `Image` `from:` references a frozen/unknown system.

rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use `from: packages.<name>` for an `.Oci` image, or keep the system image as research capture.

rows.what: A `jet os` target has no host, or its `host@root` selector has an empty half.
rows.why: D-JPK-REF1 amends D-JPK-OSHOST1: a bare host selects `system.<host>` in `./config.jet`; both halves of `host@root` are required for an external root.

rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Write `jet os switch laptop` or `jet os switch laptop@../machines`.

rows.meaning: A `jet os` host names a `System` the config doesn't define (D-JPK-OSHOST1)
rows.what: A `jet os` host names a system the config doesn't define.
rows.why: D-JPK-OSHOST1=C: the host selects one `system.<host>` contribution in `config.jet`.

rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Define `system.<host>: { … }`, or select one of the systems the config already defines.

rows.meaning: A `jet os` config file doesn't exist (D-JPK-OSHOST1)
rows.what: The `jet os` config file doesn't exist.
rows.why: A bare host loads `./config.jet`; `host@root` loads `root/config.jet` when `root` is a directory, or the file named by `root`.
rows.fix: Create it with `jet os init <host>`, or pass an external root as `host@root`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Create it with `jet os init <host>`, or pass an external root as `host@root`.

rows.meaning: `use <pkg>` names an `executable` package — executables go on PATH, not `use` (U17)
rows.what: `use <pkg>` named a package that is realized as an `executable`.
rows.why: U17: one import concept (`use`) covers files, modules, and `library` packages; an `executable` package installs a binary on your PATH — you run it, you don't import its code.
rows.fix: Remove the `use`, and run the executable's binary instead; or, if you meant to import its code, change the package to `library` in `package.jet`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Remove the `use`, and run the executable's binary instead; or, if you meant to import its code, change the package to `library` in `package.jet`.

rows.meaning: `use <pkg>` names a declared `library` dependency that hasn't been realized yet (U17)
rows.what: `use <pkg>` named a `library` dependency the project declares but that hasn't been realized (its source isn't staged in the shared hangar store, and isn't on disk as a path dep).
rows.why: U17: `jet build`/`check`/`test` never realize on demand; `jet run` delegates a declared project environment to Jetpack, but `--no-prepare` and standalone undeclared dependencies remain non-resolving.
rows.fix: Run `jetpack env --prep` to realize the library into the hangar, or rerun `jet run` without `--no-prepare` from the declaring project.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Run `jetpack env --prep` to realize the library into the hangar, or rerun `jet run` without `--no-prepare` from the declaring project.

rows.meaning: Value crossing a concurrent boundary is not sendable (D-CONC-CROSS1)
rows.what: A value crossing a task, channel, parallel-worker, or safe-kernel boundary is not sendable.
rows.why: Concurrent boundaries move owned data between workers. A view, trait value, mutable capture, borrowed closure, or thread-confined cell cannot cross.
rows.fix: Send plain owned data, make an ordinary owned copy when permitted, or use `Shared<T>` for deliberate shared state.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Send plain owned data, make an ordinary owned copy when permitted, or use `Shared<T>` for deliberate shared state.

rows.what: `.detach()` called on a task that had a sendability error (E1102) at spawn.
rows.why: A detached task runs unsupervised and may outlive the caller; a task that already has sendability problems is doubly unsafe to detach.
rows.fix: Fix the E1102 error at the spawn site first; once the task only holds owned data, `.detach()` is safe.

rows.meaning: `#Layout(c)` struct contains a growable field (D-REPRC1)
rows.what: `#Layout(c)` struct contains a field whose type is growable (`[T]`, `Map`, or `String`).
rows.why: Growable Rust heap types don't have a stable C layout — the raw data pointer and length live at unpredictable offsets.
rows.fix: Use a fixed-size array `[T#N]` instead, or remove `#Layout(c)` if C interop is not required.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use a fixed-size array `[T#N]` instead, or remove `#Layout(c)` if C interop is not required.

rows.meaning: `#Layout(packed)` / first-argument `#Layout(align(N))` not yet supported (D-REPRC1 reserved)

rows.why: The supported variants are `c`, `columnar`, and the second argument `align(N)` on `#Layout(c)`; `packed` and first-argument `align` remain reserved.
rows.fix: Use `#Layout(c)`, `#Layout(c, align(64))`, or `#Layout(columnar)`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use `#Layout(c)`, `#Layout(c, align(64))`, or `#Layout(columnar)`.

rows.meaning: `.detach()` called on a task that captured a `view` borrow (D-DETACH1) — the view may outlive the caller
rows.what: `.detach()` called on a task that captured a `view` borrow.
rows.why: A detached task runs unsupervised and may outlive the borrow's source; the captured `view` would dangle.
rows.fix: Pass an owned `copy`, or a `Shared<T>` handle, to the task instead of a `view`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass an owned `copy`, or a `Shared<T>` handle, to the task instead of a `view`.

rows.meaning: `columnar [T]` per-container layout prefix is reserved (D-SOA2C)
rows.what: The per-container layout prefix `columnar [T]` was written in a type.
rows.why: A per-use columnar override isn't built yet — only the whole-struct form `#Layout(columnar) struct …` ships in v1 (D-SOA2C reserves this spelling).
rows.fix: Put `#Layout(columnar)` on the `struct` declaration instead.

rows.meaning: List method not yet supported on a `#Layout(columnar)` list (D-SOA1)
rows.what: A list method (e.g. `.map`, `.filter`, `.sort`, `.pop`, `.remove`, `.get`) was called on a `#Layout(columnar)` list.
rows.why: v1 columnar lists support the core surface — indexing, field access, `len`, `is_empty`, `push`, and iteration; the rest is deferred rather than silently miscompiled.
rows.fix: Drop `#Layout(columnar)` from the struct to use the full list API, or rewrite the operation with indexing and a loop.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Drop `#Layout(columnar)` from the struct to use the full list API, or rewrite the operation with indexing and a loop.

rows.meaning: Partial `#Layout(columnar: …)` is deferred — whole-struct only in v1 (D-SOA2B)
rows.what: A partial columnar annotation `#Layout(columnar: f, g)` was written.
rows.why: v1 supports whole-struct columnar only — every field becomes a column; per-field columnar needs new ownership/aliasing surface (D-SOA2B, deferred).
rows.fix: Write `#Layout(columnar)` to convert the whole struct.

rows.meaning: `task` has no active lexical or parameter task group, targets a group other than the innermost active one, or lets `Group` escape (D-CONC-SPAWN1=D, D-TASKGROUP-PARAM1)
rows.what: The bare `task` keyword needs a lexical `task.group` or a `Group` parameter, always targets the innermost active one, or `Group` is stored or captured by an escaping lambda.
rows.why: Structured spawning uses the innermost active lexical `task.group` or a direct `Group` parameter. A group may flow down the call stack, but it cannot become stored state or escape its scope.
rows.fix: Write `task work()` inside the active group, or pass that handle directly to `fn helper(group: Group)`; do not store or capture it.

rows.meaning: *Retired by D-CONC-CROSS1; parallel crossings use E1101/E1102*

rows.meaning: A task combinator has no task branch (D-CONCSELECT1)

rows.why: A task combinator must have a child to join or select

rows.meaning: Write through a frozen value (D-CONC-FREEZE1=A)
rows.what: `{name}` cannot {action}; it was frozen at {freeze_site}
rows.why: `freeze(...)` creates a deeply immutable owned snapshot so a task can read it without a race. A write through any field or index would change that snapshot.
rows.fix: Create a new value, freeze a new snapshot, or use `Shared`/`Cell` when shared mutation is intentional
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Create a new value, freeze a new snapshot, or use `Shared`/`Cell` when shared mutation is intentional

rows.meaning: freeze source is not deeply snapshot-able (D-CONC-FREEZE1=A)

rows.why: A frozen value must be an owned cloneable value with no shared handle, resource, function, trait value, or mutable view inside it.
rows.fix: Use `^` to give the owned value to the task, use `Shared`/`Cell` for deliberate shared state, or rebuild a plain owned value
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use `^` to give the owned value to the task, use `Shared`/`Cell` for deliberate shared state, or rebuild a plain owned value

rows.meaning: Teaching: retired `Shared.new(x)` constructor → prefix `shared x` (D-CONC-SHARE1=A)
rows.what: `Shared.new(…)` is the retired shared-cell constructor.
rows.why: D-CONC-SHARE1=A gives shared state one construction word, so every shared cell reads the same on the page.
rows.fix: Write `shared <value>` instead of `Shared.new(<value>)`.

rows.meaning: Teaching: retired `Shared.read(f)`/`Shared.edit(f)` closures → plain field access (D-CONC-SHARE1=A)
rows.what: `` `Shared.{method}(…)` is the retired closure form for shared access. ``
rows.why: D-CONC-SHARE1=A made a shared value read and write like a value: a field read is one locked read, a field write is one locked write, and each statement is one atomic step. The closure per touch proved nothing the compiler did not already know.
rows.fix: Read the field directly (`config.name`) and write it directly (`config.hits += 1`); group several steps under `#Transact {{ … }}`, or take an expert guard with `.guard_edit()`.

rows.meaning: `task.all` mixes named and positional branches (D-CONC-ALLNAMED1=A)
rows.what: `task.all` branches must all be named or all positional.
rows.why: D-CONC-ALLNAMED1=A gives named results stable record fields and keeps positional results as ordered lists; mixing the two shapes would make the result type ambiguous.
rows.fix: Use `task.all { first: work(), second: other() }`, or remove every branch label.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use `task.all { first: work(), second: other() }`, or remove every branch label.

rows.meaning: Legacy `#Align(…)` marker is not supported (D-PLACE1=A)
rows.what: `#Align(…)` is not a supported layout marker.
rows.why: D-PLACE1=A puts alignment in the registered `#Layout(c, align(N))` rule so the layout kind and alignment remain one declaration fact.
rows.fix: Replace `#Align(64)` with `#Layout(c, align(64))` on the struct declaration.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Replace `#Align(64)` with `#Layout(c, align(64))` on the struct declaration.

rows.meaning: Layout alignment value is not usable (D-PLACE1=A)
rows.what: `align({value})` is not a usable layout alignment.
rows.why: `#Layout(c, align(N))` requires a positive power-of-two byte alignment no larger than 1048576 bytes; {reason}.
rows.fix: Write `#Layout(c, align({suggestion}))` with a positive power-of-two byte value no larger than 1048576 bytes.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `#Layout(c, align({suggestion}))` with a positive power-of-two byte value no larger than 1048576 bytes.

rows.what: `policy.lints.deny` takes a lint name, not diagnostic code `{code}`.

rows.meaning: Unsupported lock format version (D-BUILDCOMPAT1)
rows.what: The lock file `{path}` declares unsupported format version `{version}`.
rows.why: During `jet build`, this reader supports lock format version `{supported}`. An unsupported marker may change required meanings, so Jet stopped before using or rewriting the lock.
rows.fix: Use a Jet toolchain that supports version `{version}`, or remove the lock only after confirming its dependencies and rerun an unlocked build to create version `{supported}`.

rows.meaning: A dependency in `package.jet` has no locked revision — `--locked`/publish needs every dep pinned (D-SUPPLY1)
rows.what: `{dep}` is in `package.jet` but has no locked revision.
rows.why: A `--locked` build (and `jet registry publish`) requires every dependency to be pinned in the lockfile to a resolved version, so the build is reproducible. The dep is declared but not pinned.
rows.fix: Run `jet fetch` to resolve and pin `{dep}`, then commit the lockfile.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Run `jet fetch` to resolve and pin the dependency, then commit the lockfile.

rows.meaning: A breaking public-API change is published under a non-major version bump (D-SUPPLY1)
rows.what: Publishing `{new}` after `{old}` is a {bump} bump but breaks the public API item `{item}`.
rows.why: A {bump} bump promises callers no breaking changes under SemVer, but the public API changed since `{old}`. This is the local publish-time gate; the registry re-checks live with E2601 on receipt.
rows.fix: Bump to `{next_major}.0.0` (a major release), or restore `{item}` (a deprecated shim counts). Use `--force` to publish anyway with an explicit warning banner.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Bump to the next major version, or restore the removed public item.

rows.meaning: Unknown build profile name passed to `--profile` (D-BUILDPROFILE1)
rows.what: `--profile={name}` is not a defined build profile.
rows.why: Blessed profiles `release`, `debug`, and `ci` have built-in defaults. Any other name must be declared in your `package.jet` `build { }` block as `{name}: Build{ optimize: … }`.
rows.fix: Use `--release` for the release profile, `--profile=debug` for debug, `--profile=ci` for CI, or add `{name}: Build{ optimize: full }` (or `none`/`basic`) to the `build { }` block in `package.jet`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Select the desired profile or declare its build settings in `package.jet`.

rows.meaning: A transitive dependency uses an effect outside the `package.jet` `authority.holds` budget (Panic names the stop site) (D-EFFBUDGET1, D-NOPANIC1=D)
rows.what: `{dep}` uses the `{effect}` effect, which this package's budget doesn't allow.
rows.why: An `authority.holds` budget fails the build when any dependency reaches an effect you didn't list; a denied `Panic` row names the stop site.
rows.fix: For an ordinary effect, add `{effect}` to `authority.holds.allow` or grant it to `{dep}` in `authority.grants`; for deny-only `Panic`, return a fallible result or add facts/`#Pre`/refinement proof.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Grant the required effect or change the source to stay within the declared authority.

rows.meaning: A malformed `authority:` block in `package.jet` (D-AUTHORITY-MANIFEST1)
rows.what: `package.jet` has a malformed `authority:` block.
rows.why: `authority: { holds: { allow: […], deny: […] }, grants: { "dep": […] }, trust: { … }, providers: { … } }` is the one package authority block; rights use the thirteen grantable roots, the `FFI` parent and its language leaves including `FFI.Go`, `FFI.Py`, and `FFI.Octave`, and deny-only `Panic`/`Mem`.
rows.fix: Fix the authority field or right name; see docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md D-AUTHORITY-MANIFEST1.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Fix the authority field or right name; see docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md D-AUTHORITY-MANIFEST1.

rows.meaning: `jetpack.toml` is retired (D-ONCE-RETIRE1)
rows.what: `jetpack.toml` is retired.
rows.why: Package identity and named sources now live in `package.jet` and `env.jet`, so dependency resolution uses one Jet grammar (D-ONCE-RETIRE1).
rows.fix: Move `[repo]` `name`/`version` to `package.jet`, move `[sources]` entries to `env.jet` `sources: { … }`, then delete `jetpack.toml`.

rows.meaning: A retired manifest filename (`pkg.jet`/`pack.jet`/`payload.jet`/`jet.toml`) found where `package.jet` belongs (D-ECO-FILEROOT1)
rows.what: `{name}` is not the package manifest name — Jet reads `package.jet`.
rows.why: The manifest filename is frozen to one spelling (D-ECO-FILEROOT1) so tooling, docs, and every worked example never have to guess which file to read. `pkg.jet`, `pack.jet`, `payload.jet`, and `jet.toml` are retired names from earlier manifest reshapes.
rows.fix: Rename `{name}` to `package.jet`.

rows.meaning: `jet` and the `jetpack`/`jetos` engine binary disagree on protocol version (D-JPK-DISPATCH1)
rows.what: `jet` {jet_version} and `{engine}` {engine_version} disagree.
rows.why: `jet` and its engine binaries (`jetpack`, `jetos`) ship as one toolchain and must match exactly — a version-skewed engine may not understand what `jet` sends it. `jet` checks this with an `--engine-protocol` handshake before running any engine verb. A `jet os` or `jet image` dispatch reports this engine error.
rows.fix: Use matching `jet`/`{engine}` versions — reinstall the toolchain so both binaries come from the same release.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use matching `jet` and engine versions from one installed toolchain.

rows.meaning: An engine verb needs an engine binary (`jetpack`/`jetos`) that isn't installed (D-JPK-DISPATCH1)
rows.what: `{verb}` needs the `{engine}` engine, which isn't installed.
rows.why: `{verb}` is an engine verb — `jet` execs `{engine}` for it (D-JPK-DISPATCH1) rather than linking package-manager/OS logic into the compiler binary. A `jet os` or `jet image` dispatch reports this engine error.
rows.fix: Install the matching Jet toolchain; the `{engine}` binary ships alongside `jet`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Install the matching Jet toolchain so its engine binary ships with `jet`.

rows.meaning: A role-module contribution uses the retired `module name { ns.path: Type.{ } }` form (D-JPK-MODBODY1)
rows.what: Role namespace `{ns}` belongs in the module declaration name.
rows.why: `module {name} { {ns}.{role}: {Type}.{ … } }` splits the role across two places; the canonical form puts it once, in the declaration name, so discovery-by-declaration (`module env.dev`) reads the role straight off the name (D-JPK-MODBODY1).
rows.fix: Write `module {ns}.{role} { … }` and move the contribution's fields up to the module body.

rows.meaning: A bare/path-form ref matched more than one workspace member (D-MONOREF1)
rows.what: `{query}` matches more than one workspace member.
rows.why: A bare (`logging`) or path-form (`packages/logging`) ref with no `@source` suffix resolves against the workspace member index; this one is not unique (D-MONOREF1).
rows.fix: Address one member by its relative path (e.g. `infra/logging`), or use `package@source`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Address one member by its relative path (e.g. `infra/logging`), or use `package@source`.

rows.meaning: A bare/path-form ref matched no workspace member (D-MONOREF1)
rows.what: `{query}` is not a workspace member.
rows.why: A bare/path-form ref must name a member listed in `workspace.jet` `members:`; nothing in the index matched (D-MONOREF1).
rows.fix: Use one of the listed members (a did-you-mean is offered), fix the name, or add the package to `members:`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use one of the listed members (a did-you-mean is offered), fix the name, or add the package to `members:`.

rows.meaning: A monorepo source could not be fetched — sparse subtree checkout and full-clone fallback both failed (D-MONOREF1)
rows.what: A monorepo source could not be fetched.
rows.why: Resolving a monorepo package fetches the source's workspace index and materializes only the addressed subtree; both the sparse subtree checkout and the full-clone fallback failed (D-MONOREF1).
rows.fix: Correct the source URL and revision in `package.jet`, then run `jet fetch` again.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Check the source URL/rev and network access; if the provider lacks partial-clone support the full clone should still work, so this usually means the rev or repo is unreachable.

rows.meaning: An in-repo dependency names a package outside the source's workspace index (D-MONOREF1)
rows.what: In-repo dependency `{name}` is outside the workspace.
rows.why: A member's `package.jet` depends on another in-repo package, but that package is not in the source repo's `workspace.jet` member index, so the sparse checkout can't include it (D-MONOREF1).
rows.fix: Add the dependency to the source repo's `workspace.jet` `members:`, or depend on it as an external `package@source` ref.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Add the dependency to the source repo's `workspace.jet` `members:`, or depend on it as an external `package@source` ref.

rows.meaning: `jet registry publish` refused: the version already exists in the registry index and is not yanked — versions are immutable (D-VERSION1)
rows.what: `{name}` {version} already exists in the registry index and is not yanked.
rows.why: Published versions are immutable (D-VERSION1) — a version can never be overwritten, only yanked, so anyone who already locked it keeps building the exact same bytes.
rows.fix: Bump the version in `package.jet` and publish again, or `jet registry yank {version}` the existing one first if it was a mistake (yanking hides it from new resolution; it does not free the version number for reuse).
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Bump the package version or yank the existing version before publishing again.

rows.meaning: `jet registry publish`/`jet registry yank` couldn't reach the registry index, or the endpoint contains embedded credentials or URL parameters
rows.what: Couldn't reach the registry index at `{url}`.
rows.why: The Git registry transport rejects URL userinfo and query/fragment parameters before any network operation. Otherwise the Git operation failed because of network, authentication, or stale local-clone state; authentication comes from the host Git credential provider with path-scoped helper requests, and rendered endpoint details are redacted.
rows.fix: Remove credentials and URL parameters, configure the host Git credential provider for the registry path, then check network access or set `JET_REGISTRY_URL` to a reachable mirror.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Remove credentials and URL parameters, configure the host Git credential provider for the registry path, then check network access or set `JET_REGISTRY_URL` to a reachable mirror.

rows.meaning: A build fetch is unlocked or carries credentials in its URL (D-JPK-ADAPTER1)
rows.what: A build fetch is not an allowed locked, credential-free input.
rows.why: Build hooks admit only content-hash-pinned fetches without URL userinfo or credential query/fragment fields; credentials in URLs could enter action identity, cache metadata, or logs (D-JPK-ADAPTER1).
rows.fix: Add the source hash, remove URL credentials, or vendor the source with `jet registry vendor`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Add the source hash, remove URL credentials, or vendor the source with `jet registry vendor`.

rows.meaning: A build step wrote outside the package output root (D-JPK-ADAPTER1)
rows.what: A build step tried to write outside the output root.
rows.why: A build may only install files under its own package output root; writing elsewhere would let a build mutate the machine or other packages (D-JPK-ADAPTER1).
rows.fix: Install into a path under the output root (no `..`, no absolute paths).
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Install into a path under the output root (no `..`, no absolute paths).

rows.meaning: A build recipe or staged plan fragment violated its realized-tool, sandbox, authority, or finite-graph contract (D-JPK-ADAPTER1, D-JPK-DYNAMICPLAN1)
rows.what: Build recipe or staged plan action is not a valid declared action graph.
rows.why: Build tools must be realized adapter `deps:` packages, and staged plan fragments must use only declared inputs, tools, effects, platform facts, non-overlapping outputs, and acyclic dependencies; a build never falls through to host state or recursive resolution (D-JPK-ADAPTER1, D-JPK-DYNAMICPLAN1).
rows.fix: Realize every named tool, declare every input and authority fact, fix the output/dependency graph, and retry the stage.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Realize every named tool, declare every input and authority fact, fix the output/dependency graph, and retry the stage.

rows.meaning: `module workspace` declared in more than one file (discovery-by-declaration, D-JPK-FILENAME2)
rows.what: `module workspace` is declared in more than one file: `{list}`.
rows.why: The workspace index is discovered by declaration (D-JPK-FILENAME2), so exactly one file may declare `module workspace { … }`.
rows.fix: Keep one declaration (conventionally in `workspace.jet`) and delete the others.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Keep one declaration (conventionally in `workspace.jet`) and delete the others.

rows.meaning: No realized Rust toolchain and no Nix to build an `extern rust` bridge dep (D-JPK-BUILDTOOL1)
rows.what: No Rust build toolchain is available to build this package.
rows.why: Building an `extern rust` bridge dependency needs a pinned Rust toolchain realized into the hangar, or Nix; neither is present (D-JPK-BUILDTOOL1). A `jet build` run reports this toolchain error.
rows.fix: Run `jet update jet` to realize the pinned toolchain, or install Nix so the bridge builds through the compatibility provider.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Run `jet update jet` to realize the pinned toolchain, or install Nix so the bridge builds through the compatibility provider.

rows.meaning: A staged `core.<ring>` artifact is missing for the active platform (D-JPK-RINGSHIP1)
rows.what: The staged `core.{ring}` artifact is missing for this platform.
rows.why: The active toolchain object carries prebuilt ring artifacts, but none for `core.{ring}` on this platform (D-JPK-RINGSHIP1). A `jet build` run reports this toolchain error.
rows.fix: The build falls back to the compiler-embedded `core.{ring}`; to ship the staged artifact, realize a toolchain object built for this platform (`jet update jet`).
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use the embedded core artifact, or realize a toolchain object built for this platform.

rows.meaning: A captured `fleet.<name>` host references an unknown captured `system.<name>` (D-JETOS-FREEZE1)
rows.what: The fleet `{fleet}` host `{host}` names an unknown captured system `{system}`.
rows.why: D-JETOS-FREEZE1: fleets are frozen jetos research capture; captured hosts must still point at a captured system so the plan is coherent.
rows.fix: Define captured `system.{system}: { … }`, or point the host at an existing captured system.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Define the captured system or point the host at an existing captured system.

rows.meaning: `jet push <fleet>` on a valid fleet — deployment gated on single-host jetos realization (U15, Phase D)
rows.what: Fleet `{fleet}` is validated, but `jet push` is not available yet.
rows.why: The fleet's hosts parse and cross-check clean, but rolling a fleet out over ssh needs single-host jetos realization, which is gated (U15; Phase D, owner greenlight required). `jet push` never fakes a deploy.
rows.fix: Until the jetos realization tier lands, `jet push` captures and validates fleets without deploying them.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Until the jetos realization tier lands, `jet push` captures and validates fleets without deploying them.

rows.meaning: An unknown field on a captured `Fleet` record (D-JETOS-FREEZE1)
rows.what: `{field}` isn't a captured `Fleet` field.
rows.why: D-JETOS-FREEZE1: fleet deployment remains frozen jetos research; only `hosts` is captured for planning.
rows.fix: Remove `{field}`; captured fleets use `hosts: { … }`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Remove the unknown field; captured fleets use the `hosts` field.

rows.meaning: A captured `Fleet` with no `hosts:` map (D-JETOS-FREEZE1)
rows.what: This captured `Fleet` has no `hosts`.
rows.why: D-JETOS-FREEZE1: fleet deployment is frozen jetos research, but captured fleets still name hosts for later planning.
rows.fix: Add `hosts: { web1: system.<name> }` if this is research capture.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Add `hosts: { web1: system.<name> }` if this is research capture.

rows.meaning: A package signature doesn't verify against its pinned public key (D-PKGSIGN1)
rows.what: Signature verification failed for `{name}` {version}: the signature doesn't match the recorded public key.
rows.why: This means the package was tampered with after signing, or the index entry is corrupt — the author's Ed25519 signature over the content hash no longer checks out (D-PKGSIGN1).
rows.fix: Do not use this version. Re-run `jet fetch` after clearing the store entry; if the problem persists, report it — this should never happen for an untampered registry.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Do not use this version. Re-run `jet fetch` after clearing the store entry; if the problem persists, report it — this should never happen for an untampered registry.

rows.meaning: A registry with `require_signed: true` served an unsigned package (D-PKGSIGN1)
rows.what: Registry `{registry}` requires signed packages (`require_signed: true`) but `{name}` {version} has no signature.
rows.why: The registry is configured to accept only author-signed releases; an unsigned entry can't be trusted under that policy (D-PKGSIGN1).
rows.fix: Use a different registry, or ask the package author to publish a signed release (`jet registry publish` auto-signs by default — they likely used `--no-sign`).
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use a different registry, or ask the package author to publish a signed release (`jet registry publish` auto-signs by default — they likely used `--no-sign`).

rows.meaning: `jet registry keygen` refused: a signing key already exists (use `--force`) (D-PKGSIGN1)
rows.what: `jet registry keygen` refused: a signing key already exists at `{path}`.
rows.why: Overwriting it would orphan every package you've published under the old key — consumers who pinned it (TOFU) would require a reviewed, re-signed takeover release (D-PKGSIGN1).
rows.fix: Use `jet registry keygen --force` if you're sure (e.g. the old key was compromised), or back it up first with `jet registry key backup`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use `jet registry keygen --force` if you're sure (e.g. the old key was compromised), or back it up first with `jet registry key backup`.

rows.meaning: A `jet:` toolchain pin in `package.jet` isn't a valid version/channel ref (D-JPK-TOOLCHAIN1)
rows.what: `{value}` is not a valid toolchain pin.
rows.why: The `jet:` field pins which Jet toolchain builds this project (D-JPK-TOOLCHAIN1); its value is a channel ref, not a version range. `>=1.0.0`-style constraints don't name one reproducible toolchain. A `jet build` run reports this toolchain error.
rows.fix: Write a channel: `jet: 0.4` (track the 0.4 series), `jet: 0.4.2` (exact), or a named channel like `jet: main`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Write a channel: `jet: 0.4` (track the 0.4 series), `jet: 0.4.2` (exact), or a named channel like `jet: main`.

rows.meaning: A `jet:` channel pin is unlocked under `--offline`/CI — no `[[toolchain]]` lock entry (D-JPK-TOOLCHAIN1)
rows.what: Toolchain channel `{channel}` is pinned but not locked.
rows.why: An `--offline`/CI build won't resolve a channel — it needs the exact toolchain version recorded in `.jet/lock`, and none is present (D-JPK-TOOLCHAIN1). Resolving a channel reaches the network, which offline/CI forbids. A `jet build` run reports this toolchain error.
rows.fix: Run `jet update jet` to resolve `{channel}` to an exact version, then commit `.jet/lock`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Resolve the channel to an exact version with `jet update jet`, then commit `.jet/lock`.

rows.meaning: The pinned Jet toolchain has no prebuilt object for this platform — never source-built (D-JPK-TOOLCHAIN1)
rows.what: Toolchain {channel} ({version}) isn't available for {platform}.
rows.why: This project pins a Jet toolchain, but no prebuilt object for it was found for this platform. Jet realizes the pinned compiler as a prebuilt — it never builds the compiler from source and never silently falls back to a different `jet` (D-JPK-TOOLCHAIN1). A `jet build` run reports this toolchain error.
rows.fix: Move the pin with `jet update jet <channel>` to a toolchain your platform has, or install the pinned toolchain from the release page.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Move the pin with `jet update jet <channel>` to a toolchain your platform has, or install the pinned toolchain from the release page.

rows.meaning: `jet init` refused: a `package.jet` already exists here (D-JPK-TOOLCHAIN1)
rows.what: `jet init` refused: a `package.jet` already exists here.
rows.why: `jet init` writes a fresh package manifest pinning the running toolchain; overwriting one would discard its dependencies, pins, and identity (D-JPK-TOOLCHAIN1).
rows.fix: Edit the existing manifest, or run `jet init` in an empty directory.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Edit the existing manifest, or run `jet init` in an empty directory.

rows.meaning: An inline script dependency (`use pkg#version;`) didn't resolve (D-JPK-SCRIPTDEP1)
rows.what: Inline dependency `{name}#{selector}` didn't resolve.
rows.why: A manifest-less script's `use {name}#{selector};` has no source to resolve from — the Jet package registry has no fetch path yet, so an inline dependency only resolves from a committed local copy (D-JPK-SCRIPTDEP1).
rows.fix: Commit a copy at `.jet/inline-deps/{name}/<version>/`, or run `jet init` and depend on `{name}` through `package.jet` once you have a real source for it.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Commit a local inline dependency copy, or initialize a package and declare the dependency there.

rows.meaning: Project-level `jet dev` has neither `fn dev()` nor `fn run()` in its entry file (U19, D-JPK-DEVCOMPOSE1)
rows.what: This project has no `jet dev` entry.
rows.why: Project-level `jet dev` (no file argument) runs the entry file's top-level `fn dev()` if it defines one, else `fn run()` (U19, D-JPK-DEVCOMPOSE1). The entry file defines neither.
rows.fix: Add `fn dev() { … }` (a custom dev command) or `fn run() { … }` (the default) to the entry file.
