rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Add `fn dev() { … }` (a custom dev command) or `fn run() { … }` (the default) to the entry file.

rows.meaning: An untrusted project environment or build hook hit a non-interactive path with no `--trust`/exact grant (U19, D-JPK-DEVCOMPOSE1, D-JPK-BUILDSCRIPT1)
rows.what: This project's environment isn't trusted yet.
rows.why: Entering a project's declared env (`jet env`/`jet dev`) is a supply-chain decision — first entry to a repo that declares packages needs a trust decision (U19, D-JPK-DEVCOMPOSE1). stdin isn't a terminal, so an interactive prompt would hang instead of asking.
rows.fix: Pass `--trust` for this one run, or pre-authorize with `jet config trust add <pattern>`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Pass `--trust` for this one run, or pre-authorize with `jet config trust add <pattern>`.

rows.meaning: Bounded native projection cannot translate a foreign flake/devShell surface into Jet facts (U16)
rows.what: `{cmd}` cannot project the foreign environment.
rows.why: The bounded native evaluator could not translate the foreign `flake.nix`/`devenv.nix` surface into Jet facts (U16). Jet does not shell out to an installed Nix binary for this path.
rows.fix: Use the supported literal devShell fields, run `jet os bridge flake` for the loss report, or declare the environment in `env.*`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use the supported literal devShell fields, run `jet os bridge flake` for the loss report, or declare the environment in `env.*`.

rows.meaning: A `target: sandbox` package's exported interface changed incompatibly since the last frozen build (D-PLUGIN-VERSION1=A)
rows.what: This sandbox's exported interface changed incompatibly.
rows.why: A `target: sandbox` package's frozen exported interface is the load-time contract (D-PLUGIN-VERSION1=A) — a prior build's `.jet/cache/api` snapshot shows an export was removed or its signature changed. Adding a new export is always compatible.
rows.fix: Restore the removed/changed export, or accept this as an intentional breaking change (delete the stale snapshot to re-freeze).
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Restore the removed/changed export, or accept this as an intentional breaking change (delete the stale snapshot to re-freeze).

rows.meaning: A `target: sandbox` package's own code uses an effect — sandboxes are deny-by-default, zero host authority (D-PLUGIN1=B)
rows.what: A sandbox can't use any effect.
rows.why: This package builds as `target: sandbox` (D-PLUGIN1=B) — sandboxes run with zero host authority (the wasmtime host registers no host imports), so any effect (`FS`/`Net`/`DB`/…) would fail to instantiate at load time. There is no gate or grant to widen this (I1: the sandbox is the safety boundary, not an opt-in).
rows.fix: Remove the effectful call, or move it out of the sandbox into the host program that loads it.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Remove the effectful call, or move it out of the sandbox into the host program that loads it.

rows.meaning: Couldn't build a sandbox's WASM Component — missing/failed `rustc`/`wasm-tools` toolchain (D-DEP-WASM1=A)
rows.what: Couldn't build the sandbox's WASM Component.
rows.why: Building a `target: sandbox` package shells out to `rustc --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `wasm-tools component embed`/`new` (D-DEP-WASM1=A); one of them is missing or failed.
rows.fix: Make sure `rustc` supports `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `wasm-tools` is on PATH (both ship in the project's `nix develop` shell).
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Make sure `rustc` supports `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `wasm-tools` is on PATH (both ship in the project's `nix develop` shell).

rows.meaning: A sandbox's exported `pub fn` isn't one homogeneous `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, or `Text` shape (D-PLUGIN-EXPORT1=A)
rows.what: A sandbox's exported function has an unsupported signature.
rows.why: Every parameter and the return type of a sandbox export must use the same Component Model scalar: `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, or `Text`.
rows.fix: Narrow the signature to one homogeneous scalar shape, or drop `pub` if this function isn't meant to be called across the sandbox boundary.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Narrow the signature to one homogeneous scalar shape, or drop `pub` if this function isn't meant to be called across the sandbox boundary.

rows.meaning: A dev-supervised service never became healthy within the readiness timeout (U12)
rows.what: Service `{name}` never became healthy.
rows.why: `jet dev`/`jetpack services up` supervises a `services:` process, then polls its readiness contract (`ready:`, else a TCP probe on its first `ports:` entry, else a bare process-alive check) until it passes or a timeout elapses (U12); it never passed in time.
rows.fix: Check `jetpack services logs {name}` for what the process printed, confirm its `run`/`ready` declarations are correct, or raise the timeout isn't configurable yet — fix the service itself.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Inspect the service logs and correct its `run` or `ready` declaration before retrying.

rows.meaning: A dev-supervised `Service` field jetpack doesn't recognize at supervision time (U12)
rows.what: Service `{name}` has a field jetpack doesn't recognize: `{field}`.
rows.why: A dev-supervised `Service` stays the one ratified open record (U12) at parse time, but jetpack's dev-runtime tier is the only consumer of a dev service's fields — unlike the jetos `system.*.services` capture, nothing downstream forwards unread metadata, so an unrecognized key here is almost always a typo. A `jetpack services` run reports this service declaration error.
rows.fix: Rename `{field}` to one of the recognized keys (`enable`, `ports`, `run`, `shutdown`, `data_dir`, `ready`, `after`, `before_start`, `sockets`, `restart`, `watch`), or remove it.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Rename the field to a recognized service key or remove it.

rows.meaning: `jetpack secrets get <name>` names an entry that isn't in the encrypted store (D-JPK-SECRETCRYPTO1)
rows.what: No secret named `{name}`.
rows.why: `jetpack secrets get {name}` decrypted the store (`.jet/secrets.age`) fine, but it has no entry called `{name}` (D-JPK-SECRETCRYPTO1).
rows.fix: Set it first with `jetpack secrets set {name} <value>`, or check the spelling.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Set the secret entry first with `jetpack secrets set`, or check its name.

rows.meaning: A function reaches `core.crypto.vault.get` without declaring the `Secret` effect (D-JPK-SECRETCRYPTO1)
rows.what: `{fn}` reads a secret but doesn't declare the `Secret` effect.
rows.why: Reading a secret (`core.crypto.vault.get`) always requires an explicit grant (D-JPK-SECRETCRYPTO1) — unlike every other effect, there is no silently inferred default. A bare `fn` with no `-[…]>` list, or one that omits `Secret`, is rejected even though the same function may infer other effects.
rows.fix: Add `-[Secret]>` to `{fn}`'s signature, or add `Secret` to its existing effect ceiling.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Add `Secret` to the function effect ceiling before reading the vault.

rows.meaning: `core.crypto.vault.get` reached from a build-time (comptime) context — secrets are never readable at build time (D-JPK-SECRETCRYPTO1)
rows.what: `core.crypto.vault.get` can't be reached from a build-time context.
rows.why: Module-field and comptime evaluation run before secrets are decrypted (D-JPK-SECRETCRYPTO1). A repository opens its encrypted store only at ordinary runtime, such as inside a `-[Secret]>` function. There is no audited gate escape because a build artifact must never contain a decrypted secret.
rows.fix: Move the secret read out of comptime or module-field evaluation and into ordinary runtime code.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Move the secret read out of comptime or module-field evaluation and into ordinary runtime code.

rows.meaning: An `Image`'s `kind:` isn't active `.Oci`, or disagrees with what `from:` names (D-JPK-IMAGE1, D-JETOS-FREEZE1)
rows.what: `` `<word>` isn't an active image kind `` (or `` `kind: .<word>` doesn't match this image's `from:` ``).
rows.why: D-JPK-IMAGE1 + D-JETOS-FREEZE1: active Jetpack images use `.Oci`; `.Iso` disk images are frozen jetos research capture. A `jet image` run reports this image declaration error.
rows.fix: Write `kind: .Oci` for active Jetpack images, or keep `.Iso` only as research capture.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Write `kind: .Oci` for active Jetpack images, or keep `.Iso` only as research capture.

rows.meaning: An `.Oci` image's `from: packages.<name>` doesn't name an `executable`-kind package (U14, D-JPK-IMAGE1)
rows.what: The image `{image}` is built from a non-executable package `{package}`.
rows.why: D-JPK-IMAGE1: an `.Oci` image's `from: packages.<name>` must name a package this project's `package.jet` declares `executable` — a `library`-kind package has no binary to containerize, and an undeclared name can't be confirmed either way.
rows.fix: Declare `{package}: executable` in `package.jet`, or point `from:` at an existing executable package.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Declare an executable package in `package.jet`, or point the image at one.

rows.meaning: Remote OCI base or push needs a verified registry transport; local `file://` layouts are supported (U14, D-JPK-IMAGE1)
rows.what: `` `jet image <name>` cannot use remote OCI reference `<ref>`. ``
rows.why: D-JPK-IMAGE1: local OCI layouts are copied only after digest validation; remote registry transport is a separate trust boundary and is never faked.
rows.fix: Use `--push file:///path/to/layout`, or configure a verified registry transport.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use `--push file:///path/to/layout`, or configure a verified registry transport.

rows.meaning: An `.Oci` image field (`kind`/`expose`/`env_vars`/`files`/`base`) isn't shaped the way D-JPK-IMAGE1 spells it (U14)
rows.what: `` `<field>` isn't shaped like <expected>. ``
rows.why: D-JPK-IMAGE1: an `.Oci` image's `kind`/`expose`/`env_vars`/`files`/`base` fields each have one fixed shape (a bare leading-dot value, a list of ports, a string-keyed map, a list of paths, `oci("<ref>")`) — `Image` is a closed record, so a misshapen recognized field is rejected rather than silently ignored.
rows.fix: Rewrite the field to match its documented shape.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Rewrite the field to match its documented shape.

rows.meaning: An ad-hoc adapter declaration/source/recipe is not shaped or realizable (U20, D-JPK-ADAPTER1)
rows.what: Adapter package could not be realized.
rows.why: `Pkg.adapt(...)` turns source bytes into a normal package, so its string-valued `source:` must be a ref such as `"./vendor/tool"` and its recipe must be one of the supported U20 recipes: `Recipe.copy()`, `Recipe.prebuilt(bin:, as:)`, or finite `Recipe.build(steps: […])` actions (`.fetch`, `.exec`, `.install`, `.install_tree`). A `jetpack env` run reports this adapter-realization error.
rows.fix: Change `Pkg.adapt(...)` to use source `"./vendor/tool"` and a supported recipe such as `Recipe.copy()`, then rerun `jetpack env`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Check the `Pkg.adapt(...)` source and recipe.

rows.meaning: A channel source ref (`#latest`/`#main`/`#vN.x`) is not locked, or cannot be resolved during `jetpack update` (U21, D-JPK-CHANNEL1)
rows.what: Source channel `{name}` is not locked / could not be resolved.
rows.why: D-JPK-CHANNEL1 keeps tracking intent (`#latest`, `#main`, `#vN.x`) beside an exact lock entry. Build/run/env never re-resolve channels, and CI/offline may not invent a fresh exact source. A `jetpack update` run reports this package update error.
rows.fix: Run `jetpack update {name}` with network or fixture metadata, then commit `.jet/lock`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Run `jetpack update` with network or fixture metadata, then commit `.jet/lock`.

rows.meaning: One or more package refs lack a supported native Nix compatibility output (U23, D-JPK-NIXSTORE1)
rows.what: `{count}` package refs lack a supported Nix compatibility output.
rows.why: The listed refs need pinned compatibility outputs. Jetpack does not invoke an installed Nix executable for package realization, so native core and adapted packages can proceed while unsupported Nix refs are reported as holes. A `jetpack add` run reports this package-adapter error.
rows.fix: Provide a pinned fixture or verified Hangar output, or replace the listed refs with native sources/adapters; `jetpack add <ref> --adapt` drafts an adapter snippet.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Provide a pinned fixture or verified Hangar output, or replace the listed refs with native sources/adapters; `jetpack add <ref> --adapt` drafts an adapter snippet.

rows.meaning: A recipe-backed package build failed at a logged build step (U27, D-JPK-BUILDDBG1)
rows.what: Package build failed at a logged step.
rows.why: D-JPK-BUILDDBG1 preserves the failed build scratch under the hangar and records each recipe step's command/output. The primary error names the failed step instead of dumping provider noise.
rows.fix: Run `jet logs <pkg>` for the full per-step log, or rerun the build with `--shell-on-fail` to debug inside the preserved scratch.

rows.meaning: No persisted Store record or build explanation exists for the requested package/ref (U27, D-JPK-BUILDDBG1)
rows.what: No package record or build attempt exists for `{pkg}`.
rows.why: `jet explain` reads the Hangar Store and persisted Jetpack realization attempts. If neither record exists on this machine, there is no local package explanation.
rows.fix: Run `jet build <ref>` first; for diagnostic-code help, keep using `jet explain E1234`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Run `jet build <ref>` first; for diagnostic-code help, keep using `jet explain E1234`.

rows.meaning: No enforceable native sandbox is available for a local executable action (U28, D-JPK-SANDBOX2)
rows.what: Build sandboxing is required but unavailable.
rows.why: D-JPK-SANDBOX2 permits non-executing reuse and trusted substitution, but a local executable action needs the native child boundary. Jetpack refuses to launch it when the platform cannot enforce that boundary. A `jet build` run reports this sandbox error.
rows.fix: Provide a trusted substitute or approved remote builder, or enable the native sandbox, then retry.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Provide a trusted substitute or approved remote builder, or enable the native sandbox, then retry.

rows.meaning: `--offline` would need network access or a missing local package object (U29, D-JPK-OFFLINE1)
rows.what: `--offline` forbids network access.
rows.why: Realize-class verbs must run from the current lock and local hangar when offline. Network-class verbs (`add`, `update`, `outdated`, publish/cache sync) cannot refresh metadata under `--offline`, and a missing local object cannot be fetched.
rows.fix: Drop `--offline` for this command, or realize/fetch the needed object before going offline.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Drop `--offline` for this command, or realize/fetch the needed object before going offline.

rows.meaning: A jetos option key uses a retired namespace (D-JPK-OSNS1)
rows.what: A jetos option key uses a retired namespace.
rows.why: D-JPK-OSNS1=B and D-JOS-SYSTEMTREE1=A: jetos option keys start with full-word namespaces: `filesystem`, `network`, `packages`, `services`, `users`, `groups`, `secrets`, `boot`, `kernel`, `init`, or `health`.
rows.fix: Rename the option namespace, for example `net.hostName` becomes `network.hostName`.

rows.meaning: A jetos activation proof is incomplete (D-WD8)
rows.what: A jetos activation proof is incomplete.
rows.why: D-WD8 requires `jet os switch` to prove the plan, risk class, generated service artifacts, and rollback evidence before changing the active generation pointers.
rows.fix: Run `jet os switch` to regenerate the proof artifacts, or delete the hand-edited generation before retrying.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Rebuild the generation so the proof artifacts are regenerated, or discard a hand-edited generation.

rows.meaning: VM/media proof tools are missing (D-JOS-VMDEPS1)
rows.what: Jetos VM proof tools are missing.
rows.why: D-JOS-VMDEPS1=A requires pinned QEMU, firmware, ISO, bootloader, filesystem, EFI image, and initrd compression tools before install/reboot proof can run.
rows.fix: Realize or expose the required tools, then rerun `jet os vm prove <host> --disk <disk>`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Realize or expose the required tools, then rerun `jet os vm prove <host> --disk <disk>`.

rows.meaning: The first-party CachyOS kernel package is missing (D-JOS-KERNELSRC1)
rows.what: The jetos CachyOS kernel package is missing.
rows.why: D-JOS-KERNELSRC1=A: `.CachyOS` resolves to a first-party `cachyos-kernel` package with boot artifacts and provenance.
rows.fix: Declare a first-party source that provides `cachyos-kernel`, or select a different ratified kernel.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Declare a first-party source that provides `cachyos-kernel`, or select a different ratified kernel.

rows.meaning: The first-party systemd init package is missing (D-JPK-OSINIT1)
rows.what: The jetos systemd init package is missing.
rows.why: D-JPK-OSINIT1=A: the default jetos init path is systemd, so the generation needs a first-party `systemd` package with bootable init artifacts.
rows.fix: Declare a first-party source that provides `systemd`, or select a ratified init override.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Declare a first-party source that provides `systemd`, or select a ratified init override.

rows.meaning: The first-party CachyOS kernel package lacks bootable kernel/initrd artifacts (D-JOS-KERNELSRC1)
rows.what: The jetos CachyOS boot artifacts are missing.
rows.why: D-JOS-KERNELSRC1=A: the first-party `cachyos-kernel` package must provide a Linux kernel image and initrd with bootable file headers so the generation and installer can boot the same payload.
rows.fix: Add `boot/vmlinuz-cachyos` and `boot/initrd-cachyos` with real boot payloads, or select a different ratified kernel.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Add `boot/vmlinuz-cachyos` and `boot/initrd-cachyos` with real boot payloads, or select a different ratified kernel.

rows.meaning: The first-party systemd package lacks init artifacts (D-JPK-OSINIT1)
rows.what: The jetos systemd init artifact is missing.
rows.why: D-JPK-OSINIT1=A: the first-party `systemd` package must provide a bootable init binary for `/sbin/init`.
rows.fix: Add `bin/systemd`, `lib/systemd/systemd`, or `sbin/init` to the package output, or select a ratified init override.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Add `bin/systemd`, `lib/systemd/systemd`, or `sbin/init` to the package output, or select a ratified init override.

rows.meaning: The first-party CachyOS kernel package lacks source-built recipe/builder provenance (D-JOS-KERNELBOOTSTRAP1)
rows.what: The jetos CachyOS source recipe is missing.
rows.why: D-JOS-KERNELBOOTSTRAP1=A: the first-party `cachyos-kernel` package must carry source-built recipe, builder, config, patch, and initrd-input provenance beside the boot artifacts.
rows.fix: Add `source/recipe.jet`, `source/build.sh`, `source/config`, `source/patches.manifest`, and `source/initrd-inputs.manifest` to the package output.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Add `source/recipe.jet`, `source/build.sh`, `source/config`, `source/patches.manifest`, and `source/initrd-inputs.manifest` to the package output.

rows.meaning: The VM install/reboot harness exists but no guest proof has run (D-JOS-VMCOMMAND1)
rows.what: The jetos VM guest proof has not run.
rows.why: D-JOS-VMCOMMAND1=A and D-JOS-DESKTOP1=A require `jet os vm prove` to record an actual installer boot, disk install, reboot, serial guest verification, and graphical desktop verification before claiming proof. A written harness is not proof, and a guest proof must match the host, generation, disk, media proof, tool hashes, and terminal/desktop/graphical guest assertions.
rows.fix: Inspect the VM run logs, fix the boot/install path, then rerun `jet os vm prove` to capture a guest proof marker.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Inspect the VM run logs, fix the boot/install path, then rerun `jet os vm prove` to capture a guest proof marker.

rows.meaning: The first-party CachyOS kernel source recipe failed to build boot artifacts
rows.what: The jetos CachyOS source build failed.
rows.why: D-JOS-KERNELBOOTSTRAP1=A requires the first-party `cachyos-kernel` package to build boot artifacts from its recorded source recipe before VM/install proof can claim the selected `.CachyOS` kernel.
rows.fix: Check the first-party `cachyos-kernel` source recipe and rerun `jet os build`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Check the first-party `cachyos-kernel` source recipe and rerun `jet os build`.

rows.meaning: `jet os vm run` needs a proved installed disk (D-JOS-VMRUN1)
rows.what: Jetos VM run needs a proved installed disk.
rows.why: D-JOS-VMRUN1=A keeps `jet os vm run` on the same proof-before-use path as `jet os vm prove`: an interactive VM may open only the latest generation's disk after a matching guest-passed proof binds host, generation, disk, media proof, tool hashes, and assertions.
rows.fix: Run `jet os vm prove <host> --disk <disk>` first, then rerun `jet os vm run`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Run `jet os vm prove <host> --disk <disk>` first, then rerun `jet os vm run`.

rows.meaning: The GNOME desktop package is missing (D-JOS-DESKTOP1)
rows.what: The jetos GNOME desktop package is missing.
rows.why: D-JOS-DESKTOP1=A makes the default desktop profile GNOME-on-Wayland with terminal fallback, so the generation must include first-party `gdm`, `gnome-session`, and `gnome-shell` commands.
rows.fix: Declare first-party packages for `gdm`, `gnome-session`, and `gnome-shell`, or select a ratified non-GNOME desktop profile.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Declare first-party packages for `gdm`, `gnome-session`, and `gnome-shell`, or select a ratified non-GNOME desktop profile.

rows.meaning: A NixOS import failed or would overwrite output (D-JOS-NIXIMPORT1)
rows.what: Jetos could not import a NixOS configuration.
rows.why: D-JOS-NIXIMPORT1=C imports semantic NixOS, flake-parts, and Home Manager facts into JetOS source and records unsupported facts in an audit report instead of pretending conversion was complete.
rows.fix: Pass a flake/root with `jetos-import-facts.json`, rerun with `--facts-only` for an audited scan draft, or choose a fresh `--out` path when writing.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Pass a flake/root with `jetos-import-facts.json`, rerun with `--facts-only` for an audited scan draft, or choose a fresh `--out` path when writing.

rows.meaning: Real JetOS replacement proof was requested with fake/script VM tools (D-JOS-REALGUEST1)
rows.what: Jetos real VM proof needs real tools.
rows.why: D-JOS-REALGUEST1=C requires actual installed-guest behavior before JetOS can claim NixOS replacement readiness. Script fixtures and fake QEMU tools may test harness plumbing, but they cannot close replacement acceptance.
rows.fix: Rerun without `--real` for plumbing tests, or put real QEMU/image/media tools on PATH before claiming replacement proof.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Rerun without `--real` for plumbing tests, or put real QEMU/image/media tools on PATH before claiming replacement proof.

rows.meaning: A jetos real-tier system option/service/package has no NixOS mapping (D-JOS-NIXBACKEND1)
rows.what: Jetos real tier could not map every system declaration to NixOS.
rows.why: D-JOS-NIXBACKEND1=C generates a hidden NixOS backend from the checked `SystemPlan` and refuses to silently drop an option, service, or package it cannot translate — every unmapped declaration is listed together, before `nix` ever runs. A `jet os` run reports this JetOS mapping error.
rows.fix: Rename or drop the unmapped keys/packages/services, or map them to the nearest supported real-tier option (see the option/service/package mapping table for `--real`).
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Rename or drop the unmapped keys/packages/services, or map them to the nearest supported real-tier option (see the option/service/package mapping table for `--real`).

rows.meaning: Signing key generation needs cryptographic randomness (D-CRYPTO-KEYGEN-DIAG1, D-CRYPTO-KEYGEN-CODE2)
rows.what: Jet could not create the package-signing key.
rows.why: The operating system could not provide cryptographic randomness.
rows.fix: Retry as a new operation on a supported host; no key files were created.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Retry as a new operation on a supported host; no key files were created.

rows.meaning: A lint denied by `package.jet` `policy.lints.deny` fired — build failure instead of a warning (D-LINTPOLICY1, the override law)
rows.what: `` Lint `{name}` (`{code}`) is denied by policy: {what} ``
rows.why: `` {why}. This team's `policy.lints.deny` in `package.jet` turns this warning into a build failure (D-LINTPOLICY1 — the override law); it stays a warning everywhere `package.jet` doesn't opt in. The listed lint name matches. ``
rows.fix: Use the underlying lint fix ({fix}), or remove `{name}` from `policy.lints.deny` if this team no longer wants the wall.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Apply the underlying lint fix, or remove the lint from `policy.lints.deny`.

rows.meaning: `jet run <entry> -- <name>` names no `#Job fn` in the entry (D-JPK-TASKRUN1, D-JOB-SUBCMD1)
rows.what: No job named `{name}`.
rows.why: `jet run <entry> -- <name>` only invokes `#Job fn`s (D-JPK-TASKRUN1, D-JOB-SUBCMD1).
rows.fix: Mark a function `#Job`, or check the spelling; the diagnostic lists declared jobs.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Mark a function `#Job`, or check the spelling; the diagnostic lists declared jobs.

rows.meaning: `--affected-since <ref>` names a git ref that does not resolve (D-JPK-SELECTOR1)
rows.what: Git ref `{ref}` not found.
rows.why: `--affected-since` (D-JPK-SELECTOR1=C) diffs workspace member input hashes against a git baseline; that ref must resolve to a commit.
rows.fix: Pass a real branch, tag, or commit (a did-you-mean is offered when a close match exists).
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Pass a real branch, tag, or commit (a did-you-mean is offered when a close match exists).

rows.meaning: Pnpm-style `--filter` pattern DSL rejected — use `-p` / `--affected` (D-JPK-SELECTOR1)
rows.what: `{flag}` is not a Jet workspace selector.
rows.why: D-JPK-SELECTOR1=C rejects pnpm-style `--filter` pattern DSLs; Jet scopes workspace commands with exact `-p <member>` and computed `--affected` / `--affected-since <ref>` only.
rows.fix: Use `-p <member>` (repeatable) or `--affected` / `--affected-since <ref>`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use `-p <member>` (repeatable) or `--affected` / `--affected-since <ref>`.

rows.meaning: `jetpack tool install` bin name collides with a project `#Job fn` (JPK-TOOL-COLLIDE)
rows.what: `` `{bin}` is already a job in {path} ``
rows.why: JPK-TOOL-COLLIDE: `jetpack tool install` would project `{bin}` onto `~/.jet/bin`, but this project already declares `#Job fn {bin}` — the project job wins here, so the global tool would be shadowed.
rows.fix: Install under a different bin name with `jetpack tool install <ref> --as <other>`, or use `jetpack use <ref> -- <command>`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Install under a different bin name with `jetpack tool install <ref> --as <other>`, or use `jetpack use <ref> -- <command>`.

rows.meaning: `jetpack tool` ref names an external provider with no hangar realization path yet (JPK-TOOL-PROVIDER)
rows.what: `` Tool provider `{source}` isn't available yet ``
rows.why: JPK-TOOL-PROVIDER: `jetpack tool` accepts external providers (`npm`, `pypi`, `cargo`, …) so the surface is discoverable, but that provider has no hangar realization path yet — Jet never silently skips. Built-ins that work today include `nixpkgs` and `github`; local paths are bare.
rows.fix: Use a built-in ref (`name@nixpkgs`, `owner/repo@github`) or a bare local path, or wait for the `{source}` provider to land.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use a built-in provider or a local path until the requested provider is supported.

rows.meaning: Hangar Store v2 path law rejected a store path component (case-fold collision, reserved Windows name, trailing `.`/` `, absolute/dot components) (E4-JP1)
rows.what: Store path rejected: `{path}`
rows.why: Hangar Store v2 path law (E4-JP1) records POSIX byte names and rejects Windows reserved names, trailing `.`/` ` aliases, `.`/`..`, and ASCII case-fold collisions among siblings. Unicode normalization is never applied implicitly.
rows.fix: Rename the entry to a portable store path with no reserved names, no trailing `.`/` `, and no case-fold collision with a sibling.

rows.meaning: The retired `--profile` spelling selected an environment composition; presets own that word now (D-CONF-WORD1)
rows.what: `--profile` is retired
rows.why: Profile answers how hard to optimize a build. A named environment composition is a preset, so one word never answers two questions.
rows.fix: Select the composition with `--preset <name>`, declared under `presets:`.

rows.meaning: `ArgsSpec.flag` or `ParsedArgs.flag` called with wrong arity (D-ARGS1)
rows.what: `` `flag` expects 2 arguments (name, help), got N ``
rows.why: `ArgsSpec.flag(name, help)` registers a boolean flag like `--verbose`; both the flag name and a one-line help string are required.
rows.fix: Pass exactly two strings: the flag name and a help description, e.g. `.flag("verbose", "enable verbose output")`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass exactly two strings: the flag name and a help description, e.g. `.flag("verbose", "enable verbose output")`.

rows.meaning: `ArgsSpec.option` or `ParsedArgs.option` called with wrong arity (D-ARGS1)
rows.what: `` `option` expects 3 arguments (name, help, metavar), got N ``
rows.why: `ArgsSpec.option(name, help, metavar)` registers a value option like `--output FILE`; all three strings are required.
rows.fix: Pass three strings: the option name, a help description, and a placeholder like `FILE`, e.g. `.option("output", "write to FILE", "FILE")`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass three strings: the option name, a help description, and a placeholder like `FILE`, e.g. `.option("output", "write to FILE", "FILE")`.

rows.meaning: `ArgsSpec.positional` or `ParsedArgs.positional` called with wrong arity (D-ARGS1)
rows.what: `` `positional` expects 2 arguments (name, help), got N ``
rows.why: `ArgsSpec.positional(name, help)` registers a required positional argument; both name and help are required.
rows.fix: Pass exactly two strings: the positional name and a help description, e.g. `.positional("input", "file to process")`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass exactly two strings: the positional name and a help description, e.g. `.positional("input", "file to process")`.

rows.meaning: `ArgsSpec.parse` called with wrong arity (D-ARGS1)
rows.what: `` `parse` expects 1 argument (argv), got N ``
rows.why: `ArgsSpec.parse(argv)` parses a `[String]` against the spec; pass exactly the argv list.
rows.fix: Pass exactly one argument: the argv list, e.g. `spec.parse(io.args())`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass exactly one argument: the argv list, e.g. `spec.parse(io.args())`.

rows.meaning: `#CLI` struct field has a type with no CLI flag mapping (D-CLIFLAG1)
rows.what: `` Field `name` has no CLI flag mapping (Type) ``
rows.why: Only `Int` (including inline ranges), `Float`, `Bool`, `String`, `Path`, and `T?` of those map to a flag; a nested `#CLI` struct, a `Map`, a closure, or a plain `[T]` don't.
rows.fix: Change the field to a supported type, or drop it from the `#CLI` struct.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Change the field to a supported type, or drop it from the `#CLI` struct.

rows.meaning: Two `#CLI` fields derive the same flag, or a field uses reserved `--help`, `--allow`, or `--deny` (D-CLIFLAG1)
rows.what: Two `#CLI` fields derive the same flag, or a field uses a reserved flag
rows.why: Every field needs a distinct `--flag`; generated commands reserve `--help`, `--allow`, and `--deny`.
rows.fix: Rename the colliding field or choose a non-reserved flag name.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Rename the colliding field or choose a non-reserved flag name.

rows.meaning: `fn run`'s entry parameter isn't a `#CLI` program struct (D-CLI-GLOBAL1=E)
rows.what: `` `run`'s parameter isn't a CLI-derived type ``
rows.why: A typed `fn run(args: T)` entry only works when `T` is a `#CLI`-derived program struct.
rows.fix: Mark the program struct `#CLI`, or use a direct scalar-parameter `fn run` entry.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Mark the program struct `#CLI`, or use a direct scalar-parameter `fn run` entry.

rows.meaning: `#Flag` on a `#CLI` field that is already flag-only (D-CLI-POS1)
rows.what: `` `#Flag` on `name` has nothing to opt out of ``
rows.why: `#Flag` keeps a required value field flag-only (D-CLI-POS1=A). Bool fields, `T?` fields, and fields with a `{expr}` default are already flag-only.
rows.fix: Remove `#Flag`, or make the field a required scalar without a `{expr}` default.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Remove `#Flag`, or make the field a required scalar without a default.

rows.meaning: Variadic parameter not last, or variadic param has a default (D-VARIADIC1)
rows.what: A `...` rest parameter is not last, or a variadic parameter has a default value.
rows.why: A variadic parameter collects every trailing argument, so nothing may follow it; a default would contradict that job.
rows.fix: Move `name: ...T` to the end of the parameter list and remove any `{…}` default.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move `name: ...T` to the end of the parameter list and remove any `{…}` default.

rows.meaning: Spread operand is not a list (D-VARIADIC1)
rows.what: A spread operand is not a list.
rows.why: List spread `[...xs]` and call spread `f(...xs)` expand a list's elements — the operand must be `[T]`.
rows.fix: Spread a list value, or build the list without spread.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Spread a list value, or build the list without spread.

rows.meaning: Call spread at a callee without a variadic rest parameter (D-VARIADIC1)
rows.what: A call uses spread at a function with no variadic rest parameter.
rows.why: `f(...xs)` only applies when the callee's final parameter is variadic (`name: ...T`).
rows.fix: Pass arguments individually, or call a function whose last parameter is variadic.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass arguments individually, or call a function whose last parameter is variadic.

rows.meaning: Trait-bounded variadic call-site argument doesn't implement the bound trait (D-ANY-JAI1)
rows.what: `` `{arg}` doesn't implement `{Trait}` `` — a trait-bounded variadic call-site argument fails one of the bound trait(s) (D-ANY-JAI1).
rows.why: `{param}: ...{Trait}` (or `...[A, B]`) checks every argument against the bound trait(s) — that's how a function like this accepts a mix of types safely, with each argument monomorphized to its own concrete type (zero boxing).
rows.fix: Implement `{Trait}` for the argument's type, or drop the value from this call.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Implement the required trait for the argument type, or drop the value from this call.

rows.meaning: Trait-bounded variadic parameter used outside a `loop x in name { … }` loop (D-ANY-JAI1)
rows.what: `` `{name}` can only be used in a direct source loop here `` — a trait-bounded variadic parameter referenced outside its one supported shape (D-ANY-JAI1).
rows.why: A trait-bounded variadic's elements can have different concrete types, so there's no single Rust type to give the whole parameter (`.len()`, indexing, passing it on, a second loop, …) outside a loop that visits each argument once.
rows.fix: Iterate it with `loop x in {name} { … }` — that's the only supported use in v1.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Iterate the lazy value directly in the supported loop form.

rows.meaning: Hangar Store v2 ingest, reproducibility certification, or executable lease handoff aborted (source mutated during race-safe copy, unsupported special object/xattr, invalid lease service state, digest mismatch on verify, or divergent producer result) (E4-JP1, E4-JP18, D-JPK-EXECLEASE1)
rows.what: Hangar ingest, executable lease handoff, or digest verification failed
rows.why: Race-safe no-follow ingest re-stats open handles and aborts if the source mutates; the authenticated executable lease protocol rejects invalid keys, frames, owner locks, snapshots, and receipts before a child starts; verify re-hashes and compares the envelope digest; independent producer disagreement remains in `private/unreproducible/<action-key>.json` and cannot satisfy trusted cache policy.
rows.fix: Re-run realization or ingest against a stable tree; if the error names executable lease state, repair the lease service state and retry without deleting the last good Hangar object; inspect the structured reproducibility report and fix the nondeterminism.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Re-run realization or ingest against a stable tree; if the error names executable lease state, repair the lease service state and retry without deleting the last good Hangar object; inspect the structured reproducibility report and fix the nondeterminism.

rows.meaning: Ambiguous or unmatched typed package variant selection (E4-JP15, D-JPK-VARIANT1)
rows.what: Ambiguous package variants for need `{need}`: {candidates} (first distinguishing axis: {axis})
rows.why: Matching is exact-then-compatible under one total order; an ambiguous tie is never a silent pick (D-JPK-VARIANT1 / E4-JP15). Provider facts affect selection only through explicit `variant_map` entries.
rows.fix: Add a `variant_map`, pin one candidate, or make the need more specific on the named axis.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Add a `variant_map`, pin one candidate, or make the need more specific on the named axis.

rows.meaning: A direct CLI ref uses a retired provider-first order, the retired `path@` prefix, or the public `@nixpkgs` source spelling (D-JPK-REF1, D-JPK-SNIXREUSE1)
rows.what: A Jetpack CLI ref uses a retired order, path-provider prefix, or `@nixpkgs` source spelling.
rows.why: D-JPK-REF1 puts the package or upstream target before `@` and the source after it; D-JPK-SNIXREUSE1 makes Jetpack public while retaining nixpkgs as lock and receipt provenance. A `jetpack env` run reports this provider-reference error.
rows.fix: Write `target@provider`, a bare local path, or rewrite `package@nixpkgs` exactly as `package@jetpack`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Write `target@provider`, a bare local path, or rewrite `package@nixpkgs` exactly as `package@jetpack`.

rows.meaning: A `#Short` value is not one ASCII letter, or two `#CLI` fields use the same short name (D-CLI-FIELD-MARKERS1)
rows.what: `` `#Short("name")` is not a one-letter option `` or `` `#Short("n")` is used by both `first` and `second` ``
rows.why: The shared command parser treats a short option as one ASCII letter, and each spelling must select only one `#CLI` field.
rows.fix: Use one letter and give colliding fields different values.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use one letter and give colliding fields different values.

rows.meaning: `#Short` or `#Env` has no typed-CLI builder mapping at its field (D-CLI-FIELD-MARKERS1)
rows.what: `` `#Short` has no CLI mapping for field `name` ``
rows.why: `#Short` and `#Env` describe generated command inputs. They do not apply outside a `#CLI` struct; `#Env` also cannot map a presence-only `Bool` flag to the builder's value-option fallback.
rows.fix: Remove the marker, mark the command-input struct `#CLI`, or move `#Env` to a value field.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Remove the marker, mark the command-input struct `#CLI`, or move `#Env` to a value field.

rows.meaning: An external hangar root changed between reading its etag and applying a requested mutation
rows.what: An external hangar root changed between reading its etag and applying a requested mutation
rows.why: The registered jetpack rule applies here. A `jetpack hangar` run reports this external-root mutation conflict.
rows.fix: Re-read the hangar root and retry the mutation against its current etag.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Re-read the hangar root and retry the mutation against its current etag.

rows.meaning: A typed `Output` kind, payload, callable reference, callable contract, visibility, or singular selection is invalid (D-SHAPE-OUTPUT-CALLABLE1)
rows.what: The Output kind, payload, entry reference, callable contract, or singular selection is invalid
rows.why: `Output` has nine closed kinds; runnable entries are checked function references. Executables take zero or one CLI-derived parameter, Services and Checks take none, and all return `()` or `!`. A singular run without `fn run` also needs one unambiguous Executable.
rows.fix: Use a ratified kind and fields, point `entry:` at one visible safe function with the role's exact signature, or select one of the listed Executables explicitly.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use a ratified kind and fields, point `entry:` at one visible safe function with the role's exact signature, or select one of the listed Executables explicitly.

rows.meaning: Workspace/package membership escapes its root (D-ECO-MEMBERS1)
rows.what: The workspace member path escapes the workspace root
rows.why: Membership is rooted in the workspace, including the physical target behind a symlink.
rows.fix: Use a relative path below the workspace root and remove escaping symlinks.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use a relative path below the workspace root and remove escaping symlinks.

rows.meaning: A nested Package declares `members` instead of leaving membership to the workspace root; the diagnostic names the member manifest source (D-ECO-MEMBERS1)
rows.what: A member Package declares `members` (the diagnostic names its `package.jet` source)
rows.why: Membership has one level: the workspace root owns discovery, and source provenance makes the offending Package reviewable.
rows.fix: Remove the nested `members:` field from the named member manifest and declare those paths at the workspace root.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Remove the nested `members:` field from the named member manifest and declare those paths at the workspace root.

rows.meaning: Two workspace member paths resolve to the same physical directory (D-ECO-MEMBERS1)
rows.what: Two member paths resolve to one physical directory
rows.why: Two spellings cannot create two Package identities.
rows.fix: Keep one member path for the directory.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Keep one member path for the directory.

rows.meaning: Two workspace members claim the same stable package name (D-ECO-MEMBERS1)
rows.what: Two members claim the same Package name
rows.why: Stable package references need one owner.
rows.fix: Rename one Package or remove the duplicate member.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Rename one Package or remove the duplicate member.

rows.meaning: A managed environment file has an invalid destination, source, mode, permission, or content shape (D-ENV-FILES1)
rows.what: A managed environment file declaration is invalid
rows.why: Managed files are typed and plan before apply; unsafe paths or ambiguous ownership must fail closed.
rows.fix: Use a project-relative destination and a valid `source`/`content`, mode, and permission record.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use a project-relative destination and a valid `source`/`content`, mode, and permission record.

rows.meaning: An environment image references an unknown environment (D-ENV-IMAGE1)
rows.what: An environment image names an unknown environment
rows.why: An image may project only a declared environment fact graph.
rows.fix: Declare the environment or change `from:` to an existing one.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Declare the environment or change `from:` to an existing one.

rows.meaning: A typed service readiness probe has the wrong arguments or an unsafe path (D-JPK-SERVICEDEPTH1)
rows.what: A typed service readiness probe is invalid
rows.why: Probe arguments and notify paths are checked before a process can start.
rows.fix: Use the documented `exec`, `http`, `notify`, or `tcp` shape and a project-relative path.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use the documented `exec`, `http`, `notify`, or `tcp` shape and a project-relative path.

rows.meaning: A lifecycle hook is not explicitly trusted (D-ENV-LIFECYCLE2)
rows.what: A lifecycle hook is not explicitly trusted
rows.why: Hooks execute project commands during activation.
rows.fix: Set `trusted: true` after review and approve the changed environment.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Set `trusted: true` after review and approve the changed environment.

rows.meaning: Task metadata has the wrong shape or an unsafe project path (D-TASK-META1)
rows.what: Task metadata or a task path is invalid
rows.why: Task packages, cache inputs/outputs, cwd, and limits must be deterministic and project-contained.
rows.fix: Use the typed metadata shape and project-relative paths without `..`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use the typed metadata shape and project-relative paths without `..`.

rows.meaning: An environment module import escapes its project root (D-ENV-FLAKEPARTS1)
rows.what: An environment import escapes its root
rows.why: One environment graph cannot import files outside its project boundary.
rows.fix: Use a relative import directory without `..` or an escaping symlink.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use a relative import directory without `..` or an escaping symlink.

rows.meaning: One environment preset or package generation is composed with conflicting definitions (D-ENV-PROFILE1/D-JPK-PROFILE1)
rows.what: Preset or generation definitions conflict
rows.why: Composition cannot silently choose one definition's packages, variables, parents, or collision choices over another's.
rows.fix: Merge equal facts or give them different names.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Merge equal facts or give them different names.

rows.meaning: A typed environment fact, language-pack selection, dotenv declaration, or Git hook path is invalid or conflicting (D-ENV-LIFECYCLE2/D-ENV-LANGPACK1/D-ECO6)
rows.what: A typed environment fact is invalid or unusable
rows.why: Language packs use one catalog with explicit host, platform, license, and required-tool facts. Dotenv paths stay inside the project, expert allowlists make secret handling explicit, and Git hook paths stay inside the project and name an existing directory.
rows.fix: Fix the language selection/catalog fact, use a project-relative file and `Dotenv{ file, allow, secrets }` with valid variable names, or create an in-project directory for `git_hooks_path`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Fix the language selection/catalog fact, use a project-relative file and `Dotenv{ file, allow, secrets }` with valid variable names, or create an in-project directory for `git_hooks_path`.

rows.meaning: An explicit workspace member is missing or is not a Package directory (D-ECO-MEMBERS1)
rows.what: An explicit workspace member is not a Package directory
rows.why: Workspace membership names existing Package roots; a missing or manifest-free directory cannot become a stable graph node.
rows.fix: Create `package.jet`, correct the path, or use `find("./packages")`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Create `package.jet`, correct the path, or use `find("./packages")`.

rows.meaning: An environment integration, package-generation provider fact, or executable lease handoff is conflicting, lossy, or invalid (D-ENV-INTEGRATIONS1/D-JPK-PROFILE1/D-JPK-EXECLEASE1)
rows.what: An environment integration, package-generation provider fact, or executable lease handoff is conflicting, lossy, or invalid
rows.why: Integrations and package generations lower into shared typed facts; an executable child may use only a verified leased output, so a path that escapes the lease or a failed handoff cannot run. A `jetpack env` run reports this package-generation error.
rows.fix: Merge the declarations, use a supported package ref, or re-realize the package so Jetpack can hand only its verified lease to the child.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Merge the declarations, use a supported package ref, or re-realize the package so Jetpack can hand only its verified lease to the child.

rows.meaning: An environment image cannot project a service, verified package output, or extra file (D-ENV-IMAGE1)
rows.what: An environment image cannot project a service, verified package output, or extra file
rows.why: D-ENV-IMAGE1 keeps image layers tied to verified Hangar output and explicit safe project files. A service needs the typed supervisor; an absent, empty, conflicting, or wrong-platform package output, or a missing, unsafe, or secret extra file cannot be copied into an image. A `jet image` run reports this environment-image error.
rows.fix: Run the declared service through `jetpack services`, realize the environment package for the image target, or choose a regular project-relative non-secret extra file and run `jet image` again.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Run the declared service through `jetpack services`, realize the environment package for the image target, or choose a regular project-relative non-secret extra file and run `jet image` again.

rows.meaning: The requested environment module is not declared
rows.what: The requested environment module is not declared
rows.why: One environment plan activates one `env.<name>` module; silently merging siblings would mix unrelated packages and variables.
rows.fix: Select one of the declared module names, or omit `--env` to use `dev`, then `default`, then lexical order.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Select one of the declared module names, or omit `--env` to use `dev`, then `default`, then lexical order.

rows.meaning: A loadable `.jetlib` artifact's compiler-identity stamp doesn't match the running compiler — refused before mapping (D-LIB-REUSE1=B)
rows.what: This loadable library was built by Jet `{artifact_version}`, but the loading program uses Jet `{host_version}`.
rows.why: A `.jetlib` artifact pins the exact compiler identity that built it (D-LIB-REUSE1=B) — Jet makes no cross-version binary layout promise, so a mismatched artifact is refused before it is mapped, never linked with stale layout assumptions. A `jet run` run reports this library toolchain error.
rows.fix: Rebuild the library with the loading program's Jet version, or install a matching Jet toolchain.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Rebuild the library with the loading program's Jet version, or install a matching Jet toolchain.

rows.meaning: A loaded library declares an effect the load site's grant doesn't cover — refused before mapping (D-LIB-DYNTRUST1=A)
rows.what: Library `{name}` declares the `{effect}` effect, which this load site doesn't grant.
rows.why: A loadable Jet library declares its effects like any package (D-LIB-DYNTRUST1=A); the host states what it grants at the load site, and a library asking for more is refused before it is mapped. Compiler identity is verified first, so this check only runs against an artifact already proven to come from this compiler.
rows.fix: Widen the grant at the load site to include `{effect}`, or remove the effect from the library.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Widen the load-site grant to include the library effect, or remove that effect.

rows.meaning: A Jetpack command failed and no more specific registered code owns the failure
rows.what: {problem}
rows.why: Jetpack could not complete the command because the named input, project fact, tool, or operating-system operation did not satisfy it. A `jetpack env` run reports this Jetpack operation error.
rows.fix: Correct the named problem, then run the command again.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Correct the named problem, then run the command again.

rows.meaning: A selected `Library` output or loadable artifact requests an invalid target, binding, ABI, or export shape (D-LIB-EXPORT1=C, D-EMBED1=E)
rows.what: This `Library` output or loadable artifact requests an invalid target, binding, ABI, or export shape.
rows.why: D-LIB-EXPORT1=C and D-EMBED1=E use closed, checked native projections: a Library emits only the checked static/shared, C-header, and named binding surfaces, and a loadable artifact must carry the exact native target, ABI, and top-level `pub fn` export table. Unknown combinations cannot be guessed safely. A `jet build` run reports this library artifact error.
rows.fix: Select the Library output directly, use `c`, `python`, or `swift`, and give native bindings `native: true`; for a loadable artifact, rebuild it with the matching compiler and export surface.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Select the Library output directly, use `c`, `python`, or `swift`, and give native bindings `native: true`; for a loadable artifact, rebuild it with the matching compiler and export surface.

rows.meaning: The retired `--env-profile` spelling selected an environment module; `--env` owns that axis now (D-ENVFLAG1)
rows.what: `--env-profile` is retired
rows.why: `--env` selects one `env.<name>` module; `--preset` selects a named composition, so one flag never answers two questions.
rows.fix: Select the module with `--env <name>`.

rows.meaning: The retired audited-effect boolean changed gate policy semantics (D-ONCE-GATE1=A)
rows.what: The retired audited-effect boolean is not accepted.
rows.why: Audited escapes share one policy ladder, so a boolean cannot express which gate is being authorized or which organization policy may refuse it.
rows.fix: Use `--gate impure=allow`.

rows.meaning: CLI command name collides with another command or root flag (D-CLI-GLOBAL1=E)
rows.what: CLI command `{command}` collides with another command or root flag
rows.why: A program struct has one command namespace and one root flag namespace; a word cannot name both.
rows.fix: Rename the command or root field so every command word is unique
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Rename the command or root field so every command word is unique

rows.meaning: CLI command member has no callable shape (D-CLI-GLOBAL1=E)
rows.what: CLI command member `{name}` has no callable shape
rows.why: A CLI callable member needs a same-module target when bound, at most one first read-only program-struct parameter, and scalar remaining parameters.
rows.fix: Bind a visible scalar-parameter function, or use a method on the program struct
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Bind a visible scalar-parameter function, or use a method on the program struct

rows.meaning: Callable CLI members are declared on a Codable struct (D-CLI-GLOBAL1=E)
rows.what: Callable CLI members cannot be declared on a Codable struct
rows.why: CLI commands are behavior; Codable structs contain only serializable data fields.
rows.fix: Split the command program struct from the Codable data struct
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Split the command program struct from the Codable data struct

rows.meaning: CLI method receiver is writable (D-CLI-GLOBAL1=E)
rows.what: A CLI method receiver must be read-only
rows.why: Shared root flags are parsed into one program value and command dispatch must not mutate that value.
rows.fix: Change the receiver to read-only `self`
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Change the receiver to read-only `self`

rows.meaning: Signed nixpkgs index proof was rejected (D-JPK-NIXINDEX1)
rows.what: The signed nixpkgs index could not be trusted.
rows.why: The manifest, target, signature, or canonical record failed verification, so Jetpack refused to select or substitute the package. A `jetpack env` run reports this environment-provider error.
rows.fix: Refresh the signed index or use a covered locked nixpkgs input.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Refresh the signed index or use a covered locked nixpkgs input.

rows.meaning: Requested nixpkgs attr is outside signed index coverage (D-JPK-NIXINDEX1)
rows.what: The requested nixpkgs attr is not covered by the signed index.
rows.why: The signed index records only the published nixpkgs channel, revision, system, and attrs it can prove; this attr is in its explicit not-indexed coverage. A `jetpack env` run reports this environment-provider error.
rows.fix: Use a covered attr or a supported native provider, or resolve the input through an explicit compatibility path.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use a covered attr or a supported native provider, or resolve the input through an explicit compatibility path.

rows.meaning: Native Nix cache admission failed during {kind} (D-JPK-NIXCACHE1)
rows.what: Native Nix cache admission failed during {kind}.
rows.why: The signed Nix cache closure was not admitted because its {kind} check failed.
rows.fix: Repair the cache metadata or network response, then retry the admission.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Repair the cache metadata or network response, then retry the admission.

rows.meaning: Nix closure execution is unavailable on this host.
rows.what: Nix closure execution is unavailable on this host.
rows.why: Jetpack could not create the isolated /nix/store projection: {reason}. A `jetpack env` run reports this environment-provider error.
rows.fix: Use a Linux host with unprivileged user and mount namespaces, or choose a native provider for this package.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use a Linux host with unprivileged user and mount namespaces, or choose a native provider for this package.

rows.meaning: An explicitly updated source is pinned and cannot move (D-CHANNEL-AUTO1)
rows.what: Source `{name}` is pinned and cannot be updated.
rows.why: D-CHANNEL-AUTO1 keeps a declaration with no channel marker pinned forever; an update command must not move its lock or rewrite its manifest.
rows.fix: Declare `{name}` with `#latest` for manual movement or `#auto` for automatic movement.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Declare the source with `#latest` or `#auto` according to the desired update policy.

rows.meaning: A retired Jetpack shell spelling was used
rows.what: {what}
rows.why: The current shell verbs are `env` for a project environment and `use` for exactly named packages; materialization is `--prep`.
rows.fix: {fix}

rows.meaning: A retired Jetpack store spelling was used
rows.what: {what}
rows.why: Store commands are grouped under `hangar`; project commands stay at the top level.
rows.fix: {fix}

rows.meaning: A Jet command needing a declared project environment was run outside it
rows.what: This project declares {environment}; `{command}` is not running inside its verified environment.
rows.why: Jetpack preparation is disabled for this command. `jet run` delegates the declared environment unless `--no-prepare` is supplied; other verbs must be invoked through the existing Jetpack environment boundary.
rows.fix: For `jet run`, remove `--no-prepare` and retry `{command}`; for another verb, run `jetpack env -- {command}`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|For `jet run`, remove `--no-prepare` and retry `{command}`; for another verb, run `jetpack env -- {command}`.

rows.meaning: Jet could not delegate project environment preparation
rows.what: The declared project environment could not be prepared for `{command}`: {reason}.
rows.why: Jet delegates project environment resolution and realization to the matching Jetpack engine before `{command}` runs; this delegation failed before the program started. A `jet run` run reports this environment-delegation error.
rows.fix: Resolve the Jetpack installation or environment problem, then retry `{command}`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Resolve the Jetpack installation or environment problem, then retry `{command}`.

rows.meaning: An inline `package { … }` declaration is not first (D-ECO-INLINEPACKAGE1)
rows.what: An inline `package { … }` declaration must be the first top-level declaration.
rows.why: The contextual package carrier owns the file's Package facts and must be established before ordinary Jet items.
rows.fix: Move the `package { … }` block before every other top-level declaration.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Move the `package { … }` block before every other top-level declaration.

rows.meaning: An inline `package { … }` declaration appears more than once (D-ECO-INLINEPACKAGE1)
rows.what: An inline `package { … }` declaration appears more than once.
rows.why: One source file has one Package identity; accepting a second block would make facts, outputs, and authority ambiguous.
rows.fix: Keep one leading `package { … }` block and remove the duplicate.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Keep one leading `package { … }` block and remove the duplicate.

rows.meaning: An inline `package { … }` declaration is malformed or unbalanced (D-ECO-INLINEPACKAGE1)
rows.what: The inline `package { … }` declaration is malformed or missing its closing brace.
rows.why: The contextual carrier must have one balanced block before its body can be passed to the canonical Package parser.
rows.fix: Close the block and fix its structure, then let the Package field diagnostic identify any invalid field.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Close the block and fix its structure, then let the Package field diagnostic identify any invalid field.

rows.meaning: An inline Package conflicts with `package.jet` (D-ECO-INLINEPACKAGE1)
rows.what: This source declares inline Package facts while `package.jet` also exists.
rows.why: D-ECO-INLINEPACKAGE1 allows one Package context per project; choosing between two identities would make builds, dependencies, outputs, and authority nondeterministic.
rows.fix: Remove the inline block or remove `package.jet`, then keep the remaining Package declaration canonical.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Remove the inline block or remove `package.jet`, then keep the remaining Package declaration canonical.

rows.meaning: Compiler-extension host failure (load/analyze/validate fail-closed, D-DX5-HOOK1)
rows.what: `` Compiler-extension failed: {message} ``
rows.why: The configured compiler-extension component could not complete `analyze`, or returned an invalid response (D-DX5-HOOK1). Guests are sandboxed; failures stay Jet-owned (I2).
rows.fix: Fix the component, or unset `JET_COMPILER_EXTENSION` to skip the extension.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Fix the component, or unset `JET_COMPILER_EXTENSION` to skip the extension.

rows.meaning: Source nesting exceeds the shared parser, sema, and TIR evaluator limit of 256 (D-COMPILE-STACK1=A)
rows.what: `` This code nests {depth} levels deep; the limit is 256 ``
rows.why: Each nested source form needs one compiler checking frame, and unbounded depth could overflow the compiler stack. The parser, sema, and TIR evaluator enforce the same published limit (D-COMPILE-STACK1=A). During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: Pull inner parts out into named bindings or helper functions.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Pull inner parts out into named bindings or helper functions.

rows.meaning: Devtools publication needs explicit field/value labels
rows.what: this published value has no gate
rows.why: a published value must name itself with both `field:` and `value:` labels
rows.fix: write `devtools.publish(field: .<state_field>, value: <expr>)`
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|write `devtools.publish(field: .<state_field>, value: <expr>)`

rows.meaning: Devtools panel identity is registered more than once
rows.what: devtools panel `{identity}` is registered twice
rows.why: one package/module/function identity may describe only one panel (first at {first})
rows.fix: keep one marked public `panel` function for this package
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|keep one marked public `panel` function for this package

rows.meaning: Devtools panel declaration does not satisfy its typed panel contract
rows.what: devtools panel `{panel}` is invalid
rows.why: a devtools panel must match the public `panel(state: State) UiNode` contract
rows.fix: write one valid `#DevPanel` function with the required signature and state
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|write one valid `#DevPanel` function with the required signature and state

rows.meaning: Devtools publication names no panel state field
rows.what: devtools publication names unknown state field `{field}`
rows.why: package `{package}` module `{module}` has no marked panel `{panel}` field with that name
rows.fix: write `field: .{field}` using a field from the package's marked `panel` state
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Publish a panel-state value using one of the package panel fields.

rows.meaning: Devtools publication value type differs from its panel state field
rows.what: published value for `{package}::{module}::{panel}::{field}` has type `{actual}`
rows.why: the panel state field has type `{expected}`
rows.fix: publish a value with type `{expected}` or change the state field
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Publish a value of the declared state-field type, or change that field type.

rows.meaning: Devtools panel state field has no publication
rows.what: devtools panel `{panel}` state field `{field}` has no publication
rows.why: every panel state field must have a checked `core.devtools.publish` site
rows.fix: publish `field: .{field}` with the field's declared type
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Publish the panel field with its declared type.

rows.meaning: Per-input fuel cap hit — snippet ran more than ~10M interpreter steps
rows.what: This snippet ran more than `{N}` interpreter steps without finishing.
rows.why: The REPL interpreter caps each input to avoid hanging your session; this almost always means a loop that never ends. A `jet repl` run reports this interpreter limitation.
rows.fix: Check any loops for a condition that never becomes false. Use `:run` to allow unbounded execution (compiles and runs instead of interpreting).
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Check any loops for a condition that never becomes false. Use `:run` to allow unbounded execution (compiles and runs instead of interpreting).

rows.meaning: Hard-rejected feature in the REPL (FFI, tasks, `#Unsafe`, OS-level APIs)
rows.what: The REPL interpreter can't run `{feature}`.
rows.why: The REPL is an interpreter for learning Jet; some features — FFI, tasks/channels, `#Unsafe`, and OS-level APIs — require the real compiler. A `jet repl` run reports this interpreter limitation.
rows.fix: Run `jet run <file.jet>` or `jet build <file.jet>` to use the full compiler.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Run `jet run <file.jet>` or `jet build <file.jet>` to use the full compiler.

rows.meaning: Application authority is undecided or denies a required effect
rows.what: Application authority is undecided or denies a required effect; the report names `required_effects`, `granted_effects`, `denied_effects`, and `authority` separately.
rows.why: The effect projection distinguishes sema requirements from policy grants, denials, and the policy identity; execution stops before host state changes.
rows.fix: Add `allow: [IO, Mem.Alloc, Exec]` under `authority.holds` in `package.jet` (use every value in this report's `undecided_effects` list); otherwise deny effects deliberately, or approve the exact operation once or for the project in an interactive terminal.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Add `allow: [IO, Mem.Alloc, Exec]` under `authority.holds` in `package.jet` (use every value in this report's `undecided_effects` list); otherwise deny effects deliberately, or approve the exact operation once or for the project in an interactive terminal.

rows.meaning: `package.jet` requests an edition this toolchain can't provide (E2-M2, D-REL3)
rows.what: This package needs a newer Jet.
rows.why: Editions opt a project into a specific era of Jet syntax. A newer edition can use syntax this compiler does not understand.
rows.fix: Upgrade with `jet self upgrade`, or set `edition: "2026"` in `package.jet`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Upgrade with `jet self upgrade`, or set `edition: "2026"` in `package.jet`.

rows.meaning: A deprecated item is used past its migration window (E2-M2, D-REL5)
rows.what: A deprecated item was used past its migration window.
rows.why: The item was deprecated in an earlier edition and no longer exists in this one; it has reached the end of its migration window.
rows.fix: use the named replacement, or run `jet fix` to migrate automatically.
rows.structured_fix: source_edit|behavior-preserving

rows.meaning: Unknown or moved command spelling, with the canonical grouped spelling (E2-M3, D-DX, D-CLI-SURFACE1, D-CLI-SURFACE2)
rows.what: Unknown or retired CLI route. Moved bare form: `` `{cmd}` moved under `jet {group}` ``. Invalid nested form: `` `{action}` isn't a jet {group} command ``.
rows.why: Moved bare form: `infrequent commands live in a named area so daily Jet commands stay easy to scan`. Invalid nested form: `jet {group} accepts only commands in its named area`.
rows.fix: Moved bare form: ``run `jet {group} {cmd} {args}` ``. Invalid nested form: ``run `jet {group} help` ``. Human output renders these as Error/Why/Fix lines; JSON uses these exact message, why, and fix strings with control characters, quotes, and backslashes escaped.

rows.meaning: Unknown or ambiguous flag on the command line, with a suggestion (E2-M3, D-DX)
rows.what: `{flag}` isn't a flag jet understands.
rows.why: Jet ignores no flags silently, so a typo can't quietly change a build.
rows.fix: Did you mean `{closest}`? Run `jet help` to see the flags.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use the suggested flag spelling or run `jet help` to select a supported flag.

rows.meaning: External completion could not read a verified JetCommandSchema record (D-SHAPE-CLI-CARRIER1, D-SHAPE-CLI-COMPLETE1)
rows.what: Couldn't read command metadata from `{program}`.
rows.why: The path has no safe command basename, contains a control character, could not be opened once as a regular file, exceeded the 512 MiB bounded read, is not ELF/PE/Mach-O/Wasm, or its JetCommandSchema record is missing, malformed, duplicated, unsupported, nested inside another universal Mach-O container, or inconsistent across universal Mach-O slices. Completion discovery never executes the program and never accepts unverified metadata. A `jet self completions` run reports this completion-metadata error.
rows.fix: Run `jet self completions` again after rebuilding `{program}` with this Jet toolchain.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Rebuild the program with this Jet toolchain, then try again. Exits 1 (user error), not 2.

rows.meaning: A command has missing, malformed, or conflicting input
rows.what: `{problem}`
rows.why: Jet needs valid command input before it can run this command.
rows.fix: Correct the named argument or input, then run the command again.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Correct the named argument or input, then run the command again.

rows.meaning: A driver file, tool, or operating-system operation failed
rows.what: `{problem}`
rows.why: Jet could not complete the named file, tool, or operating-system operation.
rows.fix: Correct the named problem, then run the command again.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Correct the named problem, then run the command again.

rows.meaning: Unknown syntax token with a nearest registered spelling
rows.what: `{token}` is not registered Jet syntax.
rows.why: syntax.rs is the one registry for user-typeable keywords, markers, operators, and sigils.
rows.fix: Did you mean `{closest}`? Run `jet explain {closest}`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use the suggested syntax spelling or run `jet explain` for the registered form.

rows.meaning: Automatic GC or its trace failed safely (D-OPTGC1, cards #658/#659)
rows.what: Automatic memory management failed, or its trace cannot be reported.
rows.why: The private collector rejected an unsafe or impossible operation, or the trace is missing, unsafe to read, larger than 4 MiB, malformed, incompatible, stale, or incomplete. Reports never estimate promotions omitted by a bounded trace.
rows.fix: check the trace path and retry with a smaller workload; for reports, run `jet run --gc-trace <file.jet>` before `jet gc report`. Exits 1 (user error).
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|check the trace path and retry with a smaller workload; for reports, run `jet run --gc-trace <file.jet>` before `jet gc report`. Exits 1 (user error).

rows.meaning: Collector-owned graph escapes into an ownership-only function (D-OPTGC1, card #658)
rows.what: A collector-owned graph cannot leave its scoped GC policy here.
rows.why: The callee returns hidden traced storage, but the receiving function is governed by ordinary ownership.
rows.fix: add `#Policy(gc)` to the receiving function or convert the graph to ordinary ownership before the boundary.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|add `#Policy(gc)` to the receiving function or convert the graph to ordinary ownership before the boundary.

rows.meaning: The cross-run memory witness ledger is missing, unsafe, oversized, malformed, or incompatible (card #1895)
rows.what: Memory ledger cannot be used: {detail}.
rows.why: `jet audit memory` and `jet fix memory` read one bounded, append-only ledger of exercised GC and unsafe-sentry witnesses; they reject missing or unsafe evidence instead of guessing.
rows.fix: Run the relevant workload once to create the ledger, or repair the configured `.jet/memory/ledger-v1.jsonl` path, then retry.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Run the relevant workload once to create the ledger, or repair the configured `.jet/memory/ledger-v1.jsonl` path, then retry.

rows.meaning: `jet dev` can't interpret a feature (task/FFI/`#Unsafe`/native std); names it and `jet build`/`jet run` (E2-M4, D-DEV1)
rows.what: `jet dev` can't interpret this program yet — it uses a feature the dev interpreter doesn't cover (a task/channel, `extern rust`/C FFI, an `#Unsafe`/`core.mem` region, or a native-only core module like files/clock/random/environment/process).
rows.why: The dev interpreter runs a deterministic, pure-enough subset for instant feedback; features that touch threads, foreign code, raw memory, or the outside world need the real native build.
rows.fix: Run `jet build` then the binary, or `jet run <file>` to compile and run it; `jet dev` keeps showing checks live. Opt in with `jet dev <file> --try-anyway` to attempt execution past the boundary, with no guarantees (D-DEV1).
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Run `jet build` then the binary, or `jet run <file>` to compile and run it; `jet dev` keeps showing checks live. Opt in with `jet dev <file> --try-anyway` to attempt execution past the boundary, with no guarantees (D-DEV1).

rows.meaning: `jet dev` interpreter step budget exhausted — likely an unbounded loop (E2-M4)
rows.what: A program ran too long for `jet dev` to keep interpreting (the step budget was exhausted).
rows.why: `jet dev` interprets your program; a run that never finishes is almost always a loop whose condition never becomes false.
rows.fix: check the loop near the pointed-at line for a condition that never ends; `jet run` executes the real build with no step limit.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|check the loop near the pointed-at line for a condition that never ends; `jet run` executes the real build with no step limit.

rows.meaning: An interpreter-only debug session can't step through a feature outside its safe boundary; the native `jet debug` CLI routes these programs to LLDB (D-DBG3)
rows.what: `jet debug` can't step through this program yet — it uses a feature outside the safe interpreter boundary (a task/channel, `extern rust`/C FFI, an `#Unsafe`/`core.mem` region, or a native-only core module such as files/clock/random/environment/process).
rows.why: The interpreter debugger cannot model threads, foreign code, raw memory, or host state. The native `jet debug` CLI normally selects the LLDB backend for this program.
rows.fix: use the native `jet debug <file>` path with LLDB installed, or use `jet run <file>` when native debugging is unavailable.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|use the native `jet debug <file>` path with LLDB installed, or use `jet run <file>` when native debugging is unavailable.

rows.meaning: `jet debug` session ended early — the user typed `quit` at the `(jet)` prompt before the program finished (D-DBG3)
rows.what: The `jet debug` session ended before the program finished — you typed `quit` at the `(jet)` prompt.
rows.why: Quitting the debugger stops the interpreted run; the program did not run to completion.
rows.fix: Run `jet debug <file>` again and use `continue` (or `c`) to run to the end, or `jet run <file>` to run it without the debugger.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Run `jet debug <file>` again and use `continue` (or `c`) to run to the end, or `jet run <file>` to run it without the debugger.

rows.meaning: A `jet dev` edit changed a type surface, so the dev loop restarts instead of swapping (c77, D-HOTSWAP1)
rows.what: This edit changed a type, so `jet dev` is restarting instead of swapping (the message names what changed — a struct field, an enum variant, or a function signature).
rows.why: A hot swap re-applies code while the program's types stay the same; changing the shape of your data means the running code is rebuilt cleanly from the new types.
rows.fix: Nothing to fix — `jet dev` restarted with the new types; this note just explains why the swap became a restart. Type-stable edits (function bodies, statements) swap without a restart.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Nothing to fix — `jet dev` restarted with the new types; this note just explains why the swap became a restart. Type-stable edits (function bodies, statements) swap without a restart.

rows.meaning: *Retired by D-LENS-RUN2=A / #778* (was: resident Cranelift gap hard-stopped `jet run`; gaps now silent-deopt to the canonical interpreter; use `--trace-tiers`)
rows.what: *Retired by D-LENS-RUN2=A / #778* — was: Jet JIT has a compiler gap for this checked program.
rows.why: Coverage gaps no longer hard-stop `jet run`; the function deopts to the canonical interpreter.
rows.fix: use `jet run --trace-tiers` to see per-function tier, reason, and timing.

rows.meaning: *Retired for raw references by D-MEM1/S3* (raw-reference return spelling `-> &T` remains absent; invalid named-view returns use E2305/E2307)
rows.what: *Retired for raw references by D-MEM1/S3* (raw-reference return spelling `-> &T` remains absent; invalid named-view returns use E2305/E2307)
rows.why: The registered sema rule applies here
rows.fix: Follow the guidance for E2301

rows.meaning: *Retired for raw references by D-MEM1/S3* (raw-reference field spelling `&T`/`#Ref` remains absent; named view fields follow D-MEM-VIEWRET1)
rows.what: *Retired for raw references by D-MEM1/S3* (raw-reference field spelling `&T`/`#Ref` remains absent; named view fields follow D-MEM-VIEWRET1)
rows.why: The registered sema rule applies here
rows.fix: Follow the guidance for E2302

rows.meaning: A `View<T>` crosses a task/channel boundary (E2-M5; emitted as E1102)
rows.what: A `View<T>` (or a string view) crosses a `tasks.spawn` or `Sender.send` boundary.
rows.why: A view points into something another scope owns; a task or channel moves owned data between threads, so a view can't cross without ownership. Reported as **E1102** (the unsendable-value rule), not separately, so one situation gives one error.
rows.fix: Send plain owned data, or rebuild the value as an owned copy (`~x`) before crossing.
