rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Send plain owned data, or rebuild the value as an owned copy (`~x`) before crossing.

rows.meaning: *Retired for raw references by D-MEM1/S3* (named slice-view returns follow D-MEM-VIEWRET1 and use E2305 when invalid)
rows.what: *Retired for raw references by D-MEM1/S3* (named slice-view returns follow D-MEM-VIEWRET1 and use E2305 when invalid)
rows.why: The registered sema rule applies here
rows.fix: Follow the guidance for E2304

rows.meaning: A declared `View<T>` would outlive its owner, or the compiler cannot infer, prove, and stabilize its public owner provenance (D-MEM-VIEWRET1/D-MEM-COPYSEM1)
rows.what: A declared `View<T>` would outlive an owner, or sema cannot stabilize a public owner set for each declared view slot. Read-only views entering non-view owning slots materialize by default; `copies: .Explicit` restores the refusal.
rows.why: Each declared view slot keeps a bounded set of possible receiver, parameter, or static sources through every return path, call, generic instantiation, aggregate projection, function value, lambda, and trait implementation. Every possible owner must stay live.
rows.fix: Keep every possible owner alive, preserve the declared view boundary, or remove `copies: .Explicit` / write `~view` when an owning destination is intended.

rows.meaning: The delegation target `{field}` doesn't implement `{trait}`, or the type has no field named `{field}`.
rows.what: The delegation target `{field}` doesn't implement `{trait}`, or the type has no field named `{field}`.
rows.why: `impl Type.Trait using field` forwards every `Trait` method to the `field` field; if that field's type hasn't implemented `Trait`, there's nothing to forward to.
rows.fix: Implement `impl FieldType.Trait` on the field's type, or choose a different field that does implement `Trait`. If the field doesn't exist, add `{field}: FieldType` to the struct.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Implement the trait on the delegation target or choose a field that already implements it.

rows.meaning: Fallible call cannot convert `{err}` into `Err` — no declared conversion exists
rows.what: A fallible call cannot convert `{err}` into `Err` — no declared conversion exists
rows.why: A fallible call uses the declared conversion rail; `{err}` can reach `Err` only through `impl {err} -> Err`.
rows.fix: Add `impl {err} -> Err { … }` before this function, or change the enclosing return type to `T !{err}`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Declare an error conversion into `Err`, or change the enclosing fallible return type.

rows.meaning: Field-pun name `{name}` is not in scope (or is not a field of `{type}`).
rows.what: Field-pun name `{name}` is not in scope (or is not a field of `{type}`).
rows.why: `Type { name }` is shorthand for `Type { name: name }` — it reads the local variable `name` and assigns it to the field of the same name. If no such local exists, or if `Type` has no field by that name, the shorthand is ambiguous.
rows.fix: Introduce a local `name :: …;` before the struct literal, or write the long form `Type { field_name: value }`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Introduce a local `name :: …;` before the struct literal, or write the long form `Type { field_name: value }`.

rows.meaning: `?` can't turn the `{Source}` from `{callee}` into `{Target}` here
rows.what: `?` can't turn the `{Source}` from `{callee}` into `{Target}` here
rows.why: `{callee}` is defined at `{definition}` with effective failure contract `{contract}`; the caller's `{caller}` contract has no route from `{Source}` to `{Target}`
rows.fix: Declare the caller with `{Source}` as its failure domain, or add `impl {Source} -> {Target} { … }`; otherwise handle `{callee}` locally with `??`

rows.meaning: `#Rename(...)` needs a string literal.
rows.what: `#Rename(...)` needs a string literal.
rows.why: The wire key a `#Codable` field maps to is a constant string (D-SERDE5); a number or expression has no place on the wire.
rows.fix: Pass one quoted string — `#Rename("wire_name")`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass one quoted string — `#Rename("wire_name")`.

rows.meaning: `#Flatten` on `{field}` needs a struct-typed field.
rows.what: `#Flatten` on `{field}` needs a struct-typed field.
rows.why: Flatten splices another struct's keys into this object (D-SERDE5), so the field must itself be a `#Codable` struct — not a primitive, list, or map.
rows.fix: Give `{field}` a `#Codable` struct type, or drop `#Flatten`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Give the field a `#Codable` struct type, or remove `#Flatten`.

rows.meaning: `#RenameAll({style})` isn't a known casing style.
rows.what: `#RenameAll({style})` isn't a known casing style.
rows.why: The wire-casing menu is the closed typed set `camel`/`snake`/`pascal`/`kebab`/`screaming` (D-SERDE3); anything else is rejected so a typo fails at compile time, not on the wire.
rows.fix: Pick one of `camel` / `snake` / `pascal` / `kebab` / `screaming`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pick one of `camel` / `snake` / `pascal` / `kebab` / `screaming`.

rows.meaning: `E2410: missing required field `{field}`` (runtime `FieldError`).
rows.what: `E2410: missing required field `{field}`` (runtime `FieldError`).
rows.why: Decoding into a `#Codable`/`#Decode` type found no wire value for a required field and the field has no declaration default (`T{{expr}}`) and isn't optional (D-SERDE5, D-DEFAULT-SHAPE1=B).
rows.fix: Mark the field optional (`T?`), give it a declaration default (`field: T{{expr}}`), or fix the input so the key is present. Compose with `??` to supply a fallback.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Mark the field optional, give it a compile-time default, or provide the missing input key.

rows.meaning: `{Type}` can't be serialized / decoded, or a union member has no compiler-known wire shape.
rows.what: `{Type}` can't be serialized / decoded, or a union member has no compiler-known wire shape.
rows.why: Only a structurally qualifying type gets a compiler-generated codec (by default or through `#Codable`/`#Encode`/`#Decode`), unless it supplies a hand-written codec. Anonymous-union decoding also needs each member's outer wire shape; a custom or imported decoder does not declare one (D-SERDE1, D-UNIONTYPE1).
rows.fix: add a compiler-derived codec, use a configured tagged enum or `#CodableAsBase` distinct type for a union member, or remove the unsupported type from the encoded value (for example, with `#Skip`).
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|add a compiler-derived codec, use a configured tagged enum or `#CodableAsBase` distinct type for a union member, or remove the unsupported type from the encoded value (for example, with `#Skip`).

rows.what: `E2412: unknown field `{field}`` (runtime `FieldError`).
rows.why: The struct is marked `#DenyUnknownFields` (D-SERDE8) and the input carried a key the struct doesn't declare, so decoding fails instead of silently dropping it.
rows.fix: remove `#DenyUnknownFields` to ignore extra keys (the lenient default), add the field, or fix the producer.

rows.meaning: A field's `{…}` default must be a compile-time constant.
rows.what: A field's `{…}` default must be a compile-time constant.
rows.why: A decode/CLI/construction default fills a missing field, so it is baked into the program and its value has to be known at compile time (D-SERDE5, D-DEFAULT-SHAPE1=B). An expression that can only be computed at runtime has no fixed value to bake, and every tier must agree (I9). During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: use a literal or a `comptime`-evaluable expression, e.g. `port: Int{8080}`, `env: String{"prod"}`, or `ports: [Int]{[80, 443]}`.

rows.what: Union `{Union}` can't be decoded — `{A}` and `{B}` share wire shape `{shape}`.
rows.why: Anonymous-union decode (D-UNIONTYPE1=A) picks a member by primary wire shape; two members with the same shape would force an arbitrary declaration order.

rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use a named enum with an explicit tag, or change the members so each has a distinct wire shape.

rows.why: Runtime config decoding uses the shared `__jet_Decode` codec, so a bad value, missing field, or unknown field is reported at its typed path while secret values stay redacted (D-CONFIG-ENV1).

rows.why: Error conversions must form an acyclic route so a failure has one finite meaning.

rows.meaning: `Never` cannot be used in a value position.
rows.what: `Never` cannot be used in a value position.
rows.why: `Never` has no values; only a function return slot or function-type return slot may promise it (D-NEVER2=B).
rows.fix: Move `Never` to a function return type, or use `()`/another value type.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move `Never` to a function return type, or use `()`/another value type.

rows.meaning: Function `{function}` promises `Never` but can reach the end.
rows.what: Function `{function}` promises `Never` but can reach the end.
rows.why: A declared `Never` return means every path must stop; this path falls through instead (D-NEVER2=B).
rows.fix: End every path with `panic`, a `Never` call, or another diverging operation, or remove `Never`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|End every path with `panic`, a `Never` call, or another diverging operation, or remove `Never`.

rows.meaning: Function `{function}` promises `Never` but uses a bare `return`.
rows.what: Function `{function}` promises `Never` but uses a bare `return`.
rows.why: A declared `Never` return cannot complete with an empty return; every path must diverge (D-NEVER2=B).
rows.fix: Remove the bare `return`, or make this function return a value type.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Remove the bare `return`, or make this function return a value type.

rows.meaning: Function `{function}` promises `Never` but returns a value.
rows.what: Function `{function}` promises `Never` but returns a value.
rows.why: A declared `Never` return has no success value (D-NEVER2=B).
rows.fix: Remove the value and diverge, or change the return type.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Remove the value and diverge, or change the return type.

rows.meaning: Function value does not satisfy `fn() Never`.
rows.what: Function value does not satisfy `fn() Never`.
rows.why: `fn() Never` promises the callable never completes, so a returning function has the wrong contract (D-NEVER2=B).
rows.fix: Pass a function declared `Never`, or change the expected function type.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass a function declared `Never`, or change the expected function type.

rows.meaning: A live query key is already registered with a different dependency footprint (D-WEBQUERY1)
rows.what: Query key `{key}` already uses footprint `{registered}`; requested `{requested}`
rows.why: An explicit key is the sole cache identity. Registering it with a second footprint would make invalidation ambiguous and split one logical query into multiple cache entries.
rows.fix: Use the existing footprint for `{key}`, or choose a new key for the new dependency declaration.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Use one dependency footprint per query key, or choose a new key.

rows.meaning: A form action does not accept the form's derived input type (D-WEBFORM1)
rows.what: Form action `{action}` does not accept `{form}`
rows.why: The form derives its fields from `{form}` and the one server-function action boundary must receive that exact input type.
rows.fix: Change `{action}` to accept `{form}` as its first parameter.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Change the action's first parameter to `{form}`.

rows.meaning: A typed table column names a row field that does not exist (D-WEBTABLE1)
rows.what: Table column `{column}` is not a field on `{row}`
rows.why: A typed table uses one row schema for sorting, filtering, and every renderer.
rows.fix: Rename the literal column name to an existing field on `{row}`, or declare `{column}` on the row struct.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Rename the literal column name to an existing row field, or declare that field on the row struct.

rows.meaning: `{method}` is not available on a {direction} file handle.
rows.what: `{method}` is not available on a {direction} file handle.
rows.why: `files.open` returns a read-only handle; `files.create`/`files.append` return a write-only handle. Calling a write method on a reader (or a read method on a writer) is a type error.
rows.fix: use the correct handle type for the operation: `files.open` to read, `files.create`/`files.append` to write.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use the correct handle type for the operation: `files.open` to read, `files.create`/`files.append` to write.

rows.meaning: A line stream can only be used directly in a loop.
rows.what: A line stream can only be used directly in a loop.
rows.why: `.lines()` hands back a lazy line reader meant to be iterated in place; storing it in a name would let it leave the loop, where it has no use. (The boundary is enforced in sema so codegen never has to lower a stray line stream — c109/I3.)
rows.fix: Iterate it directly: `loop line in handle.lines() { … }`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Iterate it directly: `loop line in handle.lines() { … }`.

rows.meaning: `.ReduceOp` is not a reduce operation, or a retired `#Op` spelling was used.
rows.what: `.ReduceOp` is not a reduce operation, or a retired `#Op` spelling was used.
rows.why: SIMD reduction takes one typed `ReduceOp` value: `.Add`, `.Mul`, `.Min`, `.Max`, or `.Avg`.
rows.fix: Pass a listed dot value, or use `v.sum()` / `v.product()` / `v.min()` / `v.max()`.

rows.meaning: Operator `{op}` isn't defined between `{lhs}` and `{rhs}`.
rows.what: Operator `{op}` isn't defined between `{lhs}` and `{rhs}`.
rows.why: Built-in lane and linalg operators keep fixed shapes: one lane/vector type on both sides, or a matrix and its matching vector; any other pair needs an operator hook.
rows.fix: Match the operand types (`T.splat(x)` lifts a scalar into every lane), call a named method like `.dot()`/`.matmul()`, or implement the operator's hook trait on your own type for this pair.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Match the operand types (`T.splat(x)` lifts a scalar into every lane), call a named method like `.dot()`/`.matmul()`, or implement the operator's hook trait on your own type for this pair.

rows.meaning: Matrix multiplication needs equal inner sides, but these are {left_inner} and {right_inner}
rows.what: Matrix multiplication needs equal inner sides, but these are {left_inner} and {right_inner}
rows.why: The left column measure must match the right row measure
rows.fix: use `Matrix<{left_rows}, {left_inner}> * Matrix<{left_inner}, {right_cols}>`
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use matrix operands whose inner dimensions are equal.

rows.meaning: A point or displacement is used with a value from another coordinate space (D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1=A)
rows.what: `{operation}` needs `{expected}` space, got `{actual}`.
rows.why: Coordinate-space tags are ordinary type facts; combining different spaces would make a numerically valid result mean the wrong thing.
rows.fix: Use a `{expected}` point or displacement, or convert it with a checked transform.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use a `{expected}` point or displacement, or convert it with a checked transform.

rows.meaning: Transform composition has incompatible middle spaces (D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1=A)
rows.what: Cannot compose `{first}` with `{second}`: `{middle_a}` does not match `{middle_b}`.
rows.why: A transform chain is valid only when the destination of the first transform is the source of the next one.
rows.fix: Reverse or replace one transform so both middle spaces are the same.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Reverse or replace one transform so both middle spaces are the same.

rows.meaning: A transform cannot be inverted because it is singular (D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1=A)
rows.what: Cannot invert transform `{transform}`: its determinant is zero.
rows.why: A singular transform has no unique inverse, so inventing one would silently map points to the wrong place.
rows.fix: Use a non-singular transform or handle the failed inverse result.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use a non-singular transform or handle the failed inverse result.

rows.meaning: A geometry value belongs to an old frame or viewport revision (D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1=A)
rows.what: `{value}` belongs to frame `{value_frame}`, but the transform uses frame `{transform_frame}`.
rows.why: Static spaces do not identify dynamic scene or viewport instances; a changed frame cannot safely consume an older value.
rows.fix: Re-read the point or use the transform created for `{value_frame}`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Re-read the point or use the transform created for `{value_frame}`.

rows.meaning: Perspective picking needs depth or returns a ray, not a unique world point (D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1=A)
rows.what: `{operation}` needs depth or ray semantics for a perspective screen point.
rows.why: A screen coordinate under perspective represents a line of possible world positions; choosing one without depth or a ray would invent geometry.
rows.fix: Pass an explicit depth/plane, or call `.ray()` and intersect it with a known plane.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass an explicit depth/plane, or call `.ray()` and intersect it with a known plane.

rows.meaning: This release is tagged `{version}` but removes (or changes incompatibly) the public API item `{item}`.
rows.what: This release is tagged `{version}` but removes (or changes incompatibly) the public API item `{item}`.
rows.why: `{version}` is a {bump_kind} bump, which promises no breaking changes under SemVer. Callers pinned to `^{major}.0` would stop compiling.
rows.fix: Bump to `{next_major}.0.0`, or restore `{item}` (a deprecated forwarding shim counts). Use `--force` to publish anyway with an explicit warning banner.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Bump to the next major version or restore the removed public item.

rows.meaning: Dependency resolver conflict: `{package}` requires `{req_a}` from `{from_a}` but `{req_b}` from `{from_b}`, and no version satisfies both.
rows.what: Dependency resolver conflict: `{package}` requires `{req_a}` from `{from_a}` but `{req_b}` from `{from_b}`, and no version satisfies both.
rows.why: Jet uses a PubGrub-style resolver that requires a single version per package. Two incompatible constraints cannot both be met.
rows.fix: Upgrade or downgrade one of the conflicting dependents so their `{package}` constraints overlap, or ask the authors to release a version that satisfies both.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Align the conflicting dependency constraints or ask for a compatible release.

rows.meaning: `[{severity}]` advisory `{advisory_id}` matches `{package}` `{version}`: {title}.
rows.what: `[{severity}]` advisory `{advisory_id}` matches `{package}` `{version}`: {title}.
rows.why: The advisory database flags this version as having a known vulnerability, exposed interface, or supply-chain risk. `jet inspect audit` exits nonzero only on a `critical` match; lower severities inform and exit 0.
rows.fix: Upgrade to `>= {fixed_version}` (or the version listed in the advisory). Run `jet inspect audit --explain {advisory_id}` for details.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Upgrade to the fixed version named by the advisory and inspect its details.

rows.meaning: Integrity check failed for `{package}` `{version}` — expected `{expected}`, got `{actual}`.
rows.what: Integrity check failed for `{package}` `{version}` — expected `{expected}`, got `{actual}`.
rows.why: A fetched artifact's content hash differs from what the lockfile recorded. This means the artifact changed after it was locked — accidental or deliberate tampering. A `jet fetch` run reports this integrity failure.
rows.fix: Re-run `jet fetch` after cleaning stale Jetpack hangar entries (`jet clean`). If the problem persists, the upstream source may have been altered; audit the change before proceeding.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Re-run `jet fetch` after cleaning stale Jetpack hangar entries (`jet clean`). If the problem persists, the upstream source may have been altered; audit the change before proceeding.

rows.meaning: `{name}` v{version} cannot be published from a dirty working tree.
rows.what: `{name}` v{version} cannot be published from a dirty working tree.
rows.why: The registry records the exact source revision that was published. A dirty tree means uncommitted changes would be silently excluded, making the published package unreproducible.
rows.fix: Commit or stash all uncommitted changes (`git status` to list them), then run `jet registry publish` again. Use `--force` to bypass with an explicit warning banner.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Commit or stash all uncommitted changes (`git status` to list them), then run `jet registry publish` again. Use `--force` to bypass with an explicit warning banner.

rows.meaning: `jet registry yank` requires a version argument.
rows.what: `jet registry yank` requires a version argument.
rows.why: A yank marks one specific published version as deprecated; without a version the command doesn't know which one to yank.
rows.fix: Run `jet registry yank <version>`, e.g. `jet registry yank 1.2.3`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Run `jet registry yank <version>`, e.g. `jet registry yank 1.2.3`.

rows.meaning: `{source}` is malformed: `{detail}`.
rows.what: `{source}` is malformed: `{detail}`.
rows.why: Supply-chain metadata is security-sensitive, so Jet rejects ambiguous or partial records instead of silently skipping them.
rows.fix: Fix the malformed record and retry; use the parser contract in `spec.md` and UTF-8 text.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Fix the malformed record and retry; use the parser contract in `spec.md` and UTF-8 text.

rows.meaning: Registry package name `{name}` is blocked: {reason}
rows.what: Registry package name `{name}` is blocked: {reason}
rows.why: Package names are trust labels. Jet compares each new name with existing names, folds common homoglyphs, and reserves misleading suffixes so a lookalike cannot borrow an established package's identity.
rows.fix: Choose a different package name than `{reference}`, remove the reserved suffix if present, then publish again.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Choose a distinct package name and remove any reserved suffix before publishing.

rows.meaning: `{package}#{version}` is not mature under the advisory policy.
rows.what: `{package}#{version}` is not mature under the advisory policy.
rows.why: A trusted signed feed records the first immutable inclusion of this `{source_class}` release; the configured maturity window has not elapsed.
rows.fix: Wait for the maturity window, or add a reviewed exact `{package}#{version}` exception with a reason, reviewer, and expiry.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Wait for the maturity window or add a reviewed exact-version exception.

rows.meaning: `{source}` was rejected: `{detail}`.
rows.what: `{source}` was rejected: `{detail}`.
rows.why: Advisory policy is security-sensitive; Jet will not use unsigned, stale, rolled-back, forked, or downgraded evidence.
rows.fix: Refresh the signed offline feed and trust root, or repair the lock provenance before retrying.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Refresh the signed offline feed and trust root, or repair the lock provenance before retrying.

rows.meaning: `jet inspect audit` needs `{input}`.
rows.what: `jet inspect audit` needs `{input}`.
rows.why: An audit without its lock or advisory database could report a false clean result.
rows.fix: Provide the lock file and advisory database required by `jet inspect audit`, then rerun `jet inspect audit`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Provide the lock file and advisory database required by `jet inspect audit`, then rerun.

rows.meaning: Malformed input to a ring library parse function — row/line number and detail (E2-M9)
rows.what: `{parser}` found malformed input at row/line {n} — {detail}.
rows.why: The ring library parse function encountered text it can't interpret: a missing delimiter, an unclosed quote, or an unexpected character. The row or line number points at the first offending record.
rows.fix: Fix the input at the location named, or validate it before parsing.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Fix the input at the location named, or validate it before parsing.

rows.meaning: Compiler-known crypto API misuse at the boundary (E2-M9, D-CRYPTO-DIAG1)
rows.what: Crypto API misuse
rows.why: {why}
rows.fix: Replace the offending cryptographic argument with the concrete value or bound named in the diagnostic: {fix}
rows.structured_fix: crypto_misuse|reason:behavior|Use the documented cryptographic bound or supply a runtime value when the value is not compiler-known

rows.meaning: A checked time-format pattern contains an unclosed literal, incomplete percent escape, unsupported token, or zone-only token without a zone
rows.what: `E2703: {detail}`
rows.why: The checked formatter accepts one closed token grammar so a typo cannot silently become literal output, and zone fields cannot claim context that the value does not carry.
rows.fix: Close the quoted literal, complete or correct the `%` escape, choose a supported token, or format a `ZonedDateTime` when the token needs a zone.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Close the quoted literal, complete or correct the `%` escape, choose a supported token, or format a `ZonedDateTime` when the token needs a zone.

rows.meaning: A DateTime epoch conversion exceeds the signed Int carrier at the requested precision
rows.what: `E2704: Unix epoch {unit} do not fit in Int`
rows.why: The DateTime is representable in seconds, but scaling it to the requested subsecond unit would overflow the current Int carrier; clamping would silently change the instant.
rows.fix: Use seconds or a coarser precision, or handle the failed conversion explicitly.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Use seconds or a coarser precision, or handle the failed conversion explicitly.

rows.meaning: Derive orphan rule: neither `` `derive T.{Trait}` `` nor `` `{Type}` `` is local.
rows.what: derive orphan rule: neither `` `derive T.{Trait}` `` nor `` `{Type}` `` is local.
rows.why: A generated implementation has a clear local owner only when its derive provider or target type lives in the entry module (D-METADERIVE1=A). Two imported sides leave the entry package owning neither contract.
rows.fix: Define `derive T.{Trait}` or `{Type}` in the entry module.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Define the derive provider or target type in the entry module.

rows.meaning: This checked text type rejected its body
rows.what: This checked text type rejected its body
rows.why: A library's `CheckedText.check` function rejected the complete literal body (D-TEXTHEAD-TYPE1=A).
rows.fix: Fix the body so it satisfies the type's declared text grammar.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Fix the body so it satisfies the type's declared text grammar.

rows.meaning: A user derive is written `derive T.{Trait}`.
rows.what: A user derive is written `derive T.{Trait}`.
rows.why: The type parameter comes first, joined to the trait name with a dot (D-METADERIVE1, amended 2026-07-01); the `derive {Trait} for T` spelling was retired.
rows.fix: Write `derive T.{Trait} { … }`.

rows.meaning: {operation} on `{address}` failed: {detail}.
rows.what: {operation} on `{address}` failed: {detail}.
rows.why: A socket bind, listen, connect, or accept call returned an OS error. The address and operation are named so you can act on the specific failure.
rows.fix: check that the address is reachable and the port is not already in use. For `bind`, try a different port. For `connect`, verify the server is running.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|check that the address is reachable and the port is not already in use. For `bind`, try a different port. For `connect`, verify the server is running.

rows.meaning: TLS handshake with `{host}` failed: {detail}.
rows.what: TLS handshake with `{host}` failed: {detail}.
rows.why: The TLS layer could not complete a secure handshake — the certificate may be invalid, expired, or untrusted by the system trust store.
rows.fix: Verify the server's certificate, ensure the system trust store is up-to-date, or use `core.net.tls.insecure_skip_verify()` in a test environment only.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Verify the server's certificate, ensure the system trust store is up-to-date, or use `core.net.tls.insecure_skip_verify()` in a test environment only.

rows.meaning: Request body exceeds the {limit}-byte limit.
rows.what: Request body exceeds the {limit}-byte limit.
rows.why: The server's configured `max_body` cap was reached. Allowing unbounded bodies risks memory exhaustion.
rows.fix: Raise the `max_body` option passed to `http.serve`, or reject the request in your handler before reading the body.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Raise the `max_body` option passed to `http.serve`, or reject the request in your handler before reading the body.

rows.meaning: Two routes both match `{METHOD} {pattern}`.
rows.what: Two routes both match `{METHOD} {pattern}`.
rows.why: A duplicate route makes dispatch ambiguous — one handler would never be reached. Registered at start-up so the bug surfaces immediately.
rows.fix: remove one of the duplicate registrations, or make the patterns distinct (e.g. add a static prefix to one).
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|remove one of the duplicate registrations, or make the patterns distinct (e.g. add a static prefix to one).

rows.meaning: Invalid HTTP route `{pattern}`: {reason}.
rows.what: Invalid HTTP route `{pattern}`: {reason}.
rows.why: Route patterns use one canonical grammar. Ambiguous escapes, traversal, duplicate names, or retired markers would make routing and audit metadata disagree.
rows.fix: use `:name` for one segment or final `*name` for a catch-all. Percent-encode a literal leading `:` or `*`; never encode `/`.

rows.meaning: Convention file `{path}` has no `fn page`.
rows.what: Convention file `{path}` has no `fn page`.
rows.why: Files under a `.routes(from:)` root must declare `fn page` or start with `_` to opt out. A file without a page would register an endpoint the compiler cannot analyze.
rows.fix: add `fn page()`, rename the file with a leading `_`, or remove it from the routes directory.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|add `fn page()`, rename the file with a leading `_`, or remove it from the routes directory.

rows.meaning: Route `{path}` is registered both by `{a}` and `{b}`.
rows.what: Route `{path}` is registered both by `{a}` and `{b}`.
rows.why: Explicit builder entries and `.routes(from:)` conventions must not claim the same path (D-WEBAUTHOR1).
rows.fix: remove one registration, or rename the convention file.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|remove one registration, or rename the convention file.

rows.meaning: `{kind}` `{name}` is not a statically known handler.
rows.what: `{kind}` `{name}` is not a statically known handler.
rows.why: D-WEBAPP1 records every route and action on the typed application graph; a runtime-built handler outside `.mount` is an unanalyzed edge.
rows.fix: Pass a named function, or declare `.mount(prefix, handler)` for dynamic subtrees.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass a named function, or declare `.mount(prefix, handler)` for dynamic subtrees.

rows.meaning: Doctest output mismatch. Expected: `{expected}` Got: `{actual}`
rows.what: Doctest output mismatch. Expected: `{expected}` Got: `{actual}`
rows.why: The example in the doc comment claims a different result from what the code produces. Docs cannot lie (D-TEST4/I5 generalized to user code).
rows.fix: Run `jet test --update-snapshots` to update the golden output, or fix the code to match the claimed output.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Run `jet test --update-snapshots` to update the golden output, or fix the code to match the claimed output.

rows.meaning: `#Todo` at `{file}:{line}` — expected `{type}`
rows.what: `#Todo` at `{file}:{line}` — expected `{type}`
rows.why: A `#Todo` typed goal was reached at runtime. The goal compiles anywhere and type-checks, but panics when executed (D-TOOL2).
rows.fix: Replace `#Todo` with a real implementation.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Replace `#Todo` with a real implementation.

rows.meaning: Performance-budget declaration, typed value, unit, direction, comparison, or applicability is invalid (D-PERFBUDGET-OUTPUT1)
rows.what: Performance budget `{name}` is not valid
rows.why: One grammar rule, typed value, unit, direction, comparison, or applicability constraint is invalid.
rows.fix: use the one legal typed budget form named by the diagnostic.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use the one legal typed budget form named by the diagnostic.

rows.meaning: Two performance budgets overlap on one effective key (D-PERFBUDGET-OUTPUT1)
rows.what: Performance budgets `{a}` and `{b}` overlap
rows.why: Both declarations cover the same effective metric, scope, provider, target, profile, and applicability key.
rows.fix: remove one declaration or make their applicability disjoint.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|remove one declaration or make their applicability disjoint.

rows.meaning: Performance-budget scope, target, profile, or provider cannot resolve uniquely (D-PERFBUDGET-OUTPUT1)
rows.what: Performance budget `{name}` cannot resolve `{attachment}`
rows.why: The attachment has zero or multiple canonical matches.
rows.fix: Name one qualified scope, target, profile, or provider identity.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Name one qualified scope, target, profile, or provider identity.

rows.meaning: Valid performance budget has unavailable, mismatched, stale, or insufficient provider evidence (D-PERFBUDGET-OUTPUT1)
rows.what: Performance budget `{name}` has no usable evidence
rows.why: The resolved provider returned unavailable, missing, mismatched, zero, stale, or too little evidence for this valid budget.
rows.fix: Correct the provider evidence, or bootstrap only when absent or stale evidence is eligible.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Correct the provider evidence, or bootstrap only when absent or stale evidence is eligible.

rows.meaning: Performance budget regressed or statistical evidence is inconclusive (D-PERFBUDGET-OUTPUT1)
rows.what: Performance budget `{name}` regressed / is inconclusive
rows.why: The shared evaluator's estimator and confidence bounds do not prove the declared limit.
rows.fix: Improve the measured behavior, inspect the named evidence, or record an explicit exception.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Improve the measured behavior, inspect the named evidence, or record an explicit exception.

rows.meaning: Performance-budget provider/protocol/storage operation failed before acceptance (D-PERFBUDGET-OUTPUT1)
rows.what: Performance budget operation failed
rows.why: Provider protocol/execution, report/container, CAS, permission, or durability validation refused the operation.
rows.fix: Correct the named refusal and retry; there is no force bypass.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Correct the named refusal and retry; there is no force bypass.

rows.meaning: `reactive.derived`/`effect` argument isn't a lambda (D-REACT1)
rows.what: `reactive.{kind}` needs a lambda, not {type}.
rows.why: `reactive.derived`/`reactive.effect` build a reactive value from a `() -> …` body so it can re-run when a signal changes (D-REACT1=B). A non-lambda argument has nothing to re-run.
rows.fix: Write `reactive.derived(() -> … )` or `reactive.effect(() -> { … })`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `reactive.derived(() -> … )` or `reactive.effect(() -> { … })`.

rows.meaning: `reactive.derived`/`effect` lambda takes parameters (D-REACT1)
rows.what: `reactive.{kind}` needs a zero-parameter lambda, got {n} parameter(s).
rows.why: The body of a derived/effect takes no arguments — it reads the signals it depends on via `.get()` (D-REACT1=B).
rows.fix: Drop the parameters: `reactive.{kind}(() -> { … })`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Drop the lambda parameters and read signals from the zero-parameter body.

rows.meaning: `reactive.derived` lambda returns nothing (D-REACT1)
rows.what: `reactive.derived` must compute and return a value.
rows.why: A derived value is recomputed from its signals, so its lambda has to return the new value (D-REACT1=B). A body that returns nothing is a side effect, not a value.
rows.fix: return a value from the body, or use `reactive.effect(() -> { … })` for a side effect.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|return a value from the body, or use `reactive.effect(() -> { … })` for a side effect.

rows.meaning: A reactive `Signal`/`Derived` can't hold a function value (D-REACT1)
rows.what: A reactive {kind} can't hold a {type}.
rows.why: Signals and derived values hold ordinary data so it can be copied to dependents (D-REACT1=B). A function value isn't reactive data — wrap behaviour in an effect instead.
rows.fix: use a data value (number, text, list, struct, …); put behaviour in `reactive.effect`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use a data value (number, text, list, struct, …); put behaviour in `reactive.effect`.

rows.meaning: `#Reactive fn` must not return a value (D-REACTCORE1)
rows.what: `#Reactive fn` must not return a value (D-REACTCORE1)
rows.why: The registered sema rule applies here
rows.fix: Remove the value return from the `#Reactive fn`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Remove the value return from the `#Reactive fn`.

rows.meaning: An interactive `UiAriaRole` node has an empty accessible label, lint-only (D-A11YGATE1)
rows.what: This {role} has no accessible label
rows.why: Screen readers announce a control by its accessible label; an empty label is invisible to assistive tech.
rows.fix: Pass a real label, e.g. `ui.node_role("Submit", w, h, ui.aria_role_button())`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Pass a real label, e.g. `ui.node_role("Submit", w, h, ui.aria_role_button())`.

rows.meaning: Two interactive nodes in an inline focus group share an accessible label, lint-only (D-A11YGATE1)
rows.what: Two interactive nodes both have the label "{label}"
rows.why: Assistive tech announces controls by their label — identical labels make them indistinguishable (WCAG 2.5.3).
rows.fix: Give each interactive node a distinct, descriptive label.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Give each interactive node a distinct, descriptive label.

rows.meaning: A `Layout{ … }` constraint mixes a horizontal and vertical value (D-LAYOUT1 / D-LAYOUT-GATES1)
rows.what: Layout constraint mixes a horizontal and vertical value (`{lt}` and `{rt}`)
rows.why: `left`/`right`/`width` are horizontal (`HVar`); `top`/`bottom`/`height` are vertical (`VVar`) — combining or comparing across axes is caught at compile time instead of producing a nonsensical layout.
rows.fix: Compare or combine values from the same axis (a `LengthVar`, or a plain number, fits either axis).
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Compare or combine values from the same axis (a `LengthVar`, or a plain number, fits either axis).

rows.meaning: An element inside `Layout{ … }` doesn't produce a `Constraint` (D-LAYOUT1 / D-LAYOUT-CTOR1)
rows.what: This element inside `{name} :: Layout{{ … }}` doesn't produce a constraint (found `{ty}`)
rows.why: Every element directly inside a `Layout{ … }` body must be a `>=`/`<=`/`==` comparison of layout values (a `Constraint`), comma-separated like other typed-literal element bodies.
rows.fix: Write a comparison, e.g. `label.width >= 80.0`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write a comparison, e.g. `label.width >= 80.0`.

rows.meaning: A `Layout{ … }` constraint exactly duplicates an earlier one in the same body, lint-only (D-LAYOUT1)
rows.what: This constraint repeats one already written in this `Layout{{ … }}` body
rows.why: An exact duplicate constraint doesn't tighten the layout — it's almost always a copy-paste leftover.
rows.fix: remove the duplicate line, or change it if a different constraint was meant.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|remove the duplicate line, or change it if a different constraint was meant.

rows.meaning: Teaching: retired `layout NAME { … }` → `name :: Layout{ … }` (D-LAYOUT-CTOR1)
rows.what: `` `layout` is retired ``
rows.why: Constraint layouts use typed-literal construction.
rows.fix: Write `` `{name} :: Layout{{ … }}` ``.

rows.meaning: Teaching: retired `LayoutHandle` → `Layout` (D-LAYOUT-CTOR1)
rows.what: The constraint-layout type is named `Layout`, not `LayoutHandle`
rows.why: One name for the solver/container value (I8).
rows.fix: Write `Layout` instead of `LayoutHandle`.

rows.meaning: A UI host service is used without its declared package capability (D-FOUND-PLATFORM1=A)
rows.what: UI host service `{service}` needs `{capability}`.
rows.why: The typed host row crosses an operating-system service boundary, so every tier must receive the same explicit package capability instead of discovering permission at runtime. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: Add `{capability}` to `authority.needs` in the package manifest, then rebuild.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Add the required package capability to `authority.needs`, then rebuild.

rows.meaning: A `.cmd` shortcut must be a non-empty plain key literal (D-FOUND-PLATFORM1=A)
rows.what: Invalid UI shortcut literal `{shortcut}`: {reason}
rows.why: `.cmd` is the checked command-key constructor, so its key is fixed before code generation and every tier receives the same shortcut metadata. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: Write a non-empty plain string literal, for example `.cmd("s")`; use `core.ui.host.shortcut` for a dynamic key.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write a non-empty plain string literal, for example `.cmd("s")`; use `core.ui.host.shortcut` for a dynamic key.

rows.meaning: Required proof evidence is unavailable
rows.what: Required proof evidence is unavailable
rows.why: The `complete_required` policy needs `{producer}`, but `{reason}`.
rows.fix: Perform the producer-specific action named by `jet prove`, then run the same command again.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Perform the producer-specific action named by `jet prove`, then run the same command again.

rows.meaning: Unknown proof lens `{value}`
rows.what: Unknown proof lens `{value}`
rows.why: `jet prove` accepts `all`, `refinements`, `effects`, `taint`, `contracts`, `tests`, `budgets`, `replay`, and `solver`.
rows.fix: use one exact value, for example `jet prove TARGET --lens tests`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|use one exact value, for example `jet prove TARGET --lens tests`.

rows.meaning: Solver found a counterexample to `{obligation}`
rows.what: Solver found a counterexample to `{obligation}`
rows.why: The assignment satisfies every assumption but makes the claim false.
rows.fix: change the function or claim so every admitted input satisfies the postcondition.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|change the function or claim so every admitted input satisfies the postcondition.

rows.meaning: Package policy ceiling violation (D-TEAMPOLICY1=A)
rows.what: Package policy `{rule}` rejects `{subject}` at `{path}`
rows.why: The package policy gives `{path}` an explicit ceiling, so this source use is outside the team's declared boundary.
rows.fix: Change the source or update `{rule}` in `package.jet`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Change the source or update the package policy rule.

rows.meaning: Checked frame resource accesses cannot produce a legal schedule (D-RESOURCE-SCHEDULE1=A)
rows.what: Frame resource schedule refused: {detail}
rows.why: The scheduler derives dependencies, transfers, lifetimes, and reuse only from checked access and completion facts; an unresolved alias or completion would make execution unsafe.
rows.fix: Preserve source order, declare the complete resource access, or provide the real completion event before requesting parallel execution.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Preserve source order, declare the complete resource access, or provide the real completion event before requesting parallel execution.

rows.meaning: Program-side runtime breach with Jet source location, function name, source-line context box, and (in debug builds) safe local values (E2-M12, D-OBS1/D-OBS2)
rows.what: `panic: {msg}`
rows.why: The program hit a `panic`, `assert`, or `assert_eq` call that failed, a bounds/key check triggered at runtime, or another program-side stop. The shared report boundary owns the program-side stop; an unhandled entry error is a returned report, not E3001. Jet file and line are shown in Jet terms — never generated-Rust terms (I2).
rows.fix: Fix the logic that led to the failure. Program-side stops exit 70 through the shared boundary; unhandled entry errors print their report and exit 1; exit 101 is reserved for Jet defects.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Fix the logic that led to the failure. Program-side stops exit 70 through the shared boundary; unhandled entry errors print their report and exit 1; exit 101 is reserved for Jet defects.

rows.meaning: The trail of `?` hops a failed value took, printed under the root failure with consecutive repeats collapsed (E2-M12, D-OBS1, D-FAIL-CTX1)
rows.what: `Trail [E3002] (N hops via ?, origin first):` followed by one numbered `{fn} ({file}:{line})` line per hop, each with its note after an em dash and `×N` when the same hop repeats.
rows.why: Each failed `?` joins the failure's trail, so the report can show where the failure started and which callers forwarded it.
rows.fix: Read the root failure above the trail first — it says what went wrong. Then read the trail from hop 1, the origin, down to the last hop at the entry.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Read the root failure above the trail first — it says what went wrong. Then read the trail from hop 1, the origin, down to the last hop at the entry.

rows.meaning: Deadline exceeded at a wait/IO point while a `#Context(deadline: …)` budget is active (D-DEADLINE1)
rows.what: `deadline exceeded while waiting in {wait_kind}`.
rows.why: A wait/IO point observed an active `#Context(deadline: …)` budget and the remaining time reached zero before the operation completed.
rows.fix: Raise the deadline budget, shorten the work before the wait point, or remove/adjust the ambient deadline for this scope.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Raise the deadline budget, shorten the work before the wait point, or remove/adjust the ambient deadline for this scope.

rows.meaning: task cancelled at a cooperative wait point (D-CANCELMODEL1)
rows.what: task cancelled at a cooperative wait point
rows.why: The task control plane requested cancellation before this wait completed
rows.fix: Handle `TaskFailure.Cancelled`, or use `#Shield` around a cancellation-sensitive wait.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Handle `TaskFailure.Cancelled`, or use `#Shield` around a cancellation-sensitive wait.

rows.meaning: A `#Pre`/`#Post` contract clause failed — checked in every build, not a debug/release split (D-PREPOST1)
rows.what: `@{Pre|Post} contract failed: {msg}`
rows.why: A `#Pre` (argument claim, checked at entry) or `#Post` (`result` claim, checked before return) condition evaluated false at runtime. `{msg}` is the clause's own message string. Checked in every build (not a debug/release split) — with file:line.
rows.fix: Fix the caller (a failed `#Pre` means an argument violated the function's stated contract) or the function body (a failed `#Post` means it broke its own promise about the result).
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Fix the caller (a failed `#Pre` means an argument violated the function's stated contract) or the function body (a failed `#Post` means it broke its own promise about the result).

rows.meaning: An arithmetic or bounds operation has no valid result
rows.what: `{msg}`
rows.why: The operands or position do not produce a valid result, so the safe runtime stops instead of returning corrupted data — with Jet file and line.
rows.fix: Check the operands or bounds before the operation, or use a checked operation that returns an outcome.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Check the operands or bounds before the operation, or use a checked operation that returns an outcome.

rows.meaning: A `#Todo` goal was reached at runtime
rows.what: `#Todo at {file}:{line} — expected {type}`
rows.why: This code is deliberately incomplete and reached a running program.
rows.fix: Implement the missing code before running the program.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Implement the missing code before running the program.

rows.meaning: Call depth exceeded Jet's safe runtime limit
rows.what: Stack overflow in `{fn}`
rows.why: The call stack kept growing without reaching a safe return — with Jet file, line, and source context
rows.fix: End the recursion or make progress toward a base case.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|End the recursion or make progress toward a base case.

rows.meaning: A task remained parked at the process exit boundary (D-OBSERVE-TASK1)
rows.what: Parked tasks remain at process exit: {msg}
rows.why: The scheduler reached process exit while one or more tasks were blocked on a wait target.
rows.fix: Join each task or make its wait reachable before process exit.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Join each task or make its wait reachable before process exit.

rows.meaning: A foreign function failed across a runtime boundary with Jet source location, function name, and source-line context (D-FAIL-BREACH1)
rows.what: `foreign function failed: {msg}`
rows.why: The foreign implementation or its ABI boundary rejected the call, so Jet stopped instead of fabricating a result.
rows.fix: Fix the foreign function or handle its documented failure before calling it again.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Fix the foreign function or handle its documented failure before calling it again.

rows.meaning: Low-level memory operation used outside an `#Unsafe("…")` block (D-UNSAFE2)
rows.what: `{op}` can only run inside an `#Unsafe` block.
rows.why: This operation can violate memory safety, so it must sit in an audited region.
rows.fix: wrap it: `#Unsafe("why this is safe") { … }`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|wrap it: `#Unsafe("why this is safe") { … }`.

rows.meaning: Low-level memory vocabulary used without `use core.mem` (D-UNSAFE2)
rows.what: `{item}` is part of the low-level tier.
rows.why: Naming `Ptr`, `volatile_read`, or an allocator needs the discovery gate. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: add `use core.mem;` at the top of the file.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|add `use core.mem;` at the top of the file.

rows.meaning: `#Unsafe fn` called without an enclosing `#Unsafe("…")` block (D-UNSAFE2)
rows.what: `{fn}` is an `#Unsafe` function.
rows.why: Its contract can't be checked by the compiler, so the caller must vouch for it.
rows.fix: Call it inside `#Unsafe("…") { … }`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Call it inside `#Unsafe("…") { … }`.

rows.meaning: Retired allocator-specific use-after-free diagnostic; universal close now uses E0121
rows.what: Retired allocator-specific use-after-free diagnostic.
rows.why: Terminal release now uses ordinary consuming `close(^allocator)` through the move marker `^`.
rows.fix: Follow E0121 and acquire a new allocator after close.

rows.meaning: An `#Unsafe` gate violates an organization/package `.Forbid` floor (D-UNSAFE-OBLIG1)
rows.what: Organization or package policy forbids unsafe code.
rows.why: A lexical gate cannot widen the effective safety floor.
rows.fix: remove the operation or have the policy owner change the outer policy.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|remove the operation or have the policy owner change the outer policy.

rows.meaning: `.PerSite` gate selection is missing or `.Skip` is used without `.PerSite` (D-UNSAFE-OBLIG1)
rows.what: This unsafe gate must choose a permitted obligation mode.
rows.why: `.PerSite` requires `.Track`/`.Skip`, and `.Skip` has no ambient meaning outside `.PerSite`.
rows.fix: add `obligations: .Track`, or use `.Skip` only under a package `.PerSite` policy.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|add `obligations: .Track`, or use `.Skip` only under a package `.PerSite` policy.

rows.meaning: A low-level operation is missing one or more required typed obligations (D-UNSAFE-OBLIG1)
rows.what: `{operation}` is missing unsafe obligations: `{obligations}`.
rows.why: Effective `.Obligations` policy requires a typed proof immediately after each low-level operation.
rows.fix: add `assert valid_ptr, aligned, no_alias`, reduced to the operation-specific required subset.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|add `assert valid_ptr, aligned, no_alias`, reduced to the operation-specific required subset.

rows.meaning: Unknown unsafe option/obligation, or an obligation assertion outside `#Unsafe` (D-UNSAFE-OBLIG1)
rows.what: Invalid unsafe option or obligation assertion.
rows.why: Unsafe proof vocabulary is closed and site-bound.
rows.fix: use only `obligations: .Track`/`.Skip` and `valid_ptr`, `aligned`, `no_alias` inside `#Unsafe`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|use only `obligations: .Track`/`.Skip` and `valid_ptr`, `aligned`, `no_alias` inside `#Unsafe`.

rows.meaning: Configured organization gate-policy input is unreadable or malformed; compilation fails closed
rows.what: Configured organization gate policy cannot be used.
rows.why: Admin policy never fails open when its explicit input is unreadable or malformed.
rows.fix: Fix `JET_ORG_UNSAFE_POLICY` and its manifest-shaped `policy: { unsafe: .Obligations, impure: .GateOnly, nondeterministic: .GateOnly }` file, or remove the variable.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Fix `JET_ORG_UNSAFE_POLICY` and its manifest-shaped `policy: { unsafe: .Obligations, impure: .GateOnly, nondeterministic: .GateOnly }` file, or remove the variable.

rows.meaning: Invalid swizzle lane on vector/SIMD type (D-SWIZZLE1)
rows.what: Lane `{lane}` isn't valid on `{type}`.
rows.why: Swizzle members name lanes with `x`/`y`/`z`/`w`; each type exposes only its lane count (`Vec2`: x/y, `Vec3`: x/y/z, …).
rows.fix: use only the lanes defined for `{type}`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use only lanes defined for the selected type.

rows.meaning: Overlapping write swizzle repeats a lane (D-SWIZZLE1)
rows.what: Write swizzle `{pattern}` repeats a lane on `{type}`.
rows.why: Each lane may be written at most once — overlapping patterns like `v.xx` have no single meaning (D-SWIZZLE1).
rows.fix: Assign each lane once, e.g. `v.xy = …` instead of `v.xx = …`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Assign each lane once, e.g. `v.xy = …` instead of `v.xx = …`.

rows.meaning: `#Unsafe` block/function missing its required reason argument (D-UNSAFE2, D-UNSAFE-REASON1=A)
rows.what: This `#Unsafe` block/function has no reason.
rows.why: Every gated region/function must record why it cannot break memory safety; the audit sentence is mandatory.
rows.fix: add the reason: `#Unsafe("why this is safe") { … }` or `#Unsafe("why this is safe") fn ...`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|add the reason: `#Unsafe("why this is safe") { … }` or `#Unsafe("why this is safe") fn ...`.

rows.meaning: C library `<lib>` not found (hangar + pkg-config)
rows.what: C library `{lib}` was not found.
rows.why: Jet looked for a `{lib}: c@…` dep in `package.jet`, then tried `pkg-config {lib}` on the system; neither provided include/link paths.
rows.fix: Install the system package (e.g. `pacman -S {lib}`), or declare it as `{lib}: c@system` in `deps:`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Install the required system library or declare it in `deps:` with its supported C provider.

rows.meaning: pointer/gated type crosses C boundary outside `#Unsafe` / `core.mem`
rows.what: Type `{ty}` cannot cross the C boundary here.
rows.why: C FFI allows by-value scalars and `String` in ordinary code; pointers and other gated types need `use core.mem` and an `#Unsafe { … }` region (S58).
rows.fix: Move the call inside `#Unsafe`, or change the type to a C-safe value type.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move the call inside `#Unsafe`, or change the type to a C-safe value type.

rows.meaning: Non-C-ABI type in `#Import` / `#Bindgen` fn signature
rows.what: `{ty}` is not a C-compatible type for a foreign function parameter or return.
rows.why: `#Import` / `#Bindgen` functions must use types with a stable C ABI at the edge. A `jet build` run reports this C boundary or linker diagnostic.
rows.fix: use scalars, `String`, or a struct with C layout; pointers only through the gated tier.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use scalars, `String`, or a struct with C layout; pointers only through the gated tier.

rows.meaning: Two C `use` forms for the same lib in one file
rows.what: Two different `use` forms refer to the same C library `{lib}`.
rows.why: S59 allows one bring-in per C lib per file — either `use "{header}" as alias` or `use c.[{lib} as alias]`, not both.
rows.fix: remove one line; keep the form that matches your workflow.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|remove one line; keep the form that matches your workflow.

rows.meaning: Overlay symbol clashes with bindgen (incompatible signature)
rows.what: Overlay `{name}` disagrees with the generated binding.
rows.why: User `#Import module c.{lib}` may override bindgen symbols, but the Jet signature must stay compatible when replacing.
rows.fix: Match the generated signature, or rename your overlay function.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Match the generated signature, or rename your overlay function.

rows.meaning: User declared reserved `__bindgen__` segment
rows.what: module path `{path}` uses the reserved segment `__bindgen__`.
rows.why: Autogen lives in `c.{lib}.__bindgen__`; users declare overlays as `#Import module c.{lib}` only.
rows.fix: Drop `__bindgen__` from your module path, or use `#Import module c.{lib} { … }`.

rows.meaning: `#Bindgen` outside generated `.jet/bindings/c/` file
rows.what: `#Bindgen` is only allowed in generated cache files.
rows.why: `.jet/bindings/c/{lib}.jet` is written by `jet inspect bind`; hand-written sources use `#Import module`.
rows.fix: Edit your overlay file with `#Import module`, or regenerate the cache with `jet inspect bind`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Edit your overlay file with `#Import module`, or regenerate the cache with `jet inspect bind`.

rows.meaning: `jet inspect bind` / header translation failed
rows.what: Could not generate bindings from `{header}`.
rows.why: {reason}
rows.fix: Fix the header path, install dev headers, run `jet inspect bind` manually for details, or hand-write `#Import module c.{lib}`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Correct the header path or install the development headers, then inspect the binding if needed.

rows.meaning: Linker couldn't find a declared C library at link time
rows.what: The linker couldn't find C library `{lib}`.
rows.why: Your program links against `{lib}`, but the linker reported `cannot find -l{lib}` — the library isn't on the link search path. A `jet build` run reports this C boundary or linker diagnostic.
rows.fix: Declare it in `deps:` so Jet provisions it: `{lib}: c@system` (host pkg-config, else fetched from nixpkgs), or `{lib}: c@nixpkgs:<attr>` to pick the nixpkgs attribute, or install the system package.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Declare the library in `deps:` with a supported system or nixpkgs provider, or install it.

rows.meaning: C library auto-provision from nixpkgs failed
rows.what: Couldn't fetch C library `{lib}` from nixpkgs.
rows.why: `{lib}: c@system` asked Jet to provision `nixpkgs#{attr}`, but `nix build` failed: `{reason}`.
rows.fix: check the attr exists (`nix build nixpkgs#{attr}`), or point at a local build with `{lib}: c@"<path>"`, or install it and use `system`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Choose an existing nixpkgs attribute or a local C library path, then declare the provider.

rows.meaning: String literal with a known interior NUL byte passed to a C-boundary function
rows.what: This string literal has an embedded NUL byte, so it can't cross into a C function.
rows.why: C strings are NUL-terminated, not length-prefixed — an embedded `\\0` would truncate the string on the C side, silently losing everything after it.
rows.fix: remove the embedded NUL, or split the call so the C function only sees the part before it.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|remove the embedded NUL, or split the call so the C function only sees the part before it.

rows.meaning: `#ABI` on `extern rust` (Rust FFI has no C calling convention to pick), or `#ABI(name)` names an unknown C calling convention
rows.what: `{abi}` is not a known C calling convention.
rows.why: `#ABI` accepts only the ratified native ABI names — `#ABI` also never applies to `extern rust` (Rust FFI keeps its own declared ABI).
rows.fix: use `system`, `cdecl`, `stdcall`, `fastcall`, `win64`, or `sysv64`, or remove `#ABI` from the `extern rust` function.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|use `system`, `cdecl`, `stdcall`, `fastcall`, `win64`, or `sysv64`, or remove `#ABI` from the `extern rust` function.

rows.meaning: Named C calling convention exists but isn't available on this target's OS/architecture
rows.what: `{abi}` is not available on this target.
rows.why: Native calling conventions are restricted by operating system and architecture (e.g. `stdcall`/`cdecl`/`fastcall` are Windows x86 only; `win64` is Windows x86-64; `sysv64` is non-Windows x86-64).
rows.fix: use the default C ABI or `system` for portable declarations.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use the default C ABI or `system` for portable declarations.

rows.meaning: Variadic C function used with a calling convention other than the default C ABI (or `cdecl` on Windows x86)
rows.what: Variadic C function `{name}` cannot use `{abi}`.
rows.why: Variadics allow only the default C ABI, or `cdecl` on Windows x86 — other calling conventions don't define how a variadic argument list is passed.
rows.fix: remove `#ABI`, or use `#ABI(cdecl)` on Windows x86.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|remove `#ABI`, or use `#ABI(cdecl)` on Windows x86.

rows.meaning: `#FFI(<lang>)` inline foreign fn in an unsafe language (`c`/`cpp`/`asm`) lacks the enclosing `#Unsafe("reason")` gate (D-FFI-INLINE1/ASM1/CPP1)
rows.what: `#FFI(<lang>)` inline foreign fn in an unsafe language (`c`/`cpp`/`asm`) lacks the enclosing `#Unsafe("reason")` gate (D-FFI-INLINE1/ASM1/CPP1)
rows.why: The registered sema rule applies here
rows.fix: Wrap inline foreign code in an enclosing `#Unsafe("reason")` gate.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Wrap inline foreign code in an enclosing `#Unsafe("reason")` gate.

rows.meaning: `#FFI(<lang>)` names a language with no inline foreign binder yet (systems floor ships `c`/`cpp`/`asm`, card #501)
rows.what: `#FFI(<lang>)` names a language with no inline foreign binder yet (systems floor ships `c`/`cpp`/`asm`, card #501)
rows.why: The registered sema rule applies here
rows.fix: Use an inline foreign binder for `c`, `cpp`, or `asm`, or remove the unsupported language.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use an inline foreign binder for `c`, `cpp`, or `asm`, or remove the unsupported language.

rows.meaning: Inline C/C++ body cannot satisfy its declared scalar Jet ABI, or inline asm uses a non-integer/unsupported signature; native tool output stays hidden (D-FFI-INLINE1/ASM1, I2)
rows.what: Inline C/C++ body cannot satisfy its declared scalar Jet ABI, or inline asm uses a non-integer/unsupported signature; native tool output stays hidden (D-FFI-INLINE1/ASM1, I2)
rows.why: The registered sema/build rule applies here
rows.fix: Make the inline body and signature use a supported scalar ABI.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Make the inline body and signature use a supported scalar ABI.

rows.meaning: Inline asm operands do not match the Jet signature: missing/unknown named input, duplicate or missing `; -> return`, or unaudited clobber/target register (D-FFI-ASM1)
rows.what: Inline asm operands do not match the Jet signature: missing/unknown named input, duplicate or missing `; -> return`, or unaudited clobber/target register (D-FFI-ASM1)
rows.why: The registered sema rule applies here
rows.fix: Make the asm operands, return marker, clobbers, and target registers match the Jet signature.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Make the asm operands, return marker, clobbers, and target registers match the Jet signature.

rows.meaning: `com.*` or COM binding requested away from a Windows host
rows.what: `com.*` needs a Windows host.
rows.why: COM type libraries, apartments, the registry, and IDispatch are Windows facilities.
rows.fix: Generate, build, and run the COM module on a Windows host; use a non-COM boundary for other targets.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Generate, build, and run the COM module on a Windows host; use a non-COM boundary for other targets.

rows.meaning: `#Import(c)` function uses a non-canonical body marker
rows.what: `#Import(c)` functions must name their C symbol with `= "symbol"`.
rows.why: `#Import(c)` binds a compile-time C symbol; `->` is a Jet function-body marker and cannot declare a foreign symbol.
rows.fix: Write `#Import(c) fn name(args) Return = "symbol"`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `#Import(c) fn name(args) Return = "symbol"`.

rows.meaning: OS-dependent API called on a selected no-OS target
rows.what: `{api}` is not available on a no-OS target.
rows.why: No-OS targets have no OS; only `core`-level APIs are available.
rows.fix: Embed the data at compile time with `@embed("file")`, or select a hosted target.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Embed the data at compile time with `@embed("file")`, or select a hosted target.

rows.meaning: Target triple unknown or toolchain component missing
rows.what: Target `{triple}` is not available.
rows.why: Rustc doesn't have the standard library for this target compiled in, or the target triple is not recognised. `wasm32-wasip2` is the supported WASI Preview 2 server Component target. A `jet build` or `jet run` run reports this target-support diagnostic.
rows.fix: Run `jet self doctor --target=<triple>` to see what's missing, or `rustup target add <triple>` to install it; use `wasm32-wasip2` for a WASI Preview 2 server.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Run `jet self doctor --target=<triple>` to see what's missing, or `rustup target add <triple>` to install it; use `wasm32-wasip2` for a WASI Preview 2 server.

rows.meaning: No-OS program reaches allocation without an allocator fact
rows.what: This no-OS program allocates memory but has no allocator fact.
rows.why: No-OS targets do not provide an implicit system heap.
rows.fix: Select a typed allocator provider, or use heap-free Core operations.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Select a typed allocator provider, or use heap-free Core operations.

rows.meaning: Selected target does not provide the runtime boundary for a reachable Core socket surface
rows.what: `{module}` is not available for target `{target}`.
rows.why: `{module}` needs native sockets or WASI Preview 2 sockets, and this target provides neither runtime boundary. A `jet build` or `jet run` run reports this target-support diagnostic.
rows.fix: Build for `wasm32-wasip2` or a supported native target, or remove the `{module}` import.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Build for `wasm32-wasip2` or a supported native target, or remove the native-only module.

rows.meaning: Selected target does not provide a runtime adapter for a reachable Core socket operation
rows.what: `{operation}` is not available for target `{target}`.
rows.why: The selected target has no Prelude adapter for `{operation}`; WASI Preview 2 provides TCP/UDP sockets but not this operation. A `jet build` or `jet run` run reports this target-support diagnostic.
rows.fix: use a supported TCP/UDP operation, or build for a native target.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use a supported TCP/UDP operation, or build for a native target.

rows.meaning: Selected web target does not provide the Component Model host boundary for a reachable Core plugin import
rows.what: `{module}` is not available for target `{target}`.
rows.why: The browser Web backend has no native Wasmtime host-import boundary for `core.plugin`; plugin authority and component imports must stay on a native or server host. A `jet build` or `jet run` run reports this target-support diagnostic.
rows.fix: Build for a native target or `wasm32-wasip2`, or move plugin work behind a native/server boundary.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Build for a native target or `wasm32-wasip2`, or move plugin work behind a native/server boundary.

rows.meaning: Reachable Prelude part needs a runtime layer not supplied by the selected target
rows.what: Prelude part `{api}` needs the `{required}` runtime layer, but target `{target}` provides `{available}`.
rows.why: The complete semantic Prelude closure includes `{api}`; a target cannot emit a higher layer or substitute a second Prelude.
rows.fix: Select a typed target with `{required}` support, or remove `{api}` from the reachable closure.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Select a typed target with the required API support, or remove that API from the closure.

rows.meaning: Selected target does not provide a required capability
rows.what: Target `{target}` lacks the required `{capability}` capability.
rows.why: The selected target profile must state each machine service separately; a target triple cannot imply a UART, clock, entropy source, scheduler, allocator, startup provider, or MMIO device.
rows.fix: Select a typed target profile with a `{capability}` provider, or remove the reachable operation.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Select a typed target profile with the required capability provider, or remove the operation.

rows.meaning: Target provider contract has invalid provenance
rows.what: Provider `{provider}` for `{capability}` on target `{target}` has invalid digest `{sha256}`.
rows.why: Every selected provider needs a stable identity and sha256 provenance so artifacts cannot reuse changed target behavior.
rows.fix: Declare a nonempty provider identity and a `sha256:` digest for `{capability}`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Declare a provider identity and `sha256:` digest for the required capability.

rows.meaning: Target MMIO access is outside its declared safety facts
rows.what: Target `{target}` has an MMIO fact failure: {detail}.
rows.why: MMIO addresses must lie inside a declared MMIO region and every access must carry a nonempty `#Unsafe` reason.
rows.fix: Declare a matching MMIO provider and region, then place the access inside `#Unsafe("reason")`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Declare a matching MMIO provider and region, then place the access inside `#Unsafe("reason")`.

rows.meaning: Target machine fact is invalid
rows.what: Target `{target}` has an invalid `{fact}` fact: {detail}.
rows.why: Target memory, linker, allocator, panic, startup, and execution facts are explicit inputs to sema and cannot be recovered safely from a triple.
rows.fix: Select a complete typed target profile and correct the `{fact}` declaration.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Select a complete typed target profile and correct the fact declaration.

rows.meaning: Impure call inside a `fn … -[]>` / pure-eval context, or reached from comptime evaluation (D-META-EFFECT1 c3, was E0951) — call-trace path
rows.what: `{pure_fn}` calls the impure function `{call}`.
rows.why: A `fn … -[]>` may only call other `fn … -[]>`s and pure builtins. Impure calls make the result non-deterministic (D-PURE2). In `jet eval --pure` the whole call graph from `run` is checked transitively; the why-line shows the full chain (`run → a → b calls \\`print\\``) so the user can find the leak. Compile-time (`@` blocks, `@name :: expr` bindings) shares this same call-graph walk (D-META-EFFECT1 c3): the message reads `{call}` is not allowed in comptime code instead, since there is no enclosing `-[]>` function name to report.
rows.fix: Mark `{call}` as `fn … -[]>`, or remove the call from `{pure_fn}`; at compile time, compute the value at runtime instead.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Mark the call pure, remove it from the pure function, or compute the value at runtime.

rows.meaning: Package build attempted ambient I/O or network (names the call)
rows.what: `{call}` is not allowed during a sandboxed package build.
rows.why: Package builds run with ambient I/O and network access disabled (D-PURE2).
rows.fix: Compute this value at compile time or pass it in as a parameter.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Compute this value at compile time or pass it in as a parameter.

rows.meaning: Non-deterministic construct in pure evaluation (e.g. time/random)
rows.what: `{what}` is non-deterministic and cannot appear in a pure evaluation.
rows.why: Pure evaluation must produce the same result on every machine (D-PURE2).
rows.fix: remove this call, or remove the enclosing function's explicit empty effect bound.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|remove this call, or remove the enclosing function's explicit empty effect bound.

rows.meaning: Tier-2 comptime effect (`core.files`/`core.sys`/`core.term`/`core.process`) called outside a `#Impure` gate (D-CTEFFECT1)
rows.what: `{module}.{call}` is a Tier-2 ambient comptime effect and can't run at compile time without a `#Impure` gate.
rows.why: `core.files`, `core.sys`, `core.term`, and `core.process` touch the host system at compile time. Without the gate any build tooling (caches, hermetic sandboxes) may get different results. A `jet build` or `jet run` run reports this comptime-tier diagnostic.
rows.fix: wrap the call in `#Impure("reading config") { … }`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|wrap the call in `#Impure("reading config") { … }`.

rows.meaning: Tier-2 comptime effect inside `#Impure` gate but `--gate impure=allow` not passed (D-CTEFFECT1 / D-ONCE-GATE1=A)
rows.what: `#Impure` gate present but `--gate impure=allow` was not passed.
rows.why: The `#Impure` block opts in to ambient I/O, but the invocation gate is also required so CI can audit builds that touch the host.
rows.fix: add `--gate impure=allow` to your `jet build` / `jet run` invocation.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|add `--gate impure=allow` to your `jet build` / `jet run` invocation.

rows.meaning: `core.net.{method}()` is not available at comptime (only `fetch` is Tier-1)
rows.what: `core.net.{method}()` is not available at comptime.
rows.why: Only `core.net.fetch(url, sha256:)` is supported at compile time as a Tier-1 hermetic effect. Other `core.net` methods are not planned for comptime access. A `jet build` or `jet run` run reports this comptime-tier diagnostic.
rows.fix: use `core.net.fetch(url, sha256: "…")` for content-hash-pinned downloads.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use `core.net.fetch(url, sha256: "…")` for content-hash-pinned downloads.

rows.meaning: Comptime `fetch` sha256 mismatch — content hash doesn't match the `sha256:` pin (D-CTEFFECT1 / D-NETDEP1=A)
rows.what: Fetch: sha256 mismatch for `{url}`.
rows.why: The downloaded content does not hash to the expected `sha256:` value. The pin ensures every machine gets byte-identical content; a mismatch means the URL content changed or the pin is wrong.
rows.fix: Update the `sha256:` argument to match the actual content hash shown in the Why line, or verify the URL points to the correct file.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Update the `sha256:` argument to match the actual content hash shown in the Why line, or verify the URL points to the correct file.

rows.meaning: Comptime `fetch` failed — bad URL, unsupported scheme, network error, or non-UTF-8 content (D-CTEFFECT1 / D-NETDEP1=A)
rows.what: Fetch failed / bad argument / non-UTF-8 content (message varies).
rows.why: Common causes: unsupported URL scheme (only `file://`, `http://`, `https://`), unreachable host, missing `sha256:` argument, or binary content (use `embed_bytes` for that). HTTPS TLS failures use E4201–E4203.
rows.fix: check the URL and arguments; use `file://` for local test paths.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|check the URL and arguments; use `file://` for local test paths.

rows.meaning: Audited gate denied by effective organization or package policy (D-ONCE-GATE1=A)
rows.what: The `{gate}` gate is denied by effective policy.
rows.why: The shared policy ladder is the authority for audited escapes; an invocation gate cannot widen a `.Forbid` floor.
rows.fix: remove the gate or change the owning policy to allow it.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|remove the gate or change the owning policy to allow it.

rows.meaning: Selected root `fn build` has wrong `fn(BuildContext) BuildPlan` signature (D-BUILDENTRY1)
rows.what: `fn build` must take one `BuildContext` and return `BuildPlan`.
rows.why: Build authority and graph handoff are one typed contract. A different signature cannot be selected by `jet build` or modeled by the LSP.
rows.fix: Write `fn build(b: BuildContext) BuildPlan`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Write `fn build(b: BuildContext) BuildPlan`.

rows.meaning: Programmable build evaluation, graph validation, or generated-source materialization failed
rows.what: Build plan is invalid, build evaluation returned an error, or generated source could not materialize.
rows.why: One selected root entry owns one deterministic graph. Handles cannot cross build sessions, outputs need one owner, and generated Jet must become a real file before checking.
rows.fix: Fix the named graph node or generated module; inspect it with `jet inspect graph` and `jet inspect explain-build`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Fix the named graph node or generated module; inspect it with `jet inspect graph` and `jet inspect explain-build`.

rows.meaning: Root build authority is undeclared, ungated, or denied by effective policy (D-BUILDPOLICY1)
rows.what: This root build asks for authority missing from its declaration, `#Impure` gate, or effective policy.
rows.why: Build authority must pass all three independent checks before any probe or action executes.
rows.fix: Declare the effect, gate the ambient operation with `#Impure("reason")`, and grant the effect through CLI/package/workspace policy.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Declare the effect, gate the ambient operation with `#Impure("reason")`, and grant the effect through CLI/package/workspace policy.

rows.meaning: Build action requested authority not granted by CLI/package/workspace policy (D-BUILDPOLICY1)
rows.what: Build action `{action}` asks for ungranted `{right}` authority.
rows.why: Source declaration makes authority auditable but does not grant it. Invocation, package, and workspace policy cap ambient effects independently.
rows.fix: Pass the named `--allow-<effect>` flag for a one-file build, or grant the effect in package/workspace policy.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass the named `--allow-<effect>` flag for a one-file build, or grant the effect in package/workspace policy.

rows.meaning: Typed probe or sandboxed action execution failed (D-BUILDACTION1/D-BUILDPROBE1)
rows.what: Typed build probe or sandboxed action execution failed.
rows.why: Actions run only after graph validation, in a bubblewrap sandbox with declared inputs, outputs, tools, environment, authority, and probes. Jet does not fall back to ambient execution. A `jet build` run reports this typed build-action failure.
rows.fix: Fix the named command, probe, toolchain, input/output declaration, or enable a supported sandbox.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Fix the named command, probe, toolchain, input/output declaration, or enable a supported sandbox.

rows.meaning: Generated module would shadow a hand-written module (D-BUILDGEN1)
