rows.what: `b.generate("{name}")` would shadow the module at `{path}`.
rows.why: Generation is additive: what you wrote is always what compiles.
rows.fix: rename the generated module, or delete the hand-written one.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|rename the generated module, or delete the hand-written one.

rows.meaning: Generated source rounds form a cycle or claim one path twice (D-BUILDGEN1)
rows.what: Generation rounds form a cycle: `{chain}`.
rows.why: Generated source must reach a bounded deterministic order, not loop until quiescent.
rows.fix: break the dependency between the named generators or paths.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|break the dependency between the named generators or paths.

rows.meaning: `--locked` generated input or output hash drifted (D-BUILDGEN1)
rows.what: Locked generated input `{path}` drifted.
rows.why: `--locked` requires generated input and output hashes to match the unified lock exactly before materialization.
rows.fix: Rerun without `--locked` to review and record the new generated provenance.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Rerun without `--locked` to review and record the new generated provenance.

rows.meaning: One package declares multiple `fn build` entries (D-CONF-ENTRY1)
rows.what: Two build entries for one package: both source sites are shown.
rows.why: One package has one build authority, so policy and provenance have one auditable home.
rows.fix: Keep one `fn build` and remove every other entry.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Keep one `fn build` and remove every other entry.

rows.meaning: A build fact has conflicting values from the same contribution layer (D-CONF-MERGE1)
rows.what: Two writers at the same contribution layer gave different values for `{fact}`; both source locations are shown.
rows.why: Cross-layer overrides are legal, but same-layer disagreement is ambiguous and cannot be selected by source order.
rows.fix: Make the named writers agree, or move one value to a more explicit contribution layer.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Make the named writers agree, or move one value to a more explicit contribution layer.

rows.meaning: Custom build rule used a compiler-reserved E/W numeric code (D-METADEPTH2)
rows.what: Build rule code `{code}` is reserved.
rows.why: Codes beginning with E or W followed only by digits belong to the compiler.
rows.fix: use a project prefix such as `ORG01`.

rows.meaning: One command has multiple package-scope function overrides (D-CMDOVERRIDE1)
rows.what: One {command} command has multiple overrides: {locations}.
rows.why: A command scope can select one override or the stock default, but multiple overrides are ambiguous.
rows.fix: Keep one fn {command} in the package scope, or remove the other command override.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Keep one function for the command in package scope, or remove the other override.

rows.meaning: Replay schema version is incompatible
rows.what: Replay schema version is incompatible
rows.why: The `.jetproof-replay` schema major/minor is unsupported by this `jet prove`.
rows.fix: Recapture with a compatible toolchain, or upgrade Jet.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Recapture with a compatible toolchain, or upgrade Jet.

rows.meaning: Replay semantic identity does not match
rows.what: Replay semantic identity does not match
rows.why: Source, toolchain, or adapter identity in the artifact does not match the current target. A `jet prove` run reports this replay-identity failure.
rows.fix: Recapture against this exact revision.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Recapture against this exact revision.

rows.meaning: Replay artifact is corrupt
rows.what: Replay artifact is corrupt
rows.why: Magic, header, frame hash, or footer verification failed.
rows.fix: Pass an intact `.jetproof-replay` path.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Pass an intact `.jetproof-replay` path.

rows.meaning: Replay diverged from captured authority
rows.what: Replay diverged from captured authority
rows.why: The next recorded authority, consumed-record count, or captured run outcome does not match the current producer run.
rows.fix: Recapture with `--capture`, then replay the same target identity.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Recapture with `--capture`, then replay the same target identity.

rows.meaning: Replay target cardinality is not one
rows.what: Replay target cardinality is not one
rows.why: Capture or replay selected zero or multiple runnable target members.
rows.fix: Select one runnable file or package target.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Select one runnable file or package target.

rows.meaning: Replay capture cannot model `{operation}`
rows.what: Replay capture cannot model `{operation}`
rows.why: The reachable operation has no bounded replay adapter, including opaque, native, task, or unsupported effect boundaries.
rows.fix: Route the operation through a supported deterministic input, or remove it from the captured target.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Route the operation through a supported deterministic input, or remove it from the captured target.

rows.meaning: Replay capture lacks `{effect}` authority
rows.what: Replay capture lacks `{effect}` authority
rows.why: The operation's existing lexical or invocation authority is missing; capture never grants it implicitly.
rows.fix: add the exact existing authority or change the target before capture.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|add the exact existing authority or change the target before capture.

rows.meaning: Replay capture refused sensitive data
rows.what: Replay capture refused sensitive data
rows.why: Safe capture refuses reachable Rand/IO/Net; sensitive capture needs TTY consent.
rows.fix: use `--capture` for Time-only, or run `--capture-sensitive` interactively.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use `--capture` for Time-only, or run `--capture-sensitive` interactively.

rows.meaning: Replay capture exceeded its artifact limit
rows.what: Replay capture exceeded its artifact limit
rows.why: The replay contained no usable authority or exceeded the bounded frame/payload/record budget.
rows.fix: Reduce the captured target or recapture a bounded artifact.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Reduce the captured target or recapture a bounded artifact.

rows.meaning: Replay artifact could not be finalized
rows.what: Replay artifact could not be finalized
rows.why: Destination path, rename, or durability checks refused the write.
rows.fix: Fix the path and retry; differing existing bytes are never overwritten.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Fix the path and retry; differing existing bytes are never overwritten.

rows.meaning: HTTPS client TLS handshake failed before any response was received (D-TLS1)
rows.what: TLS handshake with `{host}` failed.
rows.why: The URL reached a server, but the connection did not complete a secure HTTPS handshake. The usual cause is pointing an `https://` URL at a plain HTTP server or a server with a broken TLS setup.
rows.fix: Verify the URL points at an HTTPS server, not plain HTTP. For local tests, start the TLS fixture server.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Verify the URL points at an HTTPS server, not plain HTTP. For local tests, start the TLS fixture server.

rows.meaning: HTTPS client certificate could not be trusted (D-TLS1)
rows.what: TLS certificate for `{host}` could not be trusted.
rows.why: The server presented a certificate Jet could not verify for that host. It may be expired, for another name, self-signed, or missing an intermediate.
rows.fix: use a certificate whose subject matches the host and chains to a trusted root. For tests, trust the local fixture CA explicitly.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use a certificate whose subject matches the host and chains to a trusted root. For tests, trust the local fixture CA explicitly.

rows.meaning: HTTPS client could not find usable system certificate roots (D-TLS1)
rows.what: HTTPS could not find system certificate roots.
rows.why: D-TLS1 uses rustls with the system trust store for default HTTPS. Minimal images can omit that bundle, so there is no root set to verify public certificates against.
rows.fix: Install the system certificate bundle (for example `ca-certificates`) or run in an image that includes it.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Install the system certificate bundle (for example `ca-certificates`) or run in an image that includes it.

rows.meaning: An App feature is not available for the resolved target (D-APP-UNIFY1=B)
rows.what: App feature `.{feature}` needs target `{required}`, but the resolved target is `{target}`.
rows.why: App is one type across targets, but each feature must be supported by the target selected by `#Target` or the package manifest; rejecting it in sema keeps AOT, JIT, interpreter, and web codegen on one meaning (I9). During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: Choose a build target that supports `.{feature}` (for example `#Target(JS)` for browser features or a native target for server features), or remove that feature.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Choose a target that supports the feature, or remove the feature.

rows.meaning: Function values use `.call(…)`, not the retired adjacent-call spelling `)(` (D-CALLVALUE1=B)
rows.what: A function value is invoked with the retired adjacent-call spelling
rows.why: Named functions and direct field, index, or lambda calls keep their spelling; a returned call result uses `.call(…)` so the value and invocation stay explicit (D-CALLVALUE1=B)
rows.fix: Write `callee.call(…)`
rows.structured_fix: generated:call_value|behavior-preserving

rows.meaning: Retired bare default failure contract; use implicit failure
rows.what: `!` is a retired bare default failure contract.
rows.why: Ordinary fallible functions use the implicit default `Err` contract; the `!` prefix is only for a named error domain.
rows.fix: remove `!`; failure is implicit, or name an explicit domain such as `!IOError`.
rows.structured_fix: remove:!|formatting

rows.meaning: Retired bare failure propagation mark; propagation is implicit
rows.what: Bare `?` propagation is retired.
rows.why: Fallible calls propagate automatically; `?(text)` is reserved for adding one failure-context frame.
rows.fix: remove the trailing `?`, or write `?(text)` to add one context frame.
rows.structured_fix: remove:?|formatting

rows.meaning: Retired infix fallible type spelling; use a prefix failure contract (D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1)
rows.what: `T ! E` and `T ? E` are retired infix fallible type spellings.
rows.why: The success type and error type have one unambiguous prefix contract, so `?` keeps one meaning: possible absence when it prefixes a success type.
rows.fix: Write `?Entry !StoreError`, `Int !(DbError | TimeoutError)`, or `!IOError`; remove a bare `!` contract because failure is implicit.
rows.structured_fix: source_edit|formatting

rows.meaning: Retired suffix failure contract; use a prefix error contract (D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1)
rows.what: `Error!` is a retired suffix failure contract.
rows.why: Jet puts the error contract before its type so the success role and error role stay distinct in every type position.
rows.fix: Write `!Error`, or write `?Success !Error` when the success can be absent.
rows.structured_fix: source_edit|formatting

rows.meaning: Model package cannot be loaded
rows.what: Model package `{package}` cannot be loaded: `{reason}`
rows.why: The ordinary package loader must fail closed for missing artifacts, offline misses, unsupported providers, limits, and backend failures; it cannot download or fabricate a model.
rows.fix: Make the declared artifact available in the package, or choose a supported provider and declared limit.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Make the declared artifact available in the package, or choose a supported provider and declared limit.

rows.meaning: Model package provenance is not pinned
rows.what: Model package `{package}` has incomplete or mismatched provenance
rows.why: A model package is reproducible only when its artifact hashes, version identity, and license are recorded and verified by the ordinary package loader.
rows.fix: Add the artifact hash, tokenizer hash, package version, and license to the model package manifest.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Pin the artifact and tokenizer hashes, package version, and license in the package manifest.

rows.meaning: Model package tensor signature mismatch
rows.what: Model package `{package}` declares `{expected}` but the supplied tensor has `{actual}`
rows.why: The model boundary checks tensor names, dtypes, and shapes before a provider can run; accepting a different signature would turn a checked package into a runtime surprise.
rows.fix: Make the tensor name, dtype, and shape match the package declaration.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Make the tensor name, dtype, and shape match the package declaration.

rows.meaning: An `@if … == { }` OS dispatch's subject is not `@build.os` (D-OSTARGET2)
rows.what: An `@if … == { … }` dispatch branches on `@build.os`.
rows.why: `@build.os` is the one compiler-known comptime value this dispatch folds on — it selects the arm matching the build's target OS at compile time (D-OSTARGET2).
rows.fix: Write `@if @build.os == { .Linux -> … .MacOS -> … .Windows -> … }`, or use a plain runtime `if` for a value that isn't known at compile time.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `@if @build.os == { .Linux -> … .MacOS -> … .Windows -> … }`, or use a plain runtime `if` for a value that isn't known at compile time.

rows.meaning: An `@if @build.os == { }` arm head is not a bare `.Linux`/`.MacOS`/`.Windows` variant, or repeats one (D-OSTARGET2)
rows.what: `{found}` is not an OS arm — an `@build.os` dispatch matches `.Linux`, `.MacOS`, or `.Windows`.
rows.why: Each arm gates code for exactly one native OS, so its head is a bare, payload-free OS variant — the same set `#Target(OS.*)` uses — and each OS appears at most once.
rows.fix: Write `.Linux -> …`, `.MacOS -> …`, or `.Windows -> …` (add an `else -> …` for a shared fallback).
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write `.Linux -> …`, `.MacOS -> …`, or `.Windows -> …` (add an `else -> …` for a shared fallback).

rows.meaning: An `@if @build.os == { }` dispatch leaves some target OS uncovered with no `else` (D-OSTARGET2)
rows.what: This `@build.os` dispatch doesn't cover every target OS — missing: {list}.
rows.why: A build can target any native OS, so the dispatch must handle each one — otherwise a build for a missing OS would have no arm to run.
rows.fix: add an arm for each missing OS ({list}), or an `else -> …` catch-all.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Add one dispatch arm for each missing OS or add an `else` catch-all.

rows.meaning: A `#Target(OS.*)`-gated impl's file/module also carries a web-bucket ceiling (D-OSTARGET1)
rows.what: `#Target(OS.{os})` can't combine with `#Target({web})` on `{item}`.
rows.why: The OS axis (`OS.Linux`/`OS.MacOS`/`OS.Windows`, native platform gating) and the web axis (`Wasm`/`JS`/`Web`, D-WASM1's browser partition) are mutually exclusive — one item can't compile for both a specific native OS and a web bucket. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: Pick one axis: remove the `#Target(OS.{os})` marker or the web-axis marker.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Choose one target axis and remove the conflicting target marker.

rows.meaning: A function/method not gated to match takes or returns a value of a `#Target(OS.*)`-gated type (D-OSTARGET1)
rows.what: `{caller}` uses `{gated_type}`, whose `impl` is gated to `#Target(OS.{os})`, without itself being gated to match.
rows.why: An OS-gated impl only exists in the build for that OS; code reachable on other platforms would hit a missing method, so this is caught at compile time, not left to fail as a link (or a raw rustc) error. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
rows.fix: Only use `{gated_type}` from inside an `impl` already gated to `#Target(OS.{os})`, or move `{caller}`'s body into one.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use the gated type only inside its matching OS target, or move the caller body there.

rows.meaning: Bare member shorthand used where an ordinary value is expected (D-SUBJECT-CALL1=A)
rows.what: A bare member chain cannot be used as a value of type {expected} here
rows.why: Lower-case `.member` is shorthand only for a one-parameter callable; this argument expects an ordinary value
rows.fix: Write a value of type {expected}, or use `(subject: {expected}) -> subject{chain}`
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write an ordinary value of the expected type, or use a full subject lambda.

rows.meaning: Bare member shorthand used with a non-unary callable (D-SUBJECT-CALL1=A)
rows.what: A bare member chain cannot supply a {arity}-parameter callable here
rows.why: Lower-case `.member` shorthand supplies exactly one subject; a callable with {arity} parameters needs all parameters named
rows.fix: Write the full lambda, for example `(first, second) -> first{chain}`
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Write a full lambda with every parameter named.

rows.meaning: A JS/WASM boundary type is not ABI-safe (D-JSBIND1)
rows.what: `Point` cannot cross the JS/WASM boundary on a `#WasmExport` parameter
rows.why: Web exports and imports only admit ABI-safe types (scalars, `String`, `List`/`Map` of ABI-safe values, and `#Codable` structs/enums per D-JSBIND1). A `jet build --target=web` run reports this web-target diagnostic.
rows.fix: use a scalar, `String`, a `List`/`Map` of ABI-safe values, or a `#Codable` struct/enum whose fields are ABI-safe (D-JSBIND1)
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|use a scalar, `String`, a `List`/`Map` of ABI-safe values, or a `#Codable` struct/enum whose fields are ABI-safe (D-JSBIND1)

rows.meaning: A function in one web bucket calls a function in another (D-WASM1)
rows.what: `wasm_caller` is compiled to Wasm but calls `js_helper`, which lives in JS
rows.why: The web backend keeps DOM/view code in JS and compute in WASM; a direct call across that boundary is not allowed yet. A `jet build --target=web` run reports this web-target diagnostic.
rows.fix: Move the call behind a generated bridge, colocate both functions in the same bucket, or adjust their `#Target(Wasm|JS)` markers
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move the call behind a generated bridge, colocate both functions in the same bucket, or adjust their `#Target(Wasm|JS)` markers

rows.meaning: Native `jet run` cannot execute a web-targeted program (D-WEBRUN1=A)
rows.what: `jet run` cannot execute a web-targeted program natively
rows.why: The web target produces browser artifacts, not a native console executable
rows.fix: Use `jet dev <file.jet>` for the live browser loop, or `jet build --target=web <file.jet>` for web artifacts
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Use `jet dev <file.jet>` for the live browser loop, or `jet build --target=web <file.jet>` for web artifacts

rows.meaning: A Wasm-pinned function also carries the `Browser` effect (D-WASM1)
rows.what: `bad` is pinned to Wasm but uses the `Browser` effect
rows.why: The web backend keeps DOM/view code in JS and compute in WASM; a Wasm-pinned function cannot call browser APIs directly. A `jet build --target=web` run reports this web-target diagnostic.
rows.fix: remove the `#Target(Wasm)` pin, move browser work into a `#Target(JS)` function, or drop the browser API calls
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|remove the `#Target(Wasm)` pin, move browser work into a `#Target(JS)` function, or drop the browser API calls

rows.meaning: A web-targeted executable body is outside the checked TIR boundary (D-WEBTIR1)
rows.what: Web output cannot compile `{fn}` yet.
rows.why: Web builds use the same checked executable body path as native builds; this function uses a construct the web output cannot lower today (D-WEBTIR1). A `jet build --target=web` run reports this web-target diagnostic.
rows.fix: Move the unsupported work behind a Wasm export that uses covered Jet constructs, or simplify this function for the web target.
rows.structured_fix: reason:design|Move the unsupported work behind a Wasm export that uses covered Jet constructs, or simplify this function for the web target.

rows.meaning: Source importer omitted a construct
rows.what: Source import omitted {construct} at {source}
rows.why: The importer cannot prove an equivalent Jet construct: {reason}
rows.fix: Implement `{construct}` in Jet at `{source}`, or review the generated target `{target}` before rerunning the import.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Implement the omitted construct in Jet or review the generated target before rerunning import.

rows.meaning: Source import operation failed
rows.what: Source import could not {operation}
rows.why: {reason}
rows.fix: Check the source path and write permissions, then rerun
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Check the source path and write permissions, then rerun

rows.meaning: Source import merge conflict
rows.what: Source import conflict in {paths}
rows.why: Generated source and editable Jet both changed since the stored baseline
rows.fix: Reconcile the files, then rerun with `--update`
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Reconcile the files, then rerun with `--update`

rows.meaning: An unused local binding is dead code and may hide a missed use (D-LINT-UNUSED1, warning)
rows.what: Local binding `{name}` is never read.
rows.why: A binding that no later expression reads adds dead code and may hide a computed result that should have been used.
rows.fix: Remove the binding when its initializer is side-effect free, or rename `{name}` to `_{name}` when the value must be computed.
rows.structured_fix: source_edit|behavior-preserving

rows.meaning: An unused parameter is dead interface surface (D-LINT-UNUSED1, warning)
rows.what: Parameter `{name}` is never used.
rows.why: An unused parameter often means the function contract or implementation is incomplete; Jet keeps this warning-only so prototypes stay unblocked.
rows.fix: Use `{name}`, rename it to `_{name}` when it is intentionally unused, or remove it from the function contract.
rows.structured_fix: source_edit|behavior-preserving

rows.meaning: An unused import adds dead name and dependency surface (D-LINT-UNUSED1, warning)
rows.what: Import `{name}` is never used.
rows.why: An unused import adds a name and dependency to the file without contributing to checked code.
rows.fix: Remove the import, or rename `{name}` to `_{name}` when the import is intentionally kept.
rows.structured_fix: source_edit|behavior-preserving

rows.meaning: An unused private function is dead code (D-LINT-UNUSED1, warning)
rows.what: Private function `{name}` is never called or used as a value.
rows.why: A private function with no reachable reference is dead code; public functions stay exempt because other modules may use them.
rows.fix: Remove the function, or rename `{name}` to `_{name}` when it is intentional.
rows.structured_fix: source_edit|behavior-preserving

rows.meaning: A package-scoped export has no reachable consumer (D-STRUCT-LIVE1)
rows.what: Package export `{name}` is unreachable.
rows.why: The package's explicit import graph and application roots contain no consumer for this package-scoped export; library `pub` remains open to external consumers.
rows.fix: Remove the export, or rename `{name}` to `_{name}` when it is intentional.
rows.structured_fix: source_edit|behavior-preserving

rows.meaning: Typestate: two paths meet and leave one value in different states, so it is untracked from there (D-STATE1, D-FACT-FLOW1, warning)
rows.what: `{value}` ends in state `{one}` on one path and `{other}` on another.
rows.why: Typestate (D-STATE1, D-FACT-FLOW1): after two paths meet, a state holds only when both paths agree — here they do not, so the value is untracked from this point and later state checks on it stay silent.
rows.fix: Bring both paths to the same state before they meet, or do the work that needs the state inside the path that reaches it.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Bring both paths to the same state before they meet, or do the work that needs the state inside the path that reaches it.

rows.meaning: Typestate: a declared state is unreachable from every entry transition (D-STATE-TERMINAL1, warning)
rows.what: `{type}.State.{state}` is unreachable from every entry transition.
rows.why: When a state graph has entry transitions, no entry path reaches this state. It may be an unused branch or a state name that is not connected to the protocol.
rows.fix: Add an entry or transition path to `{state}`, or remove it from the declaration.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Add an entry or transition path to the declared state, or remove it from the declaration.

rows.meaning: Auto-clone `Shared` inside loop (lint)
rows.what: Auto-clone `Shared` inside loop (lint)
rows.why: The registered sema rule applies here
rows.fix: Move the `Shared` clone before the loop, or replace the loop with a blocking `Condition` wait.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Clone the `Shared` value deliberately before entering the loop, or restructure the loop.

rows.meaning: An inline script dependency (`use pkg#version;`) uses a loose/unpinned version selector (D-JPK-SCRIPTDEP1)
rows.what: `use {name}#{selector};` isn't pinned to an exact version.
rows.why: An inline script dependency has no lockfile until `jet fetch --lock` runs; a loose selector (`1.4` rather than `1.4.2`) can resolve to a different version on a fresh clone (D-JPK-SCRIPTDEP1).
rows.fix: Write the exact version Jet resolved (`use {name}#<major.minor.patch>;`), or run `jet fetch --lock` to pin it in `<script>.lock`.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Write the exact resolved dependency version, or run `jet fetch --lock` to pin it.

rows.meaning: A `flake.nix`/`devenv.nix` field `jet os bridge flake` couldn't translate into `env.*` form (U16)
rows.what: `{field}` in `{file}` has no `env.*` equivalent yet.
rows.why: `jet os bridge flake` (U16) is a best-effort translator; some `flake.nix`/`devenv.nix` fields (`shellHook`, multiple named devShells, `buildInputs` vs `nativeBuildInputs`) have no ratified `env.*` spelling.
rows.fix: Review the generated shim and add `{field}`'s effect by hand if you need it — the shim is a starting point, not a full translation.
rows.structured_fix: reason:ambiguous|Review the generated shim and add the field effect by hand if needed.

rows.meaning: Build sandboxing is unavailable and trusted substitution is allowed by policy (U28, D-JPK-SANDBOX2)
rows.what: Build sandboxing is unavailable; local executable actions will be refused after substitution/remote resolution.
rows.why: D-JPK-SANDBOX2 requires a strong sandbox for fetched or transitive executable actions. Jetpack may use a trusted substitute or approved remote builder, but never an unsandboxed local action. A `jetpack env` run reports this sandbox warning.
rows.fix: Provide a trusted substitute or approved remote builder, or enable the native sandbox.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Provide a trusted substitute or approved remote builder, or enable the native sandbox.

rows.meaning: A `SharedGuard` lock spans a long lexical scope (D-SHAREDGUARD1)
rows.what: `` `Shared.{method}()` keeps its lock through a long lexical scope ``.

rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Bind the loop with `::` to collect its values, or write `loop v in &values -> v *= 2` so it takes write access (&) for items.

rows.meaning: The default HTTP body text limit is passed through a lower-level body call (D-HTTP-TEXT1=A)

rows.meaning: Fixed decimal output is immediately stripped of grouping separators (D-FMT-PLAIN1=A)

rows.meaning: Manual unit unwrap/scale/rewrap hides a direct scalar operation (D-UNIT-SCALAR1=A)
rows.what: A policy-free unit unwrap/scale/rewrap can use direct scalar unit arithmetic

rows.fix: Add at least one assertion, or remove the test if it only exercises compilation.

rows.why: Cognitive complexity counts nested branches, loops, dispatches, mixed boolean sequences, and recursion so a refactor can be checked mechanically.

rows.meaning: Raw `{operation}` outside `{gate}`'s allocation provenance
rows.what: Runtime fault [R0801]: raw `{operation}` outside `{gate}`'s storage
rows.why: The pointer is outside the allocation provenance tracked for the active `#Unsafe` gate; runtime evidence never replaces a required static obligation.
rows.fix: Bound the raw access before it reaches storage — obligation `{obligation}` was not met on this run.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Bound the raw access before it reaches storage and satisfy the named unsafe obligation.

rows.meaning: Use of storage after its lifetime ended
rows.what: Runtime fault [R0802]: use of storage after its lifetime ended in `{gate}`
rows.why: The storage was released or its owning Jet frame expired before this raw `{operation}`; the gate's lifetime obligation was not met.
rows.fix: Do not use the pointer after release or frame exit — obligation `{obligation}` was not met on this run.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Do not use the pointer after release or frame exit; satisfy the named lifetime obligation.

rows.meaning: Misaligned raw `{operation}`
rows.what: Runtime fault [R0803]: misaligned raw `{operation}` in `{gate}`
rows.why: The pointer alignment does not satisfy the allocation provenance for the active `#Unsafe` gate.
rows.fix: Align the raw access before it reaches storage — obligation `{obligation}` was not met on this run.
rows.structured_fix: reason:behavior|Align the raw access before it reaches storage and satisfy the named alignment obligation.
